journeys.title: Playback storm: three clips in one viewer, only one of them coherent
journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first, including the sync_tone config edit and the separate microphone WAV. Journey-specific setup:

1. Generate three SILENT, deterministic, guaranteed-dark clips once into D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\ (reusable across takes):
   clip-a (incoherent zoom): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "mandelbrot=size=1280x720:rate=30" -t 90 -vf "format=yuv420p,eq=brightness=-0.10" -c:v libx264 -preset medium -crf 20 -an clip-a.mp4
   clip-b (incoherent churn): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "life=size=1280x720:rate=30:mold=10:ratio=0.10:death_color=#101418:life_color=#3aa06a" -t 90 -vf format=yuv420p -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -an clip-b.mp4
   clip-c (COHERENT horizontal pan, the matched control): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "nullsrc=s=1280x720:r=30" -t 75 -vf "format=gray,geq=lum='120+90*sin((X+T*80)/23)*cos(Y/31)',format=yuv420p" -c:v libx264 -crf 20 -an clip-c.mp4
2. MANDATORY flash-hazard check on each clip before use: ffmpeg -i clip-X.mp4 -vf "scale=64:36,format=gray,signalstats" -f null - 2>&1 | findstr YAVG  and confirm no frame exceeds YAVG 230. jem_eval's flash detector calls a frame bright at mean grey > 245 and treats a bright run as a sync flash; an extra detected flash makes the manifest pairing fail with "sync alignment ambiguous" and loses the take.
3. CORRECTION vs the original proposal: all three clips play in the SAME Edge media viewer, in the same window at the same geometry. The original played clip-c in fullscreen VLC, which confounded the coherence variable with player, chrome and window rect and made the 'matched control' claim unsupportable. VLC is removed from this journey.
4. Edge: one window, one tab, maximized on the recorded monitor, dark theme, at http://localhost:8099/ . Memory/performance tab badge OFF. Navigation is always Ctrl+L, then the full URL including http://, then Delete to clear inline autocomplete, then Enter.
5. Fixture server on MONITOR 2: python -m http.server 8099 --directory D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys
6. Pin taskbar order Edge=1, Windows Terminal=2, so Win+1 and Win+2 are deterministic.
7. All three clips are silent by design. Speakers must still be the default output device, because JEM's 1 kHz sync tone has to reach the microphone.
8. No sign-in, no accounts, no personal files. Only locally generated synthetic clips and the committed synthetic fixture, served from localhost.

steps.action: Click Start in JEM on monitor 2. Then sit still and stay completely silent for four seconds. About 500 ms after Start, the white sync flash paints on the recorded monitor and JEM plays its 1 kHz tone through the speakers; the separately-running WAV recorder captures it. Do NOT clap, type or move the mouse during this window.
steps.produces: start flash in the video plus the matching 1 kHz tone in the microphone WAV: anchor 1 of the two-anchor offset-plus-drift fit solved by capture.audio_align. The flash window is foreground on the recorded monitor, so JEM logs one recorder context span that jem_eval identifies by flash and excludes.

steps.produces: Stop fires the END sync flash and its 1 kHz tone on the recorded monitor: anchor 2. JEM filters both clicks and foreground changes by monitor, so the click on monitor 2 and JEM's own window raise nothing in events.csv; only the flash window does.

narration.line: I am going to watch three short test clips back to back in the browser.
This opening clip is a fractal render that never holds still.
Every single frame is different but I have not changed what I am working on.
I am enjoying watching this one, it is genuinely lovely to look at.
It bothers me that a video like this can look exactly like a hundred task switches.
Okay next, I want the cellular automaton clip.
This one is pure churn, there is no camera motion at all to lock onto.
I like that it is deterministic, the same recipe gives the same frames on every take.
A detector that fires on this is going to drown my report in junk boundaries.
Moving on to the panning clip, in the same viewer and the same window.
The whole picture is sliding sideways at a perfectly steady rate.
Nothing has changed except that the motion is coherent this time.
That is a much calmer result and I am really pleased with it.
After that, I will run the little checkout fixture to prove real switches still land.
Three page changes, each one about eight seconds apart.
The clips are over and I am wrapping up this recording.

journeys.expected_physical: ~9 left clicks (1 Edge body, up to 3 play controls, 4 fixture buttons; the Stop and Save clicks are on monitor 2 and are dropped by JEM's monitor containment filter). ~139 keypress rows: three clip navigations of ~36 rows each, one home navigation of ~27, and two Win+digit pairs. Counting rule: JEM writes one row per key-DOWN with OS auto-repeat suppressed, and Ctrl, Shift and Win are their own rows with key_category=modifier, so they must be excluded from any physical-effort count. Zero deliberate scrolls. Three dead zones of 90 s, 90 s and 75 s contain no JEM input events at all while the screen changes on every frame.
journeys.stresses: Primary target is providers/context_switch.py. Video playback has never been measured on real footage. Clips a and b produce high band-max content_val with low phase-correlation response, so translation_like() (phase_response_threshold 0.25 AND phase_shift_px_threshold 2.5) is false, decide_post_filter returns no_translation, and the only remaining defence is min_scene_len_frames=10 at PROXY_FPS 5.0 plus min_gap_seconds=2.0, giving a predicted ceiling of ~45 spurious cuts per 90 s clip. Clip c is now a genuine matched control: same Edge media viewer, same window rect, same source resolution and frame rate, comparable motion energy, but coherent translation that should trip the post-filter. Running all three inside one recording with the player held constant isolates coherence from motion energy, which no prior JAMS experiment has done. Secondary: this is the cleanest journey in the corpus for label-noise asymmetry, because JEM logs zero context switches across 255 s of continuous visual change, so every JAMS detection there is a false positive against JEM proxy labels while being a real visual change; jem_eval's per-event visual delta (VISUAL_CORROBORATION_DELTA 0.30) lets that be audited rather than argued. It also stresses proxy_motion's decimation: 30 fps source inside a 30 fps capture rendered to a 5 fps, 480 px grayscale proxy means the detector sees one frame in six.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: nothing sensitive is on screen. Locally generated synthetic clips and the committed synthetic fixture only, served from localhost. No login, no account, no payment, no personal files, no mail or chat window. Keep Edge on the single fixture tab so no other tab title can leak anything.
SYNC: the sync tone, not a clap, is the audio anchor. capture.audio_align requires at least 90 ms of continuous 1 kHz energy holding at least 35 percent of frame energy; a hand clap is broadband, would be rejected, and if it overlaps the tone it drives the in-band share down and can destroy the anchor. Silence and stillness for two seconds either side of Start and Stop is mandatory. Headphones defeat the anchor entirely.
REPRODUCIBILITY: the three clips are deterministic given these ffmpeg recipes, so a second take sees identical pixels; human variance is limited to click timing. Edge may autoplay a direct MP4 URL depending on version and media-autoplay setting; predict one play click per clip but record what actually happened rather than asserting it.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) the clips must be verified sub-230 YAVG before recording, or a bright run inside a clip is counted as a sync flash and the flash-count check fails with "sync alignment ambiguous"; (b) Edge must stay in dark theme and the media viewer must not show a white loading state at full window size between navigations; (c) touching mouse or keyboard during a playback block destroys the dead-zone property and confounds the false-positive measurement; (d) Edge address-bar autocomplete can navigate somewhere unintended, so always Ctrl+L, full URL with http://, Delete, Enter; (e) a notification toast during a dead zone is both a foreground change and a visual change, so Do Not Disturb is mandatory.

journeys.title: Dark on dark: four applications at the same luminance
journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first. Journey-specific setup:

1. Visual Studio Code: theme "Dark+ (default dark)", sidebar hidden with Ctrl+B, minimap on, maximized on the recorded monitor, with ONLY D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\index.html open. VS Code puts the active file in the window title, so any extra tab opened during the take fires an unplanned context_switch.
2. Windows Terminal: PowerShell profile, colour scheme "One Half Dark", acrylic/transparency OFF, maximized, started in D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys, scrollback cleared. In settings.json set this profile's "suppressApplicationTitle": true and "tabTitle": "jem". This is REQUIRED: without it every command rewrites the tab title, JEM logs an extra NAMECHANGE context_switch per command, and the expected count below is wrong by four.
3. Notepad++: Settings > Style Configurator > theme "Deep Black", maximized, new file saved as C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\notes-adversarial-02.md. Then type one character and do NOT save. The modified marker is already in the title before recording starts, so no title change (and no phantom context_switch) occurs during the take. Save after Stop.
4. Microsoft Edge: dark theme, one tab at http://localhost:8099/ , memory/performance tab badge OFF.
5. Pin taskbar order Edge=1, Terminal=2, Code=3, Notepad++=4. All switching uses Win+1..4.
6. MANDATORY CALIBRATION, done before recording and written into the take log: screenshot each of the four apps maximized, then for each run  ffmpeg -i shot.png -vf "scale=64:36,format=gray,signalstats" -f null -  and record the YAVG. The journey is only adversarial if the four values sit within about 12 grey levels of each other and all are well under 245. If any pair differs by more than 20, adjust that app's theme and re-measure. Record the four numbers; they are part of this journey's ground truth and without them the adversarial claim is unfalsifiable.
7. No credentials and no secrets. index.html is a committed synthetic fixture. Do not open any .env, any file under infra/, or anything outside D:\git\jams\fixtures and the scratch note.

narration.line: I am looking at why the fixture page changes screens without loading anything.
The whole styling lives in one small block at the top of the file.
This terminal has almost the same background as the editor, which is going to be a problem.
I am writing down a short note about the routing while it is fresh in my head.
Okay next, I want to walk through the onboarding screens.
The form appears but the background colour has not shifted at all.
The welcome screen is green, so this one transition has a real brightness step.
Every window I use is dark, and I actually prefer working this way.
Back in the editor, the page function swaps the body colour and the inner markup together.
Listing the directory gives me the same pale grey text on the same black field.
Switching between these four applications barely changes a single grey level.
Moving on to the checkout screens, which is where the colours get interesting.
The cart screen is purple and the receipt screen is green.
Those two have almost identical brightness, which is exactly the case I was worried about.
In grayscale they are the same picture, and that is a real blind spot.
The editor and the terminal are both sitting around the same luminance value.
After that, I want the four measured numbers written into the note file.
Four applications, seventeen transitions, and hardly any contrast between any of them.
This was a genuinely useful thing to capture and I am glad I did it.
I am wrapping up the recording here.

journeys.expected_physical: ~8 left clicks. ~300 keypress rows: four shell commands of 34 to 48 rows each, roughly 166 rows of typed notes, plus 8 Win+digit pairs. Counting rule: one row per key-DOWN with auto-repeat suppressed; Win, Ctrl and Shift each write their own row with key_category=modifier and must be excluded from effort counts. ~8 scroll spans of 3 notches each, kept at least 0.8 s apart so JEM's scroll aggregator does not merge them. Physical density is deliberately ordinary so it does not confound the visual measurement.
journeys.stresses:
Primary target is the absolute luminance floor in providers/context_switch.py. min_content_val=12.0 with low_response_candidate_floor_factor=0.8 gives a hard candidate floor of 9.6 on a grayscale band-max delta measured on a 480 px wide, 5 fps proxy. This journey is engineered so most transitions sit near or under that floor. It supplies the labelled dark-on-dark development data that docs/JEM-HILLCLIMB-2026-09-09.md identifies as missing. Three separable classes live inside one recording: (a) dark-app to dark-app switches at matched luminance; (b) a hue-only page change at near-zero luminance delta (#4d304c to #244831, luma ~60 and ~59) that a grayscale proxy is structurally blind to and that no threshold tuning can recover; (c) two positive controls with a genuine 20 to 30 level delta that must still be detected. Class (b) earns the slot on its own: it decides whether this failure mode is a threshold problem or a colour-space problem, which decides whether hillclimb budget goes to thresholds or to adding a chroma channel to proxy_motion. The mandatory YAVG calibration makes each transition's difficulty a measured quantity. jem_eval now records a per-truth-event visual delta against VISUAL_CORROBORATION_DELTA=0.30, so the near-zero-delta events will be reported as proxy-only truth and can be split out without re-running.
CORRECTION to the original framing: the hillclimb record does not say min_content_val=4 'broke' IANA and Outlook. It says the low-floor variant recovered the two weak controlled receipt and recovery transitions, moved IANA from 0 TP / 0 FP / 2 FN (F1 0.0) to 2 TP / 2 FP / 0 FN (F1 0.6667) with two website-scroll false positives, and left Outlook at 0 / 2 / 1 (F1 0.0). That is a precision-recall trade with new false positives, not a regression to zero, and the journey's value is supplying the labelled data to adjudicate it.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: no credentials and no secrets. Only the synthetic fixture, a scratch note file, and three harmless read-only shell commands. Explicitly do not open any .env, credential store, or private repo file, because the video captures everything visible. Keep the terminal in D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys so a directory listing cannot expose anything else. Clear terminal scrollback before starting.
REPRODUCIBILITY: the four themes must be identical on a second take, which is why the YAVG values are recorded. Windows Terminal transparency and the VS Code minimap both move the measured luminance, so both are pinned in setup. Win+digit removes the variance of clicking taskbar targets.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) if any app is left in a light theme the frame mean can approach jem_eval's 245 bright-frame test and be read as a phantom sync flash, which fails the flash-count check and loses the take; (b) VS Code puts the active file in the window title, so opening any extra file adds unplanned context_switch rows; (c) Edge's memory-usage tab badge must be off or its volatile tab name emits spurious switches; (d) Windows Terminal MUST have suppressApplicationTitle set and Notepad++ MUST be pre-dirtied, or four and one extra title-change switches respectively appear and the expected count of 17 is simply wrong, which would be scored as detector false positives when they are really unlabelled truth; (e) if the four YAVG values are not measured, the adversarial claim is unfalsifiable and the take is worth much less.

journeys.title: Long silences: twelve minutes, eleven sentences, no spoken cues
journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first. Journey-specific setup:

1. Visual Studio Code, Dark+ theme, sidebar hidden, maximized on the recorded monitor, with the JAMS repo open and NO file open. Files are opened during the journey with Ctrl+P, and only these three: docs/EVALUATION-MATRIX.md, worker/src/jams_worker/jem_eval.py, docs/PLAN.md.
2. Windows Calculator: leave it at its DEFAULT WINDOW SIZE, not maximized, positioned centre-left on the recorded monitor, and do not move it once recording starts. A small window changing over a large static dark background is a localized change that probes band-max amplification in proxy_motion, and it is the hardest single switch in this journey.
3. Notepad++, Deep Black theme, maximized, new file saved as C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\notes-adversarial-03.md. Type one character and do NOT save, so the modified marker is already in the title before recording and no phantom title-change switch occurs during the take. Save after Stop.
4. Pin taskbar order Code=1, Notepad++=2, Calculator=3, and use Win+1, Win+2, Win+3 only. (The original pinned these at 3, 4 and 5 with slots 1 and 2 unassigned, which makes Win+5 land on whatever happens to be fifth.)
5. Windows dark mode ON so Calculator renders dark. Verify before recording that Calculator is not a light grey panel.
6. THIS JOURNEY HAS NO SPOKEN SEGMENTATION CUES BY DESIGN. Read the narration aloud once before recording and confirm that none of the exact DEFAULT_CUES phrases appear: let's get started, lets get started, get started, to start, first, starting, okay next, next, moving on, now, then, after that, done, finished, complete, that's it, that is it, finally. Matching is a word-boundary regex on the lowercased utterance, so 'first' inside 'first-pass' would still match. If the operator improvises any of these the uncued stratum is destroyed.
7. Silence discipline: during the silent stretches do not sigh, hum, mutter, tap the desk, or clear your throat. Those windows must contain room tone only. Keep the chair still. This does NOT apply to the two sync-tone windows, where silence is required for a different reason: the 1 kHz tone must dominate the frame.
8. Only repository documentation and source on screen. Do not open .env, anything under infra/, or any file with a connection string.

journeys.expected_physical: Zero deliberate clicks on the recorded monitor (the Stop and Save clicks are on monitor 2 and are dropped by JEM's monitor containment filter). ~245 keypress rows spread thinly over 12 minutes. ~5 scroll spans. Roughly one JEM input event every three seconds, against about one per second in a normal working journey. The 40 to 90 second dead zones between events are the point, not an accident.
journeys.stresses:
This is the only journey in the corpus that will NOT saturate the scoring lanes, which is why it earns its slot. Verified against worker/src/jams_worker/effort_score.py: PER_MINUTE_SCALE is context_switch 36.75 and spoken_word 2.47, so saturation is 2.72 switches per minute and 40.5 words per minute. At 11 lines of about 12 words over 12 minutes this runs near 11 wpm, normalizing spoken_word to roughly 27 instead of the 100 that every continuously narrated journey pins to; at 0.9 switches per minute context_switch normalizes to about 34. neg_density is share multiplied by 250 and is DURATION weighted over sentiment measure spans with the negative test value_num < -0.15, not a line count, so two comparable-length negative lines out of eleven land near 45 provided their durations are comparable. All four lanes sit in their responsive range simultaneously, making this the only journey where an improvement in any provider can actually move the headline effort score.
Secondary targets: (1) Silero VAD under sparse speech, with total speech coverage near 7 percent of wall duration, comfortably above the 2 percent two-pass rescue trigger (which also requires audio_rms_db above -45) but far outside the model's normal operating regime; (2) ASR hallucination on room tone, since long silences are the classic condition for Whisper to invent text, and an invented utterance carries an invented sentiment label straight into neg_density; (3) segmentation with ZERO audio cues, forcing the boundary set to come entirely from the context-switch union, which after the MIN_SEGMENT_MS=10000 merge will produce roughly 11 machine segments against 4 human tasks; (4) the small non-maximized Calculator switch, the hardest localized-change case in the corpus.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: only repository docs and source are shown. Explicitly forbidden on screen: .env files, anything under infra/, apps/web/.env*, browser windows, mail, chat. The scratch file under Documents\JEM contains only arithmetic. No credentials are typed anywhere and capture_key_text stays off, so events.csv records key categories, not characters.
REPRODUCIBILITY: the silent stretches are the fragile part. A cough, a chair creak, a notification chime or a phone vibration inside a silent window changes the audio ground truth and can create a phantom utterance. Do Not Disturb on, phone out of the room, operator genuinely still. A second take will differ in exact silence lengths but the coverage fraction should reproduce within a few percent.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) any improvised cue phrase from the DEFAULT_CUES list destroys the uncued stratum, which is the only reason this journey can measure the scene-boundary fallback; (b) 12 minutes at full monitor resolution is a real test of jem_eval's subprocess timeouts, verified as 120 s for flash detection and 300 s for the CFR re-encode, both sized for 90 s clips, so run this journey through jem_eval BEFORE recording the rest of the set and raise the timeouts if it blows; (c) numbers are spoken as words, so the WER normalization protocol (spoken 'one hundred and forty' versus written 140) must be declared in writing before any score is computed; (d) if Whisper hallucinates on the silence, report the hallucinations rather than deleting them, because the hallucination rate on room tone is itself the finding; (e) Calculator's window must not be moved mid-recording or the localized-change geometry changes; (f) pressing Ctrl+S in Notepad++ during the take adds an unplanned title-change switch, so the save happens after Stop.

Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first. Journey-specific setup:

1. Visual Studio Code, Dark+ theme, maximized, with ONLY D:\git\jams\worker\src\jams_worker\jem_eval.py open, scrolled to the top. No other editor tab, because the active file is in the window title.
2. Windows Terminal, One Half Dark, maximized, cwd D:\git\jams\worker, scrollback cleared, and this profile set to "suppressApplicationTitle": true with "tabTitle": "jem". This removes the version-dependent question the original left open about whether running a command emits a title change: with suppression on, it does not.
3. Pin taskbar order Terminal=1, Code=2, and use Win+1 and Win+2 only. (The original pinned Terminal=2 and Code=3 with slot 1 unassigned.)
4. DELIVERY RULES, which are part of the experiment and must be followed exactly:
   - Speak the lines as written, INCLUDING every um, uh, and repeated word. The written line IS the reference transcript. If you improvise an extra filler, write it into the corrected reference afterwards rather than pretending it did not happen.
   - Leave at least 1.5 s of silence between lines so each scripted line maps to exactly one utterance. Verified constants: SPLIT_GAP_MS is 1200 and MERGE_GAP_MS is 700, so gaps under 0.7 s will merge lines and break the one-line-one-label mapping.
   - The line at t=92 ("Hm, okay.") probes the transcription timestamp invariant at providers/transcription.py:255, which requires mean word duration per utterance between 60 and 1200 ms. Say it CRISPLY, the whole thing inside about 0.8 s (mean ~400 ms per word), and leave 2 s of silence on both sides so it stands alone. Drawling two words across 3 s gives a 1500 ms mean and trips the invariant.
   - The line at t=213 is a deliberate long run-on of about 65 words over roughly 25 s, which is about 156 wpm and a mean word duration near 385 ms. Say it in one breath group with no full stop until the end, to approach but not cross the 30 s VAD force-split (max_speech_duration_s=30) and to stay well inside MAX_UTTERANCE_MS=45000.
5. No credentials on screen. jem_eval.py is source with no secrets. Keep the terminal in D:\git\jams\worker, do not print environment variables, and do not run anything that shows a git remote with a token.

journeys.expected_physical: Zero deliberate clicks on the recorded monitor (Stop and Save are on monitor 2 and are dropped). ~250 keypress rows dominated by three long PowerShell commands of 68 to 74 rows each. ~9 scroll spans of three notches, kept at least 0.8 s apart. Physical volume is ordinary; the load in this journey is entirely on the speech path. Note two blocks of substantial visual change with no context-switch truth at all: the three find-next jumps around t=55 and the Ctrl+G viewport replacement at t=262.
journeys.stresses: Primary target is the transcription and utterance-assembly path in providers/transcription.py, benchmarked so far only on clean scripted speech. Four mechanisms are exercised. (1) WER under disfluency: the plan gate is under 5 percent and the realistic expectation is 10 to 18 percent; this is the first real measurement on disfluent speech, and because the scripted line IS the reference no separate transcription pass is needed. (2) Utterance assembly: repeated false starts and mid-line restarts test SPLIT_GAP_MS 1200, MERGE_GAP_MS 700, MAX_UTTERANCE_MS 45000 and the n-gram de-repetition rule in _dedupe_repetition, which collapses an n-gram repeated four or more times and which real stammering can trip. (3) The timestamp invariant at transcription.py:255, which raises PipelineError when mean word duration per utterance falls outside 60 to 1200 ms: the two-word interjection at t=92 is a controlled, bounded approach to that boundary and whether it trips is itself a finding. (4) The 65-word run-on at t=213 approaches the VAD max_speech_duration_s=30 force-split. Secondary target is sentiment on garbled text: twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) sees fillers and restarts it was never trained on, and each line can be scored twice, once on ASR output and once on the written reference, which decomposes ASR-induced sentiment error from classifier error. Third target is the segmentation cue false-positive rate: the script was checked line by line against DEFAULT_CUES and contains zero matches, so any audio_cue boundary that appears is a measured false positive on disfluent speech. Fourth, and independently valuable: the narration's factual claims were verified against the source and are correct, so the take also serves as a readable explanation of two real defects (the plural/singular kind mismatch between JEM's click/keypress/scroll and JAMS' clicks/keypresses/scrolls, and the fact that jem_eval's excluded_kinds at line 537 is a report field that filters nothing, the real filter being the kind == context_switch inclusion test at line 418).
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: only JAMS source is on screen and no credentials are typed. Do not run anything that prints environment variables or a tokenised git remote. Clear terminal scrollback beforehand.
REPRODUCIBILITY: this is the least reproducible journey in the set, because disfluency is hard to repeat verbatim. Mitigation: the script is the reference and must be followed literally, and any deviation is corrected into that take's reference rather than ignored. WER is always computed against the corrected reference for that specific take.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) if the t=92 interjection violates the mean-word-duration invariant the JAMS run fails with PipelineError. CORRECTION to the original risk text: this does NOT take the recording with it. jem_eval is a separate local harness that reads the MP4 and events.csv directly, so the video, the physical truth and the context-switch scoring all survive, and the take can simply be re-analysed after the invariant is addressed. Report it as a finding and lengthen the interjection to four words on the next take rather than quietly deleting the probe. (b) Lines spoken less than 0.7 s apart merge and the one-line-one-label mapping breaks, so the 1.5 s gap discipline is not optional. (c) No em dashes or ellipses appear in the script, precisely because they make the WER reference ambiguous; none should be introduced. (d) If the operator slips into fluent speech the journey stops being adversarial and duplicates a normal narration journey. (e) Windows Terminal must have suppressApplicationTitle set, or each command adds an unplanned title-change switch and the expected count of 6 is wrong.

journeys.title: Noise floor: three acoustic stages inside one take, with identical visual truth
journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first. Journey-specific setup:

1. Build a deterministic FOUR-segment audio bed once, into C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\beds\. The fourth segment is the critical correction: the original bed ran under the closing sync tone, which would have destroyed the take.
   s1 (clean): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "anullsrc=r=48000:cl=mono" -t 150 s1.wav
   s2 (broadband): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "anoisesrc=color=pink:r=48000:a=0.05:seed=1234" -t 220 s2.wav
   s3 (tonal): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "sine=f=196:r=48000" -f lavfi -i "sine=f=294:r=48000" -f lavfi -i "anoisesrc=color=brown:r=48000:a=0.04:seed=99" -filter_complex "[0][1][2]amix=inputs=3:normalize=0" -t 100 s3.wav
   s4 (mandatory trailing silence so the CLOSING sync tone is clean): ffmpeg -y -f lavfi -i "anullsrc=r=48000:cl=mono" -t 60 s4.wav
   Concat s1..s4 with the ffmpeg concat demuxer into bed.wav and verify with  ffmpeg -i bed.wav -af volumedetect -f null -  that duration is 530 s.
2. WHY s4 EXISTS: capture.audio_align finds the 1 kHz sync tone by requiring at least 90 ms of continuous energy holding more than 35 percent of frame energy in the 1 kHz bin. A pink or tonal-plus-brown bed playing through the same speakers raises total frame energy and drives that share under the threshold, so the closing anchor is not found, alignment fails with "found 1 tone(s) but 2 flash(es)", and the entire nine-minute take is unusable. The bed MUST be in silence when Stop is pressed, and the operator must confirm by ear that the bed has gone quiet before pressing Stop.
3. Windows default output device set to the desk SPEAKERS, not headphones. This is required twice over: acoustic coupling into the microphone is the point of this journey, and the JEM sync tone can only reach the microphone through speakers. System volume 20, unchanged for the whole take.
4. On MONITOR 2, in a terminal:  Start-Sleep -Seconds 30; ffplay -nodisp -autoexit -volume 60 C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\beds\bed.wav   then immediately raise JEM and press Start within that window. Nominal timing then puts the bed start near recording t=+15, pink onset near t=165, tonal onset near t=385, and bed silence from t=485. The exact stage boundaries are RECOVERED AFTERWARDS from the recorded audio, where the pink onset is unmistakable in a spectrogram; do not assume the nominal times.
5. Edge dark theme at http://localhost:8099/ with the fixture server on monitor 2. Notepad++ Deep Black on a new file C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\notes-adversarial-05.md, pre-dirtied with one unsaved character. Windows Terminal One Half Dark in D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys with suppressApplicationTitle true. Pin taskbar order Edge=1, Terminal=2, Notepad++=3 and use Win+1..3. (The original pinned Notepad++ at 4 with slot 3 empty.)
6. Two BED-ONLY WINDOWS are scripted, roughly t=200-240 and t=428-468: the operator keeps working but says nothing at all. These measure ASR hallucination on broadband noise and on pitched audio separately.
7. Two lines, at t=280 and t=496, are spoken DELIBERATELY QUIETLY at about half normal volume, to probe VAD misses under a raised noise floor. CORRECTION: the original put one of these quiet lines at t=460, inside bed-only window B, which contradicted itself. Both quiet lines are now outside both silent windows.
8. MANDATORY DRY RUN: before the real take, record a 60 s throwaway session with the bed playing at the same volume, and confirm  python -m capture.audio_align align  finds two anchors. Alignment under an acoustic bed is the single most likely way to lose this take, and it is cheap to prove in advance.
9. No credentials, no accounts, no personal audio. The bed is generated tones and noise, not recorded music, which also removes any content concern from the recording.

journeys.expected_physical: ~10 left clicks on the recorded monitor (the Stop and Save clicks on monitor 2 are dropped by JEM's monitor containment filter). ~235 keypress rows: two shell commands of about 40 and 42 rows, roughly 148 rows of typed notes, and 5 Win+digit pairs whose modifier halves must be excluded from effort counts. Zero deliberate scrolls. Physical activity is deliberately ordinary so the acoustic variable is isolated. CORRECTION: the expected switch count drops from 18 to 16 because with suppressApplicationTitle set the two terminal commands no longer rewrite the tab title and no longer emit their own context switches.
journeys.stresses: Primary target is providers/transcription.py under a degraded acoustic floor, in three stages inside ONE recording so the visual and physical ground truth is identical across all three and only the audio varies. That single-take design is what makes this journey scientifically usable: stage-to-stage WER differences cannot be blamed on different content, different apps or different operator behaviour. Specific mechanisms: (1) Silero VAD at threshold 0.5 against a raised noise floor, where the risk runs both ways, missed speech and noise admitted as speech; (2) the two-pass quiet-speech rescue at transcription.py, which only fires when VAD coverage is under 2 percent of duration AND audio_rms_db is above -45, and a noise bed RAISES mean volume, so the bed can mask genuinely quiet speech from the rescue path, a real and previously unexamined failure mode that the two deliberately quiet lines probe directly; (3) the two 40 s bed-only windows, which separate Whisper hallucination on broadband noise from hallucination on pitched quasi-musical audio; (4) sentiment contamination, since any hallucinated utterance carries a sentiment label into neg_density even though nothing was said. Secondary and previously unnoticed: the bed also degrades capture/audio_align.detect_transients, which uses a fast-to-slow envelope ratio with a default threshold of 6.0, so refine_offset_by_events will match fewer JEM click and keypress times against audio transients in stages 2 and 3 than in stage 1. That degradation is measurable within this one take and is itself a finding about the acoustic transient library the experimental physical providers depend on.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: no credentials, no accounts, no personal audio, no recorded music. Only the committed synthetic fixture, a scratch note, two read-only shell commands, and a locally generated bed of tones and noise.
SYNC, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT LOSES TAKES: the closing 1 kHz sync tone must land in silence. The bed's fourth segment exists solely for this, the operator must confirm by ear before pressing Stop, and the 60 s dry run must have proved that capture.audio_align finds two anchors under this exact speaker volume. Without alignment there is no narration track on the video and the entire acoustic experiment is void.
REPRODUCIBILITY: the bed is byte-deterministic given these recipes and seeds. Speaker volume, microphone gain, and the physical distance from speakers to microphone must be recorded in the take log, because the coupling ratio is the independent variable and it is not recoverable afterwards. Nominal stage boundaries WILL drift by several seconds depending on how fast Start is pressed, which is why the boundaries are recovered from the recorded audio rather than assumed.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) speaking inside either bed-only window destroys the hallucination measurement for that stage; (b) changing system volume mid-take makes the three stages incomparable, which is the whole point of a single take; (c) a notification chime is both an unscripted sound and a foreground change; (d) if the bed is loud enough to clip the microphone preamp the stages measure clipping rather than acoustic masking, so check the recorded WAV peak stays below about -3 dBFS; (e) Windows Terminal must have suppressApplicationTitle set and Notepad++ must be pre-dirtied, or the expected count of 16 is wrong.

journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first, including the A/V MARKER protocol (P5).

Journey-specific setup:

1. Four applications, each maximized on the recorded monitor, each in a dark theme, each with a STABLE window title that will not change for the whole take:
   - Edge: one tab at http://localhost:8099/index.html, memory badge off, sleeping tabs off.

   - Notepad++: Deep Black, one saved unmodified file open. Type NOTHING, so the title asterisk never appears.

Do NOT use Alt+Tab: it draws a large translucent overlay that is itself a big visual event with no context change, which would confound the cadence measurement. journeys.expected_physical: PLANNING ESTIMATE ONLY; authoritative counts from events.csv. Roughly 0 clicks on the recorded monitor, roughly 190 keypress rows (88 Win+digit pairs at 2 rows each, plus 6 marker Spaces), and zero scrolls. This is by a wide margin the highest context-switch density in the corpus at roughly 18 switches per minute, against the 2.72 per minute saturation point, so the context_switch scoring lane will be pinned at 100 and this journey is deliberately useless for headline-score sensitivity. Its value is entirely in the per-block recall curve.
journeys.stresses: Primary target is the min_gap_seconds=2.0 suppression floor in providers/context_switch.py, which imposes a HARD, arithmetic ceiling on recall that no amount of threshold tuning can lift. This journey measures that ceiling directly rather than inferring it, by sweeping cadence through three levels inside one recording while holding contrast, content, apps and operator constant. The predicted recall ceilings are about 0.50 at 1.0 s, about 0.80 at 1.6 s and about 1.00 at 3.0 s; if measured recall tracks those predictions, min_gap is confirmed as the binding constraint and the hillclimb should make it a tunable or replace it with a refractory model rather than tuning content thresholds. If measured recall falls BELOW the ceiling in the 3.0 s control block, the binding constraint is elsewhere and the whole cadence hypothesis is falsified, which is equally valuable and is exactly why the control block is included rather than assumed. Secondary targets: (1) JEM's own fast-path limits, namechange_quiet_ms=200 and foreground_resolve_timeout_ms=200, which this journey exercises for the first time at 1.0 s cadence and which determine whether JEM's truth is itself complete at speed; if JEM drops rows here, the JEM-side label is no longer a gold standard and that must be discovered on a purpose-built journey rather than in the middle of a mixed one. (2) The A1/A2 and B1/B2 replicates isolate within-take drift from the adaptive threshold's trailing mean, which no other journey can separate from content effects. (3) jem_eval's exposure_ms union denominator is exercised against 90 short adjacent spans rather than a few long ones, which is a different arithmetic regime from anything measured so far.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: only PLAN.md, a scratch text file, a local fixture page and an empty terminal are on screen. No credentials, no personal data. Confirm the VS Code recent-files list and the Edge tab set are clean before recording.
REPRODUCIBILITY: human cadence accuracy is the main variance source, which is why the silent visual metronome on the unrecorded monitor is mandatory rather than advisory, and why each cadence is practised once before the take. Report the ACTUAL inter-switch intervals measured from events.csv per block, not the nominal ones, and bin the recall curve on the measured intervals. A take where the measured 1.0 s block has a standard deviation above about 250 ms should be re-recorded, because the cadence blocks would then overlap.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) any in-app identity change during the take (a terminal command, a Notepad++ keystroke setting the asterisk, a VS Code tab change, an Edge navigation) inserts a switch that is not part of the cadence design and corrupts the block statistics; this is why all four apps are frozen and why nothing is typed into them. (b) Alt+Tab is forbidden here because its overlay is a large visual event with no context change, which would inflate detections and confound the cadence measurement; it is deliberately reserved for journey 08. (c) Do NOT press Pause in JEM. (d) If JEM itself drops rows at 1.0 s cadence, the JEM truth is incomplete and the recall figures for block A become uninterpretable as stated; check for missing rows by comparing the JEM context_switch count against the known press count of 88 BEFORE computing any recall, and if they disagree, report the JEM shortfall as the primary finding of this journey rather than reporting a JAMS recall number. (e) The six pairwise YAVG values must be logged, or a low recall in this journey cannot be separated from the journey 02 contrast failure mode.

journeys.title: Sentiment traps: negation, mixed polarity, jargon and flat delivery
journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first, including the MULTI-PAGE FIXTURE REBUILD (P3) and the A/V MARKER protocol (P5).

Journey-specific setup:

1. In this journey the NARRATION IS THE PAYLOAD and the on-screen work is scaffolding whose only job is to keep JEM truth present and keep the operator looking busy. Keep the screen activity simple so it cannot distract from delivery.
2. Edge dark theme, one tab, fixture server on monitor 2. Notepad++ Deep Black on C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\notes-adversarial-07.md. Visual Studio Code Dark+ on D:\git\jams\docs\EVALUATION-MATRIX.md, fresh window, cleared recent-files list. Pin taskbar order Edge=1, Code=3, Notepad++=4.
3. THE SENTIMENT LABEL IN THIS SCHEMA IS THE TEXT LABEL. It is the label an independent human rater would assign to the WRITTEN line with no audio. This is the correct reference for JAMS, because providers/sentiment.py runs Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX over utterance TEXT and never hears the audio. For the six flat-delivery lines at the end, the declared label is still the TEXT label, and the intended DELIVERY is stated inside the line's step notes; the gap between them is the measurement.
4. DELIVERY RULES: leave at least 1.5 s of silence between lines so each line becomes exactly one utterance (SPLIT_GAP_MS=1200). Speak blocks 1 to 5 in a normal, engaged voice. Speak block 6 (from t=470 onward) in a deliberately FLAT, affectless monotone, as if reading a phone book, regardless of what the words say.
5. INDEPENDENT RATING IS MANDATORY BEFORE RECORDING. Have a second person, or a separate model run with no access to these labels, assign positive/negative/neutral to all 34 written lines. Any line where the independent rating disagrees with the declared label must be either reworded until it agrees or dropped from scoring and marked as such. A sentiment ground truth that only the author agrees with is not ground truth. Log the agreement rate; it is the ceiling on any macro-F1 this journey can report.
6. No credentials, no personal data, no real customer names, no real incidents. Every complaint in the script is about the local fixture or about the evaluation itself.

journeys.expected_physical: PLANNING ESTIMATE ONLY; authoritative counts from events.csv. Roughly 14 left clicks, roughly 170 keypress rows (two address-bar entries of 26 and 30 keys, about 80 keys of short notes, 6 Win+digit pairs, 6 marker Spaces), and 4 scroll spans. Physical activity is deliberately LOW and evenly spread, so that operator effort cannot correlate with sentiment block and confound the result. The 22 expected switches include the Notepad++ asterisk and the two marker.html navigations.
journeys.stresses: Primary target is providers/sentiment.py, a Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX INT8 model applied per utterance text. twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) is a BINARY sentiment classifier trained on movie reviews; it has no neutral class at all, and the pipeline maps its output onto a -1 to +1 value that feeds the neg_density lane of the effort score. This journey is the only one in the corpus that attacks that mapping directly, with six blocks that separate distinct failure mechanisms rather than lumping them: (1) plain polarity controls, which establish a per-session accuracy floor and prove the model is loaded and working at all, a check that the 2026-09-17 E2E session showed is not redundant; (2) negation and double negation, the best-documented systematic weakness of sentence-level classifiers and one that a movie-review model will fail in a specific, predictable direction; (3) mixed polarity within one sentence, where the correct answer is a judgement and where the ten genuinely mixed lines let the disagreement between the model and the independent rater be quantified rather than asserted; (4) software-domain jargon whose surface polarity is INVERTED relative to its meaning ("failed fast" is good, "passed silently" is bad, "everything went green" is alarming), which is the exact register real JAMS users speak in and which a movie-review training set cannot possibly cover; (5) British hedging and understatement, where the polarity is carried by register rather than by vocabulary; (6) flat monotone delivery of strongly polarized text, which measures the size of the text-only gap directly, because the text label and the audible affect disagree by construction and JAMS can only ever see the text. Block 6 is the block that decides whether prosody belongs on the roadmap: if the effort score computed from text alone diverges sharply from what a human listener would report for that same block, then text-only sentiment is a product-level limitation rather than a tuning target, and no amount of classifier swapping fixes it. Nine of the thirty-four lines are neutral, which quantifies how a no-neutral-class binary model distributes genuinely neutral speech, and that distribution feeds straight into neg_density on every real customer recording where most speech is neutral.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: nothing sensitive. All complaints are about the local fixture or about this evaluation. No customer names, no incident references, no real project grievances that would be awkward in a shared dataset. Confirm before recording that no line could be read as being about a real person.
REPRODUCIBILITY: delivery affect is the least reproducible variable in the corpus, which is why block 6's manipulation is coarse (flat monotone versus normal) rather than subtle, and why blocks 1 to 5 are delivered normally. The independent rating in setup item 5 must be done ONCE and frozen before any JAMS score is computed, exactly as the evaluation matrix requires for the holdout; re-rating after seeing model output is the single easiest way to fabricate a good score here.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) if the independent rater disagrees with the declared label on a line, that line is not usable as ground truth and must be reworded before the take or excluded from scoring afterwards, declared in advance. The human-human agreement rate is the ceiling on the reportable macro-F1 and must be published alongside it; a macro-F1 quoted without it is meaningless. (b) Lines spoken less than 0.7 s apart merge into one utterance and the one-line-one-label mapping breaks, taking two labels with it. (c) ASR errors propagate: score every line twice, once on the ASR text and once on the written reference, so classifier error is separated from transcription error; without that decomposition a poor result here cannot be attributed. (d) If the operator's voice follows the text in block 6, the manipulation never happened and block 6 silently duplicates block 1; confirm by listening back before scoring. (e) Do NOT press Pause in JEM. (f) Without the multi-page fixture rebuild (P3), thirteen of the expected switches do not exist. (g) This journey's context-switch rate of about 2.2 per minute sits just under the 2.72 saturation point, so unlike most of the corpus its effort score is still slightly responsive; do not treat it as a pure sentiment journey when reading the headline number.

journeys.title: Same process, different window: geometry churn and the proxy-label gap
journeys.setup:
Run the SHARED PREFLIGHT in category_notes first, including the MULTI-PAGE FIXTURE REBUILD (P3) and the A/V MARKER protocol (P5).

Journey-specific setup:

1. DESKTOP HYGIENE, mandatory because this journey deliberately reveals the desktop: set a plain solid dark wallpaper (a single dark colour, not a photo), and either clear the desktop of all icons or right-click the desktop and turn off Show desktop icons. The desktop WILL be visible during the snap and virtual-desktop steps, and desktop icons are file names, which are personal data.
2. Microsoft Edge, TWO separate windows (Ctrl+N for the second), both dark theme, both maximized on the recorded monitor:
   - Window 1 at http://localhost:8099/index.html
   - Window 2 at http://localhost:8099/receipt.html
   Same process, different URLs and different titles, which is the case that separates process-level from window-level identity.
3. Notepad++, Deep Black, maximized, with TWO saved unmodified files open as two tabs: notes-a.md and notes-b.md under C:\Users\chris\Documents\JEM\. Type nothing, so the asterisk never confounds a tab switch.
4. Visual Studio Code, Dark+, one file open, maximized. Used only as the control application.
5. VIRTUAL DESKTOP: create a SECOND virtual desktop before recording (Win+Ctrl+D) and leave it completely empty. Confirm it shows only the plain wallpaper. Switch back to desktop 1. During the take, Win+Ctrl+Right and Win+Ctrl+Left move between them.
6. Pin taskbar order Edge=1, Code=3, Notepad++=4.
7. PREFLIGHT PROBE P2 IS ESPECIALLY IMPORTANT FOR THIS JOURNEY. Before recording, run a 90 s throwaway JEM session that performs each of the six mechanisms below once, then read events.csv and record, for each, whether JEM emitted a context_switch row: (a) Alt+Tab between two Edge windows, (b) Ctrl+Tab between two Notepad++ tabs, (c) Win+Left snap of a single window, (d) F11 fullscreen toggle in Edge, (e) Win+Ctrl+Right to the empty virtual desktop, (f) Ctrl+F opening the Notepad++ Find dialog. The predictions in the steps below are PREDICTIONS; the probe converts them into facts, and the journey's expected_context_switches must be recomputed from the probe result before the real take. Do not record this journey until the probe has been run.
8. No credentials, no personal files, no Explorer window showing personal folders.

steps.action: With Edge window 1 foreground on marker.html, press Space three times at roughly 1 s intervals, then navigate to localhost:8099/index.html.
steps.produces: three audio/video co-markers; 3 JEM keypress rows; then a JEM context_switch on the navigation

steps.action: MECHANISM A, both agree. Press Alt+Tab once to raise Edge window 2 (the receipt page). Hold Alt only briefly.
steps.produces: JEM context_switch: same process msedge.exe, different identity, because the URL and the title both differ between the two windows. Large pixel delta (#142d44 home to #244831 receipt). Both JEM and JAMS should fire. Positive control for the whole journey.

steps.produces: NO JEM context_switch: the foreground window, its process and its title are all unchanged, so ContextIdentity is unchanged and no row is written. Meanwhile roughly half the frame turns over. Every JAMS detection here is scored as a FALSE POSITIVE against JEM proxy labels while being an unambiguously genuine visual change. This is the cleanest single demonstration in the corpus that JEM proxy labels are a lower bound on visual change, not a gold standard.

The tab change alters only a few characters of title bar and tab-strip text on an otherwise identical dark background, so its pixel delta is far below the 9.6 candidate floor. narration.line: I have two browser windows open on the same two local pages.
Swapping between them changes the whole screen and the recorder sees it.
That pair is the easy case and I am confident about it.
Snapping the window to one side uncovers half the desktop.
Half the picture just changed and the event log says absolutely nothing.
The window is back to full size again.
Full screen removes every piece of browser furniture from the top.
That is another enormous change with no matching row anywhere.
The second desktop is completely empty apart from the wallpaper.
I really like that this one does produce a row.
In the editor I am flipping between two files in the same window.
The recorder logs every one of those, but only a few characters moved.
It is depressing that the two sides disagree in both directions at once.
The find box opens as its own small window over the text.
These next three are ordinary application switches, spaced well apart.
Those are the ones I expect both sides to agree on perfectly.
Snapping the editor around gives me the same silent result as before.
Going back through the easy cases one more time for a second reading.
Full screen again, and again nothing at all is written down.
The empty desktop one more time, and back.
That is every mechanism covered and I am very happy with the coverage.

journeys.expected_physical: PLANNING ESTIMATE ONLY, and this journey's number is more provisional than any other in the set because six of its mechanisms are predictions until preflight probe P2 resolves them. Roughly 2 left clicks, roughly 90 keypress rows (Alt+Tab pairs, six Win+arrow pairs, four Win+Ctrl+arrow triples, four Ctrl+Tab pairs, two F11 pairs, one address-bar entry of about 30 keys, 6 marker Spaces), and zero scrolls. The 20 expected switches assume mechanisms A, B, E and F emit rows and C and D do not; recompute from the probe before the take. The defining number in this journey is not the switch count but the count of LARGE VISUAL CHANGES WITH NO JEM ROW, which is 10 by design (six snap or maximize operations and four fullscreen toggles).
journeys.stresses: This journey exists to measure the proxy-label gap in BOTH directions inside a single recording, which nothing else in the corpus does and which is the assumption the entire JEM-versus-JAMS comparison rests on. docs/EVALUATION-MATRIX.md already states that foreground and title spans are PROXY labels for visual context rather than task boundaries; this journey turns that caveat into a number. Direction one, JEM-blind: ten deliberate large-area visual changes (window snapping, maximize, restore, F11 fullscreen toggles) that leave process, window handle and title completely unchanged, so ContextIdentity never changes and JEM writes no row. Every JAMS detection there is counted as a false positive by jem_eval while being a genuine visual change, which means precision as currently reported is a LOWER BOUND, and this journey quantifies by how much. If the storm in journey 01 and the gap here both turn out large, then the precision figures in every prior JAMS evaluation need restating with a proxy-label correction, which is a reporting change rather than a code change and is cheaper than any amount of detector tuning. Direction two, JAMS-blind: four Notepad++ tab switches that change the window title, and therefore write a JEM row, while altering only a few characters of dark-on-dark text, putting them far below the 9.6 candidate floor. Those are structural false negatives that no threshold tuning can recover without destroying precision elsewhere, and having four of them in one journey gives a rate rather than an anecdote. The journey also separates same-process window switching (two Edge windows, which JEM catches only because its identity is title-derived or URL-derived rather than process-derived) from same-window tab switching, which is the distinction that determines whether JEM's identity model is adequate as a labelling scheme at all. The virtual-desktop and Find-dialog mechanisms probe the edges of foreground resolution, where JEM's documented weakness is that unresolvable windows report as unknown. Replicates of mechanisms A, C, D and E in the second half control for adaptive-threshold drift.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: this journey deliberately reveals the desktop, which is the one place in the corpus where personal data can appear without anyone opening a file. The plain dark wallpaper and the hidden or cleared desktop icons in setup item 1 are mandatory, not advisory, and must be verified on screen before pressing Start. Also confirm the taskbar shows no notification badges with sender names, and that no Explorer window showing personal folders is open on either virtual desktop.
REPRODUCIBILITY: snap behaviour, snap assist and virtual-desktop animation are all Windows-build-dependent, which is the main threat here. Snap assist in particular can pop a window picker after Win+Left, which would insert an unplanned foreground change; the Escape instruction handles it but its occurrence must be logged. Record the Windows build number in the journey log.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (a) the expected_context_switches figure is a PREDICTION until preflight probe P2 has been run, and the journey must not be recorded before the probe; six of the mechanisms could go either way and guessing them would make every derived metric unfalsifiable. (b) Alt+Tab draws a large translucent overlay for as long as Alt is held, which is itself a visual event with no context change; hold Alt only briefly and consistently, and note that the overlay contributes to JAMS detections near every mechanism A transition. (c) Do not type into Notepad++ at any point, or the title asterisk inserts identity changes that are indistinguishable from tab switches in events.csv. (d) Do NOT press Pause in JEM. (e) If JEM reports the virtual desktop foreground as unknown, mechanisms E become JEM-blind rather than both-agree, which CHANGES THE SIGN of that result; record it before scoring, never after. (f) Without the multi-page fixture rebuild (P3), Edge window 2 must still be a genuinely different document from window 1, so receipt.html must exist as a real file.

journeys.title: Long-form documentation read: Rust Book ownership chapters, scroll-dominated
journeys.setup:
Shared preflight P1-P18 (see category_notes), plus:
- Edge MAXIMIZED on the JEM-selected monitor, exactly two tabs open in this order:
  Tab 1: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-01-what-is-ownership.html
  Tab 2: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-03-slices.html
- Set the Rust Book theme ONCE: on Tab 1 click the paintbrush icon at top left and choose 'Coal'. The setting is localStorage per origin, so it applies to Tab 2 after you RELOAD Tab 2 (Ctrl+R). Do not assume it propagated; look at Tab 2 and confirm it renders dark. A cleared profile silently reverts to the light theme, which is a P6 flash-collision hazard.
- Scroll both tabs to the very top before starting.
- KEY COMBOS: fully RELEASE all modifier keys between every combo in this journey. JEM emits one row per key-DOWN with OS auto-repeat suppressed, so a held Ctrl across two presses yields ONE modifier row, not two, and the expected counts below assume full release.
- JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'browser-research-01-longform-scroll'. Single unpaused take.
- Begin step 1 only after the opening flash has cleared (roughly 1 s after Start).

The evaluator's truth instant is each customer span's t_start_ms, so THIS IS TRUTH EVENT #1, not a free extra. It is also visually large (JEM window to Edge) and should be an easy true positive. The click row is also the first audible transient for refine_offset_by_events.

EXPECT ZERO context_switch rows: scrolling changes no window title and no URL, so JEM never re-resolves identity. This is the core precision stress for the category.

Timing note: JEM backdates the switch to the LAST NAMECHANGE's own wall timestamp, not to the poll that noticed it, so hooks.namechange_quiet_ms does NOT add 200 ms of lag to the recorded instant. Any residual offset from the visual cut is the gap between the pixels changing and the title settling.

journeys.expected_physical: Heavy scroll, light click, light keypress. COUNT CONVENTION: expected_context_switches is the number of customer-app context_switch ROWS in events.csv, which includes the initial entry into Edge, because jem_eval takes each row's t_start_ms as a truth instant. Scroll: ~31 JEM spans (6 x 3-notch, 4 x 10-12-notch, 8 x 5-6-notch, 6 x 5-notch, 3 x 4-notch upward, plus the 4 x 4-notch after the chapter link). 3 click rows total: the opening focus click, and two scrollbar-thumb drags that each log exactly ONE click row despite a large drag. 1 further click on the Next chapter link, so 4 click rows in all. 11 keypress rows assuming full modifier release between combos: 4 PageDown, 1 End, 1 Home, Ctrl+Tab (2 rows), Ctrl+Shift+Tab (3 rows); 3 of the 11 are key_category=modifier and must be excluded from physical-effort counts. JEM logs NO mouse-movement, drag, or hover events at all.
journeys.stresses: Primary target: context_switch PRECISION under sustained scrolling, the known hard case where coherent whole-frame translation must not be read as a cut. 31 scroll spans against only 3 mid-session switches gives roughly a 10:1 adversarial ratio, the cleanest precision measurement in the corpus. Secondary targets: (a) the PageDown, End and Home beats produce wholesale content replacement with zero JEM context_switch, verified from source (JEM re-resolves identity only on a foreground change or a window-title NAMECHANGE, and none of these change the title), so every JAMS detection there is a false positive against JEM proxy labels and a true positive against human visual labels; this is the journey that forces the two label sets apart. (b) Two same-site dark-on-dark tab switches exercise the min_content_val floor, the documented false-negative class. (c) The scrollbar-drag beats prove JEM's physical truth (one click row, logged on button-down only) diverges from visual truth (massive translation), which matters before anyone tries to score clicks visually. (d) Segmentation stratum A: cues land on real boundaries at 186 s ('okay next' and 'next'), 226 s ('moving on'), 300 s ('then') and 328 s ('that is it'), all four verified against the DEFAULT_CUES list in segmentation.py.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: none beyond the general rule. doc.rust-lang.org is public static documentation, no account, no credentials, no personal data on screen. Keep the Edge favourites bar hidden and the profile renamed so no personal bookmarks or real name appear in frame (P3). Confirm no other person is audible in the room before starting the microphone recorder (P17).
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) If the 'Coal' theme is not applied the page renders near-white, and a maximized light page can trip the flash luma threshold and make the whole session unscoreable. Verify visually before Start and re-verify with detect_flash_runs immediately after (P14). (2) JEM's Edge identity is the FULL URL string whenever UIA enrichment succeeds, and the parsed tab title only when it does not. If enrichment drops out mid-session the identity path silently flips, which changes what counts as the same context. Check the detail column of every context_switch row: a 'uia:' prefix means the URL path was used. (3) The Rust Book is versioned with Rust releases; a release between takes changes page length and shifts every scroll beat. Record the page byte length or ETag at take time. (4) Scrollbar-thumb position depends on window size and display scaling; keep Edge maximized and never change scaling mid-session. (5) Pin and record the Edge version, because an Edge update can change how the address bar exposes its value to UIA and therefore which identity path JEM takes.
REPRODUCIBILITY: scroll beats are timed, not position-targeted, so a second take lands at slightly different page offsets. That is acceptable because the compared ground truth is event timing and event kind, not page position. All three mid-session switches are at least 30 s apart, so no structural sub-2 s false negatives are possible here.
