journeys.expected_physical: Switch-heavy, scroll-heavy, one large typing burst. COUNT CONVENTION: 20 customer-app context_switch ROWS, comprising the initial entry into Edge plus 19 mid-session identity changes. Scroll: ~51 JEM spans, mostly 4 to 6 notches, mixed up and down. Click rows: 5, being the opening focus click, one on-page contents anchor, one MIDDLE click (value_text 'middle', the rare button category), one in-article link, and one GitHub Issues tab. Keypress rows: roughly 105, dominated by the address-bar burst at 458 s (about 72 to 75 rows, shift-dependent); the remainder are 15 Ctrl+key or Alt+Left combos at 2 rows each. Roughly 22 to 24 rows are key_category=modifier and must be excluded from physical-effort counts. All counts assume full modifier release between combos, because JEM emits one row per key-DOWN with auto-repeat suppressed, so a held Ctrl across two presses would collapse to a single modifier row.
journeys.stresses: Primary target: context_switch RECALL on the wide-spacing stratum, with a deliberately hostile mix of switch difficulties. Of the 19 mid-session switches, 8 are MDN-to-MDN, MDN-to-GitHub or Wikipedia-to-GitHub dark-on-dark transitions sitting close to the min_content_val floor (the documented false-negative class), 6 are easy wholesale replacements, and 5 are same-site tab hops. That spread makes recall diagnostic rather than a single opaque number. Secondary targets: (a) the on-page contents anchor at 96 s is a clean visual-change-without-title-change case, verified against ContextSwitchConsumer's re-resolve triggers, forcing the precision denominator to come from human visual labels rather than JEM rows; (b) the middle click at 192 s exercises a JEM button category nothing else in the corpus produces; (c) the address-bar burst is real keypress-burst truth under a narrated soundtrack, exactly the condition that broke the audio-onset keypress detector, and must be reported as skipped or no_audio rather than zero; (d) SEGMENTATION STRATUM B: this script was re-checked word by word against the verified DEFAULT_CUES list in segmentation.py (six start, six next, six done phrases, matched case-insensitively on word boundaries) and contains NONE of them, so the seven real task boundaries must be found entirely by the scene-boundary fallback. Expected outcome is under-segmentation, and that is the measurement.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: GitHub must be SIGNED OUT, because a signed-in session puts a real avatar, username and private repo list in frame. MDN and Wikipedia anonymous. No credentials typed; the only typed text is a public MDN URL. Keep the favourites bar hidden (P3) and Edge's password-manager UI disabled. Cookie prompts dismissed before Start with the privacy-preserving option, never during the take. Confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone (P17).
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) MDN restructured its HTTP reference paths; /Web/HTTP/Headers/* now redirects to /Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/*. Open every tab and let the redirect settle BEFORE Start, because a redirect mid-take changes the title and writes an unplanned JEM switch. (2) JEM's Edge identity is the full URL when UIA enrichment succeeds and the parsed tab title when it does not; check the detail column for a 'uia:' prefix on every row so you know which path was used, and treat a mid-session flip as a session annotation, not a detector result. (3) GitHub's signed-out dark theme depends on prefers-color-scheme; with Windows in light mode the repo page renders near-white and maximized, a flash-collision risk. Verify visually. (4) GitHub's Issues tab is a soft navigation whose title-change timing is not fully deterministic, so the JEM boundary and the visual cut can diverge more than usual. Flag that switch in the annotation rather than trusting it blindly. (5) MDN and Wikipedia content changes over time and shifts scroll beats between takes; the comparison is event-level so this is acceptable, but record the take date. (6) Ctrl+6 at 530 s depends on the middle click having opened a sixth tab; if it did not, use whatever sits in position six and log the deviation rather than pausing to fix it.
REPRODUCIBILITY: every switch is at least 10 s from its neighbour, so no structural sub-2 s false negatives.

journeys.title: Tab-switching burst: rapid cycling, marginal spacing, and near-identical tabs
journeys.setup:
Shared preflight P1-P18, plus:
- Edge MAXIMIZED, exactly six tabs in this exact order:
  Tab 1: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Caching
  Tab 2: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Caching?jemdup=1
  Tab 3: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_cache
  Tab 4: https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy
  Tab 5: https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch04-01-what-is-ownership.html
  Tab 6: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cache-Control
- THE ?jemdup=1 QUERY STRING ON TAB 2 IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE REMOVED. JEM's Edge context identity is the FULL URL string when UIA enrichment succeeds (verified in ContextSwitchConsumer.BuildEdgeContext), and SwitchTo returns early without writing a row when the identity is unchanged. Two tabs on a byte-identical URL would therefore produce ZERO context_switch rows and block D would measure nothing at all. The query string makes the URL differ (so JEM logs a switch) while MDN ignores it and renders pixel-identically (so the content delta stays near zero). That is exactly the isolate block D needs.
- Tabs 1 and 2 must be scrolled to the SAME offset (both at the very top) so their rendered frames are as close to pixel-identical as possible.
- All six tabs dark: MDN theme Dark, Wikipedia Appearance Dark, GitHub signed out with Windows dark, Rust Book 'Coal'.
- All cookie and consent prompts dismissed before Start.
- KEY COMBOS: fully RELEASE Ctrl between every press. Holding Ctrl across a run of Tab presses collapses to ONE modifier row because JEM suppresses OS auto-repeat and writes only key-DOWN, which would silently halve the expected keypress count.
- JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'browser-research-03-tab-burst'. Single unpaused take.
- THIS JOURNEY DELIBERATELY VIOLATES the minimum switch-spacing rule in blocks A and C. That violation is pre-registered here, before any scoring, as a known-limit stratum. Do not treat the resulting false negatives as a JAMS defect and do not lower min_gap_seconds to chase them.

steps.action: After the opening flash clears, click once on the Edge window body to focus Edge, then sit still for 4 s.
steps.produces: First customer-app span opens. TRUTH EVENT #1, visually large. The click is also the opening audio transient; this journey has no other clicks, so do not skip it.

steps.action: BLOCK A, KNOWN-LIMIT STRATUM. Press Ctrl+Tab eight times at roughly 1.3 s intervals, fully releasing both keys between presses, cycling 1-2-3-4-5-6-1-2.
steps.produces: EIGHT JEM context_switch rows at ~1.3 s spacing + 16 keypress rows (8 modifier, 8 navigation). JAMS min_gap_seconds 2.0 and min_scene_len_frames 10 mean at most about four can ever be detected. Pre-declared structural false negatives: a harness artifact, not a detector defect.

steps.action: Sit completely still on the landing tab for 12 s, pointer parked over body text.
steps.produces: Quiet window separating the blocks. No detections expected.

steps.action: BLOCK B, FAIR-MEASUREMENT CONTROL. Press Ctrl+1, Ctrl+2, Ctrl+3, Ctrl+4, Ctrl+5, Ctrl+6, Ctrl+1, Ctrl+3 at roughly 10 s intervals, releasing fully between each, reading briefly at each stop.
steps.produces: EIGHT JEM context_switch rows at ~10 s spacing + 16 keypress rows. Every one is fairly detectable on spacing. Note the Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+2 hop is the near-identical pair and is expected to be missed on content grounds even here.

steps.action: Sit still for 12 s.
steps.produces: Quiet window.

steps.action: BLOCK C, MARGINAL STRATUM. Press Ctrl+4, Ctrl+5, Ctrl+6, Ctrl+3, Ctrl+5, Ctrl+4 at roughly 5.5 s intervals, releasing fully between each.
steps.produces: SIX JEM context_switch rows at ~5.5 s spacing + 12 keypress rows. Above the 2 s floor but tight; measures how spacing degrades matching and whether the greedy two-pointer sweep starts stealing detections.

steps.action: BLOCK D, NEAR-IDENTICAL-CONTENT STRATUM. Press Ctrl+1, wait 6 s, press Ctrl+2, wait 6 s, press Ctrl+1.
steps.produces: THREE JEM context_switch rows between two tabs whose URLs differ only by the ?jemdup=1 query string and which render the same page at the same scroll offset. Grayscale band-max delta is near zero. Expected JAMS false negatives on content grounds alone, with timing and spacing both perfectly fair. Isolates the content-floor failure from the spacing failure. VERIFY the three rows exist in the CSV before scoring: if they are absent, the query string was stripped and the block is void.

steps.action: BLOCK E. Press Ctrl+W to close the current tab, wait 6 s, press Ctrl+W again, wait 6 s, press Ctrl+Shift+T to reopen the last closed tab.
steps.produces: THREE JEM context_switch rows (each close moves focus to an adjacent tab and changes the title; the reopen restores a tab and changes it again) + 7 keypress rows (2+2+3). Tab-strip geometry changes on every one, a narrow-band change the band-max metric amplifies.

steps.action: Sit completely still for 22 s, hands off the keyboard, pointer parked over body text.
steps.produces: Final quiet window for false-positives-per-minute.

steps.action: Speak the closing line, stop speaking, then move to the JEM window and press Save.
steps.produces: Edge span closes, recorder span opens, end flash and sync tone fire.

narration.line: I am cycling through six tabs as fast as I can.
Then another one, and another one after that.
This is genuinely unpleasant and I am completely losing track.
Holding still on one page for a moment.
Taking each tab slowly, about ten seconds apart.
The first one is the caching overview.
This pace is much more comfortable to work at.
The Wikipedia page is dull and I do not want to read it.
The Caddy repository is on the next tab.
The Rust book chapter is a lovely change of scenery.
Halving the gap between switches to see what happens.
Now the second one, now the third one.
I cannot read anything at all at this speed and it is horrible.
These two tabs show the same page, which is the point.
Flipping between two identical views tells me nothing.
Closing a couple of tabs to tidy up.
I closed the wrong one and now I have to fix it.
The tab order came back exactly right, which is a real relief.

journeys.expected_physical: Keypress-dominated, almost no mouse. COUNT CONVENTION: 29 customer-app context_switch ROWS, comprising the initial entry into Edge plus 28 mid-session identity changes (8 in block A, 8 in B, 6 in C, 3 in D, 3 in E). Keypress rows: 57 assuming full modifier release between every combo, of which 29 are key_category=modifier. Block A 16, block B 16, block C 12, block D 6, block E 7 (Ctrl+W 2, Ctrl+W 2, Ctrl+Shift+T 3). NOTE the earlier estimate of ~68 rows was wrong: JEM writes one row per key-DOWN and suppresses OS auto-repeat, so each Ctrl+key combo is exactly 2 rows and Ctrl+Shift+T is exactly 3. If Ctrl is held across a run, the count drops sharply; read the actual count from the CSV. Zero scroll spans by design. Exactly ONE click row, the opening focus click, which is needed as an audio transient anchor. This is the only journey in the category with essentially no mouse input, which makes it a clean isolate for keyboard-only physical truth.
journeys.stresses: This journey exists to MEASURE THE FLOOR, not to pass. It separates three normally-confounded failure causes: spacing (block A at 1.3 s is below the structural 2 s limit, block C at 5.5 s is marginal, block B at 10 s is fair), content delta (block D switches between two tabs rendering the same page at the same offset, so spacing is generous and only the min_content_val floor can fail), and tab-strip geometry (block E's closes and reopens change only a narrow horizontal band, which the band-max content metric amplifies relative to a frame mean). Reporting blocks A through E separately turns one bad F1 into five actionable numbers. At roughly 6.5 switches per minute the cognitive lane is DELIBERATELY pinned at 100, which is itself the demonstration that the saturation knee makes the score blind to detector quality on switch-heavy work; the corpus needs at least one journey proving that, and this is it. SEGMENTATION STRATUM C: the cue words 'then' and 'after that' at 22 s, 'first' at 76 s, and 'now' twice at 180 s are all planted MID-BLOCK in non-boundary positions, while the five real block boundaries at approximately 10 s, 54 s, 152 s, 188 s and 212 s are left completely uncued. Cue false-positive rate falls straight out of that. All five cue words were verified against the DEFAULT_CUES list in segmentation.py.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: identical to journey 02. GitHub signed out, no accounts, no typed text at all beyond keyboard shortcuts, no personal data. Lowest privacy exposure in the category. Confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone (P17).
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) BLOCK D IS VOID WITHOUT THE ?jemdup=1 QUERY STRING. JEM's Edge identity is the full URL and SwitchTo writes no row when identity is unchanged, so two tabs on a byte-identical URL produce zero truth events. Confirm the query string survives in the address bar before Start, and confirm three block-D rows exist in the CSV after. (2) The pre-registration matters more here than anywhere else. Blocks A and C knowingly break the spacing rule. If anyone later lowers min_gap_seconds or widens MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS to rescue this journey's score, the whole campaign's holdout numbers become uninterpretable. Record the block boundaries in the session log at record time. (3) Ctrl+W must close TABS, not the window. Confirm more than two tabs remain before each press; closing the window ends the journey and wastes the take. (4) Ctrl+Shift+T restores the last-closed tab, but if Edge restores it in a different position the later block-E switch identities differ from plan. Log what actually happened rather than retrying. (5) Eight switches in ten seconds can outrun JEM's own namechange coalescing (hooks.namechange_quiet_ms is 200 with a poll on top), so some of block A's switches may be coalesced away by JEM itself and the row count may come back below eight. Count the actual rows and treat the CSV as truth. (6) If UIA enrichment fails, Edge identity falls back to the parsed tab title; tabs 1 and 2 have the SAME title, so block D would again collapse to zero rows. Check the detail column for the 'uia:' prefix on block-D rows and void the block if it is absent.
REPRODUCIBILITY: keystroke timing by hand varies by a few hundred milliseconds per press. Count silently or use a metronome off the recorded monitor. The block STRUCTURE (8 fast, 8 slow, 6 marginal, 3 near-identical, 3 tab-strip) is what must reproduce, not the exact millisecond.

journeys.title: Static dwell: long reading with three multi-minute zero-change blocks and sparse narration
journeys.setup:
Shared preflight P1-P18, plus:
- P1 IS CRITICAL HERE: screensaver OFF, display sleep OFF, 'turn off my screen after' set to Never, and Do Not Disturb ON. This journey contains a 150 s block with zero input; a screen blank or a notification toast destroys the take.
- Edge MAXIMIZED, exactly one tab at Start:
  Tab 1: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_the_Internet
- Wikipedia Appearance menu: Color = Dark. Verify the article renders dark before Start. FALLBACK if the dark option is unavailable in the current Wikipedia release: use https://doc.rust-lang.org/book/ch00-00-introduction.html with the 'Coal' theme and substitute the Rust Book's chapter 1 for the second article; the dwell structure is unchanged.
- Edge sleeping tabs OFF (P4): a discarded background tab reloading mid-dwell writes a spurious title change and therefore a spurious JEM switch.
- Disable Edge's password-manager prompts and the download shelf in this profile. A password-manager popup during a 150 s dwell is the one real privacy exposure in this journey.
- Park the mouse pointer over plain body text, never over a link or a UI control, during every dwell block. A hovered link draws an underline and a status-bar URL, which is a real visual change that JEM cannot log at all, because JEM records no mouse-movement or hover events.
- Scroll the article to the top. Close every other tab. Check for and dismiss any Wikipedia fundraising banner.
- KEY COMBOS: fully RELEASE all modifiers between combos.
- JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'browser-research-04-static-dwell'. Single unpaused take.

steps.action: After the opening flash clears, click once on the Edge window body (plain text, not a link) to focus Edge.
steps.produces: First customer-app span opens. TRUTH EVENT #1, visually large. This click and the keypress burst at 434 s are the only audible transients in the whole take, so both are load-bearing for refine_offset_by_events; do not skip either.

steps.action: Read the article lead section. No input.
steps.produces: No further rows.

steps.action: Three wheel bursts of 4 notches down, about 7 s apart.
steps.produces: JEM 3 scroll spans.

steps.action: DWELL BLOCK 1, 110 s. Read the packet-switching section without touching the mouse or keyboard at all. Pointer parked over body text.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows for 110 s. ZERO visual change. The primary false-positives-per-minute measurement window in the whole corpus. Any JAMS context_switch, scroll or click detection inside this window is unambiguously a false positive with no label ambiguity whatsoever.

steps.action: Two wheel bursts of 4 notches down.
steps.produces: JEM 2 scroll spans, re-establishing that the detector still fires after a long quiet period.

steps.action: MICRO-SCROLL BLOCK. Single 1-notch wheel ticks every ~18 s, five times, reading between each.
steps.produces: JEM 5 scroll spans with value_num 1 and t_start_ms equal to t_end_ms (each tick is a one-event span, and the 18 s gap far exceeds scroll_idle_close_ms of 800). Each produces a shift far below the JAMS scrolls threshold, so these are expected to be INVISIBLE to JAMS. Below-threshold physical stratum: JEM says five events, JAMS should honestly say zero, and that gap must be reported as a threshold limit, not as five misses.

steps.action: DWELL BLOCK 2, 100 s. No input at all. One short narration line at the midpoint to break total silence.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows for 100 s. Second quiet window. Also exercises Silero VAD across roughly 50 s of silence on either side of a single utterance.

steps.action: Click an inline citation marker in the body text (any bracketed reference number) to jump to the references list.
steps.produces: JEM 1 click row. This changes only the URL fragment; the document title does NOT change, so no window NAMECHANGE fires and JEM never re-resolves identity: NO context_switch row, against a wholesale viewport jump. Visual-truth-only beat. Confirm from the CSV rather than assuming.

steps.action: Press Alt+Left to return to the reading position, then release.
steps.produces: JEM 2 keypress rows (1 modifier, 1 navigation). A fragment-history step with no title change, so NO JEM context_switch. Second visual-truth-only beat.

steps.action: Three wheel bursts of 5 notches down.
steps.produces: JEM 3 scroll spans.

steps.action: Press Ctrl+T, then type en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Wide_Web in the address bar, then press Enter.
steps.produces: KEYPRESS BURST. The URL is 36 characters; capitals and the two underscores each need Shift, so expect roughly 36 alphanumeric plus 4 to 6 modifier plus 1 whitespace, plus 2 for Ctrl+T: about 45 to 50 rows. Read the actual count from the CSV rather than assuming. TWO JEM truth events: #2 when Ctrl+T changes the title to the new-tab page, and #3 when the article loads and the title changes again.

steps.action: Two wheel bursts of 4 notches down the new article.
steps.produces: JEM 2 scroll spans.

steps.action: DWELL BLOCK 3, 150 s. Absolute silence, absolute stillness. Read the early browser history section.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows and ZERO speech for 150 s. The longest quiet window in the corpus. Tests false-positives-per-minute and the transcription quiet-speech retry rule: whole-take speech coverage stays near 9 percent, comfortably above the 2 percent retry trigger verified in transcription.py, so no rescue pass should fire. Verify from the run that it did not.

steps.action: Press Ctrl+Shift+Tab to return to the History of the Internet tab, then release.
steps.produces: JEM TRUTH EVENT #4 + 3 keypress rows. Wikipedia dark to Wikipedia dark, same site, similar layout: hard class, arriving immediately after a 150 s quiet period, which is the worst case for a trailing-mean adaptive trigger computed over only the previous few frames.

steps.action: Two wheel bursts of 4 notches UP to find the date you wanted to check.

narration.line: I am reading the history of the internet article end to end.
The opening section covers the early packet switching work.
That was a long stretch of reading without touching anything.

Back up to where I left off in the article.

The timeline matches what I had in my notes exactly.
I am really pleased with what I found here.

journeys.expected_physical: Deliberately minimal. COUNT CONVENTION: 5 customer-app context_switch ROWS, comprising the initial entry into Edge plus 4 mid-session identity changes. Scroll: ~17 JEM spans, of which 5 are single-notch micro-scrolls expected to be invisible to JAMS. Click rows: 2, being the opening focus click and the citation marker. Keypress rows: roughly 52, almost all of them the address-bar burst at 434 s (about 45 to 50 rows, shift-dependent), plus Alt+Left (2), Ctrl+Shift+Tab (3) and Ctrl+Tab (2). Three blocks totalling 360 s, just over half the journey, contain ZERO physical events of any kind. Note for alignment: because physical events are so sparse, the opening click and the typing burst carry nearly all the weight for refine_offset_by_events, which correlates JEM click and keypress times against microphone transients.
journeys.stresses: This is the corpus's negative control and earns its slot on that alone. Three blocks of 110 s, 100 s and 150 s with literally zero visual change and zero logged events give an unambiguous false-positive denominator: no label ambiguity, no proxy-versus-visual disagreement, nothing to adjudicate. Every detection inside those 360 s is wrong by construction, and nothing else in the plan produces that. It also puts three lanes far off their saturation points simultaneously (cognitive at roughly 0.4 switches per minute, spoken_word around 12 words per minute, time_segment at 11.8 of 30 minutes), so it is the journey most likely to produce a genuinely responsive, non-pinned total score and to satisfy the lane-non-saturation gate. Further targets: (a) the five 1-notch micro-scrolls are a pre-declared below-threshold physical stratum where the honest JAMS answer is zero and the correct report is 'threshold limit', not 'five misses'; (b) the citation jump and the Alt+Left fragment step are visual change with no JEM row, verified against JEM's re-resolve triggers, feeding the human-visual-label precision denominator; (c) the switch at 638 s lands immediately after 150 s dead still, the adversarial case for an adaptive trigger computed from a short trailing window; (d) long silences plus sparse speech stress Silero VAD and sit deliberately above the 2 percent coverage threshold for the quiet-speech retry pass.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: Wikipedia anonymous, no account, no personal data, no typed text except a public Wikipedia URL. Very low exposure. The one real risk is an Edge notification bubble, download shelf or password-manager prompt appearing during a 150 s dwell, so disable those in the JEM profile before Start. Confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone (P17), which matters more here than elsewhere because the room is silent for minutes at a time and will pick up background conversation cleanly.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) Screen blank, display sleep, screensaver or a notification toast during any dwell block destroys the block's value and probably the take. Verify the power plan before Start, not after. (2) Wikipedia's dark mode for logged-out readers has moved between releases; if unavailable, a maximized light article is a flash-collision risk, so use the documented Rust Book fallback rather than recording a light page. (3) The pointer MUST be parked off any interactive element during dwells. A hovered link underline or tooltip is a real visual change that JEM cannot log at all, because JEM records no mouse-movement or hover events, and it silently converts a clean negative window into an ambiguous one. (4) A Wikipedia fundraising or notice banner, especially an animated one, contaminates the dwell blocks. Check before Start and re-check between takes. (5) Lazy-loading images scrolling into view during a dwell also contaminate it; let the article settle fully before each dwell begins. (6) Edge sleeping tabs must be OFF, because a background tab reloading changes the window title and writes an unplanned JEM switch straight into a dwell block.
REPRODUCIBILITY: excellent. The structure is 'read and do nothing' for fixed durations, the easiest thing in the corpus to repeat. Use a silent visible timer OFF the recorded monitor to hit the 110, 100 and 150 s blocks. Never put a timer on the recorded screen: a ticking clock is a per-second visual change that would ruin the entire point of the journey.

journeys.title: In-page find and anchor navigation: HTTP status codes, planted cue words
journeys.setup:
Shared preflight P1-P18, plus:
- Edge MAXIMIZED, exactly two tabs:
  Tab 1: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_HTTP_status_codes
  Tab 2: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Status
- Wikipedia Appearance = Dark; MDN theme = Dark. Verify both render dark before Start.
- Wikipedia's sidebar table of contents must be EXPANDED before Start, with the '4xx client errors' and '5xx server errors' entries visible without further expansion. The anchor clicks at 186 s and 222 s depend on this; if the entries are collapsed under a parent, expand that parent now and note it in the session log.
- Both tabs scrolled to the top. Find bar closed on both.
- NUMBER NORMALISATION, PRE-DECLARED NOW: this script speaks numbers as words ('four oh four', 'five oh three'). The WER normalisation protocol must map digit strings and spoken number words to a single common form. Decide the mapping once, write it into the session log BEFORE recording, and never change it after seeing a score.
- KEY COMBOS: fully RELEASE all modifiers between combos.
- JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'browser-research-05-find-and-anchors'. Single unpaused take.

journeys.expected_physical: Find-bar and keyboard heavy, moderate scroll, light click. COUNT CONVENTION: 6 customer-app context_switch ROWS, comprising the initial entry into Edge plus 5 mid-session identity changes. Keypress rows: roughly 70 assuming full modifier release, distributed as Ctrl+F plus '418' plus Enter (6), two Enters (2), Escape (1), Ctrl+F plus 'Too Many Requests' plus three Enters (about 25, shift-dependent), Escape (1), Ctrl+F plus 'gateway' plus five Enters (14), Escape (1), three Alt+Left (6), Alt+Left (2), Ctrl+Tab (2), Ctrl+F plus '304' plus Enter (6), Escape (1), Ctrl+Shift+Tab (3). Roughly 12 to 15 are key_category=modifier. Click rows: 5, being the opening focus click, two sidebar anchors, the 404 link and the 304 entry. Scroll: ~17 spans. Because privacy.capture_key_text is OFF, only key_category is recorded, so treat every typed-string count as approximate and read the real number from the CSV.
journeys.stresses: Primary target: the find bar as a BAND-MAX adversary. Eleven separate find-bar open, cycle and close events produce changes confined to a narrow horizontal band plus a viewport jump, with zero window-title change and therefore zero JEM context_switch rows, so every JAMS detection across them is a JEM-proxy false positive and a human-visual true positive. Nothing else in the corpus isolates band-localised change this cleanly. Secondary targets: (a) the five rapid Enter presses at 116 s are sub-2 s visual jumps that are NOT switches, which probes whether min_gap_seconds accidentally buys precision here while costing recall in journey 03; (b) the two sidebar anchors and the three Alt+Left fragment steps are five more fragment-only navigations with no JEM row, verified against JEM's re-resolve triggers, in direct contrast to the Alt+Left at 348 s which IS a full-document back navigation and DOES produce a row, so the journey contains the same keystroke in both a truth-producing and a truth-silent role; (c) the find bar appears on two different sites with different overlay styling, testing site-dependence of the band-max response. SEGMENTATION: cue words 'then' at 58 s, 'now' at 152 s, 'first' at 278 s and 'that is it' at 464 s are all verified against DEFAULT_CUES; 'then' and 'now' sit mid-block in non-boundary positions while 'first' sits near the real 404 boundary, giving a mixed cue precision sample.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: Wikipedia and MDN anonymous, no account, no credentials. The only typed text is public search terms and status code numbers. Keep the favourites bar hidden and the password manager disabled. Confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone (P17).
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) The NUMBER NORMALISATION protocol must be written down before recording. Numbers spoken as words against a reference transcript containing digits will inflate WER arbitrarily, and deciding the mapping after seeing a score is exactly the retuning the evaluation rules forbid. (2) Wikipedia's sidebar table of contents collapses and restructures between releases; verify the two target entries are visible and clickable before Start, and log any expansion you had to perform. (3) The find bar's exact geometry and highlight colour are Edge-version dependent, and the band-max response is the whole point of the journey, so pin and record the Edge version. (4) On the MDN Status page the '304 Not Modified' entry may be rendered as a table row link rather than a list link depending on the current page structure; verify it navigates to its own page before Start, and if it does not, substitute another status entry that does and log the substitution. (5) If UIA enrichment fails, Edge identity falls back to the parsed tab title, which does not change on fragment navigation either, so the fragment beats stay truth-silent on both identity paths. That is a rare case where the two paths agree; record the detail column anyway.
REPRODUCIBILITY: good. Every beat is a discrete keystroke or a named click target rather than a timed scroll position. The five rapid Enter presses at 116 s are the only hand-timed sub-2 s sequence; count them silently rather than trying to hit exact milliseconds, and log the actual spacing from the CSV.

journeys.title: Split-screen comparison with cross-application note-taking (Edge and Notepad)
journeys.setup:
NOTE: this journey was authored fresh during review because the original browser-research-06 was truncated out of the reviewed input (see category_notes). It must be reconciled against the original before recording.
Shared preflight P1-P18, plus:
- Snap Edge to the LEFT half of the JEM-selected monitor (Win+Left) and Notepad to the RIGHT half (Win+Right). Neither window is maximized. Do the snapping BEFORE pressing Start so no window-arrangement animation lands in the take.
- Edge, exactly two tabs:
  Tab 1: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/Cache-Control
  Tab 2: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/ETag
  Both dark (MDN theme Dark). Cookie prompts dismissed. Both scrolled to top.
- Notepad: a single empty untitled document. Turn Word Wrap ON so typing never scrolls horizontally. Set the Notepad theme to Dark (Settings, App theme, Dark) so neither half of the frame is near-white.
- Windows 11 Notepad autosaves and may show a modified marker in its title on first edit. That is a window-title change and therefore an EXTRA JEM context_switch that is not in the step list. Pre-registered here: expect up to one extra row on the first Notepad edit, read the actual titles from the CSV, and do not score it as a false positive against JAMS.
- KEY COMBOS: fully RELEASE all modifiers between combos.
- JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'browser-research-06-split-screen-notes'. Single unpaused take.

journeys.expected_physical: Cross-application, click and typing heavy, moderate scroll. COUNT CONVENTION: 11 customer-app context_switch ROWS as planned, comprising the initial entry into Edge plus 10 mid-session identity changes, PLUS up to 1 unplanned extra row if Windows 11 Notepad changes its title on first edit. Read the actual count from the CSV and annotate the extra row rather than scoring it as a JAMS false positive. Click rows: 7, being the opening focus click plus six half-window focus clicks. Keypress rows: roughly 177, being four typed notes of about 46, 37, 41 and 44 rows plus two Alt+Tab (4), Ctrl+Tab (2) and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (3). Only about 7 rows are key_category=modifier, the lowest modifier fraction in the category, because the bulk is plain lowercase prose. Scroll: ~18 spans, every one of them translating only HALF the frame. Both Notepad and Edge spans are customer-app spans; only the JEM recorder spans are excluded.
journeys.stresses: This is the only journey in the category with non-maximized windows and genuine cross-PROCESS switching, and it fills two gaps nothing else covers. (a) PARTIAL-FRAME CHANGE: every switch and every scroll alters only half the frame, so the measured delta is roughly halved before the detector sees it. The min_content_val floor and the whole-frame translation_like post-filter were both characterised on maximized single-window content, and this journey measures how far that characterisation transfers. (b) CROSS-PROCESS IDENTITY: JEM identity is process name plus semantic title, so the Edge-to-Notepad switches change identity on the process component, which is the most reliable truth signal JEM produces, while being visually among the faintest events in the corpus (a title-bar highlight and a caret). That combination, maximum proxy confidence against minimum visual delta, is precisely the divergence the September 18 rescore quantified on the Outlook session, and this journey reproduces it deliberately and repeatably instead of by accident. (c) The click at 46 s and the Alt+Tab at 118 s reach the same destination by mouse and by keyboard, isolating whether physical-lane inputs move the score when the cognitive lane does not. (d) The 40 s two-window dwell is a distinct false-positive condition from journey 04's single-window dwells. (e) Notepad's possible first-edit title change is a pre-registered example of a JEM row with essentially zero visual correlate, useful for the proxy-only stratum.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: type ONLY the four exact note strings given in the steps. Do not improvise notes, because Notepad content is fully legible in the recording and JEM video captures everything visible regardless of the capture_key_text setting. Never open an existing document in Notepad; start from an empty untitled file and do not save it. Both sites are public and anonymous. Confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone (P17).
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) Window arrangement must be fixed before Start. Any snap, resize or drag mid-take changes the geometry that every partial-frame measurement depends on and voids the comparison against other takes. Record the exact pixel geometry of both windows in the session log. (2) Windows 11 Notepad's title behaviour on first edit differs across builds and may add one unplanned context_switch row. Pre-registered above; read the titles from the CSV and annotate rather than retuning anything. (3) Notepad must be in Dark theme, because a half-frame of near-white text on a dark desktop raises the mean luma and can interact with the flash detector. Verify visually before Start. (4) Alt+Tab shows a window-picker overlay across the centre of the screen for as long as the keys are held. Press and release briskly, and note that the overlay is a real full-frame visual event with no JEM row of its own beyond the keypresses. (5) If more than two windows are open, Alt+Tab may land somewhere unplanned; close everything else before Start and verify Alt+Tab toggles only between Edge and Notepad. (6) Word Wrap must be ON, or long notes scroll horizontally and change the visual character of the typing beats.
REPRODUCIBILITY: good, provided window geometry is recorded and restored. The four note strings are fixed text, so typing-burst row counts should reproduce within a few rows across takes; any larger variation means a modifier was held or a typo was corrected, and should be logged.

journeys.title: Animated-content dwell: continuous pixel change with almost no logged input
journeys.setup:
NOTE: this journey was authored fresh during review because the original browser-research-07 was truncated out of the reviewed input (see category_notes). It must be reconciled against the original before recording.
Shared preflight P1-P18, plus:
- Edge MAXIMIZED, exactly two tabs:
  Tab 1: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_animations/Using_CSS_animations
  Tab 2: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/CSS_transitions/Using_CSS_transitions
- MDN theme Dark on both. Cookie prompts dismissed. Both scrolled to the top.
- BEFORE Start, scroll Tab 1 until at least one LOOPING live example is visible and confirm with your own eyes that it is still moving after ten seconds. These pages host continuously running CSS animations; if the current page revision no longer autoplays anything, this journey has no subject. Substitute another MDN page with a confirmed looping live example and log the substitution.
- Confirm no video autoplays with sound. This journey has no audio requirement beyond the narration and the sync tone.
- KEY COMBOS: fully RELEASE all modifiers between combos.
- JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'browser-research-07-animated-dwell'. Single unpaused take.

steps.action: After the opening flash clears, click once on the Edge window body (plain text, well away from any live example) to focus Edge.
steps.produces: First customer-app span opens. TRUTH EVENT #1. This is also the opening audio transient; this journey has very few physical events, so it is load-bearing for alignment.

steps.action: ANIMATED DWELL 1, 45 s. Sit completely still with a looping animation in view. Do not touch the mouse or keyboard. Park the pointer over plain body text, well clear of every live example.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows for 45 s, against CONTINUOUS PIXEL CHANGE. This is the corpus's only window where the screen changes constantly and the logged truth is unambiguously empty. Every JAMS context_switch, scroll or click detection here is a false positive against BOTH label sets, proxy and human visual, because a looping animation is not a task boundary to any rater.

steps.action: Three wheel bursts of 4 notches down, about 7 s apart, to bring further live examples into view.
steps.produces: JEM 3 scroll spans. Note these are translation superimposed on non-translational animation, which is the case the translation_like post-filter cannot cleanly decompose.

steps.action: ANIMATED DWELL 2, 50 s. Sit completely still with the newly revealed animations looping.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows for 50 s against continuous non-translational change. Second pure false-positive window.

steps.action: Two wheel bursts of 5 notches down to a purely STATIC prose section with no live example anywhere in the viewport. Verify visually that nothing on screen is moving.
steps.produces: JEM 2 scroll spans, then a static frame.

steps.action: STATIC CONTROL DWELL, 40 s. Sit completely still on the static prose.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows and ZERO visual change for 40 s. This is the matched control for the two animated dwells: same page, same site, same posture, same duration scale, differing only in whether pixels move. The difference in false-positive rate between this window and the animated windows isolates motion sensitivity from every other confound.

steps.action: Press Ctrl+Tab to move to the CSS transitions tab, then release.
steps.produces: JEM TRUTH EVENT #2 + 2 keypress rows. MDN to MDN, dark-on-dark, same layout: hard class. It also arrives shortly after a static dwell, unlike the switch in journey 04 which arrives after a long one.

steps.action: Two wheel bursts of 4 notches down to bring a hover-triggered transition demo into view.
steps.produces: JEM 2 scroll spans.

steps.action: HOVER BLOCK, 40 s. Move the pointer slowly on and off a hover-triggered transition demo, roughly once every 8 s, five times. Do NOT click anything.
steps.produces: THE SHARPEST JEM-BLINDNESS BEAT IN THE CORPUS: five large, deliberate, visually obvious animated state changes, and JEM logs ABSOLUTELY NOTHING, because it records no mouse-movement and no hover events at all, only button-down, keys, wheel notches and context changes. Physical truth is empty, visual truth is five clear events. Any JAMS detection here is a false positive against JEM proxy labels and a true positive against human visual labels, with a far larger delta than the fragment-navigation beats in journeys 02, 04 and 05.

steps.action: Move the pointer back to plain body text, then sit completely still for 35 s.
steps.produces: ZERO JEM rows for 35 s. Quiet window with static content.

steps.action: Press Ctrl+Shift+Tab to return to the animations tab, then release.
steps.produces: JEM TRUTH EVENT #3 + 3 keypress rows. Second dark-on-dark same-site switch, this one landing back onto a page with animations running.

steps.action: Three wheel bursts of 4 notches UP.
steps.produces: JEM 3 scroll spans, direction up.

steps.action: Sit completely still for 18 s with animations in view.
steps.produces: Final quiet window, animated.

journeys.expected_physical: Almost no physical input by design. COUNT CONVENTION: 3 customer-app context_switch ROWS, comprising the initial entry into Edge plus 2 mid-session identity changes. Click rows: exactly 1, the opening focus click. Keypress rows: exactly 5, being Ctrl+Tab (2) and Ctrl+Shift+Tab (3), of which 3 are key_category=modifier. Scroll: ~10 spans. CRITICAL: the 40 s hover block at 220 s produces ZERO JEM rows of any kind, because JEM records no mouse-movement and no hover events. Two full minutes and fifteen seconds of the take (the three dwells plus the hover block) contain no logged physical event whatsoever, and roughly half of that time the screen is nonetheless changing continuously. Alignment note: with only one click and five keypresses in the whole take, refine_offset_by_events has very little to correlate against, so the two sync-tone anchors carry nearly all the alignment weight here. Verify tone detection succeeded before trusting any timing metric from this journey.
journeys.stresses: This journey isolates MOTION SENSITIVITY, which nothing else in the category touches. Every other journey's false-positive windows are static; this one pairs 95 s of continuously animated zero-input dwell against a matched 40 s static zero-input dwell on the same page, same site, same posture. The difference in false positives per minute between those two windows is a clean, single-variable measurement of how the detector responds to non-translational motion, and it cannot be obtained from a static corpus. The scroll beats at 58 s deliberately superimpose whole-frame translation on looping animation, the one case the translation_like post-filter cannot decompose, so a detection there is diagnostic rather than merely wrong. The hover block at 220 s is the corpus's sharpest demonstration that JEM proxy truth and human visual truth are different label sets: five large, deliberate, visually obvious state changes with literally zero rows in events.csv, because JEM logs no pointer motion. That is a far bigger delta than the fragment-navigation beats elsewhere, and it is the beat to cite whenever anyone proposes scoring visual detections against JEM rows alone. Finally, with only 2 mid-session switches across 6 minutes the cognitive lane sits at roughly 0.3 switches per minute, far below saturation, so this journey contributes a genuinely responsive score alongside journey 04.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: MDN anonymous, public documentation, no account, no credentials, no typed text at all. The lowest exposure in the category alongside journey 03. Confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone (P17).
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: (1) THE JOURNEY HAS NO SUBJECT IF NOTHING ANIMATES. MDN revises these pages and live examples can be replaced or made click-to-run. Confirm with your own eyes, before Start, that at least one example loops unprompted for ten continuous seconds, and log which example it was. If none does, substitute another page with a confirmed looping example and log the substitution rather than recording a static take under this scenario name. (2) The static control dwell at 150 s must be genuinely static. Verify no live example, no animated banner and no lazy-loading image is anywhere in the viewport before the dwell begins; a single moving pixel destroys the matched-control comparison that the whole journey rests on. (3) During the hover block, hover ONLY over the demo and never over a link, because a hovered link also paints a status-bar URL in the bottom corner, which adds an uncontrolled second change region. (4) Do not click during the hover block. A single stray click writes a JEM row into a window whose entire value is that it has none. (5) Animation frame rate depends on the display refresh rate and on Edge's throttling when the window is not focused; keep Edge focused throughout and record the monitor refresh rate in the session log, because it changes how much motion lands in a 30 fps capture. (6) Reduced-motion settings suppress CSS animations entirely. Confirm Windows Settings, Accessibility, Visual effects, Animation effects is ON before Start, and record that it was.
REPRODUCIBILITY: the dwell structure reproduces easily, but the hover block is hand-timed pointer motion that JEM cannot log, so it leaves no record of what actually happened. Narrate each hover aloud as you perform it so the microphone track carries an independent timestamp for every one of the five, and note in the session log that those five timestamps come from the audio, not from events.csv.

journeys.title: Cold clone, inspect, first build of a public repo
journeys.setup: Run Standard Pre-Flight P1-P9 from category_notes. Deltas: (a) DRY-RUN GATE (mandatory, unrecorded, same day): perform the whole journey once and confirm that `npm test` on the cloned repo exits GREEN on this machine's Node version - the narration at 520 s asserts a passing suite, so if express 4.21.2's mocha suite does not pass under Node 26 the fixture is wrong and must be pinned (via nvm to the newest Node LTS the tag supports) BEFORE recording; never change the narration at record time. Record the measured clone and install durations and key the narration card to actions, not to the clock. (b) Warm the npm cache once before the first take by cloning to a throwaway dir, running the same install, then deleting it. (c) Verify `git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/expressjs/express.git` still resolves tag 4.21.2; if not, pin to the newest 4.x tag - the narration never names the version. (d) D:\jem-journeys\work must exist and be EMPTY; delete D:\jem-journeys\work\express-4212 between takes or the clone step fails. (e) Launch the terminal with `wt --title repo -d D:\jem-journeys\work pwsh -NoLogo ; new-tab --title scratch -d D:\jem-journeys pwsh -NoLogo` and select the repo tab. (f) Shorten the pwsh prompt to the leaf directory only (`function prompt { "PS $(Split-Path -Leaf $PWD)> " }` in the session) so no user-profile path renders on camera. (g) VS Code fully closed before the take, so it opens with no editors and a default Explorer scroll position. CRITICAL: record DISPLAY1 only; every journey window on DISPLAY1, JEM and the narration card on DISPLAY2; single unpaused take; clap once inside the opening flash and once inside the closing flash.

steps.action: With the WAV recorder already running on DISPLAY2, press Start in JEM. A white full-screen flash appears on DISPLAY1. Clap once, sharply, hands well apart, while the flash is on screen (flash duration is raised to 700 ms for the campaign, so this is hittable).

journeys.stresses: CUED SEGMENTATION STRATUM. All five human task boundaries carry an explicit phrase from the verified DEFAULT_CUES list - 'to start' at 24 s, 'moving on' at 104 s, 312 s and 486 s, and 'that's it' at 538 s - and every other line was checked against the full cue vocabulary and is clean, so this journey measures the intended cue path in isolation. Primary detector target is the context_switch dark-on-dark failure class: the WindowsTerminal -> Code transition at 112 s and the repo -> scratch tab transition at 408 s are both dark-surface-to-dark-surface, exactly the low-absolute-luma-delta case that the 9.6 content floor discards and that min_content_val=4 recovered on the old calibration session. Secondary target is the scroll post-filter: 10 deliberate wheel bursts interleaved with 6 genuine visual replacements give the labelled visual-change-versus-scroll development data the previous hillclimb asked for and could not get. It also carries the corpus's cleanest long auto-scrolling sample (35 s of mocha spec output) as a false-positive probe, and three input-free dwells that test that silence produces no spurious cuts. Lane arithmetic at a nominal 10.0 minute take: context_switch 12 switches = 1.20/min * 36.75 = 44; spoken_word roughly 352 words = 35 wpm * 2.47 = 87, high but deliberately short of the 40.5 wpm pin; neg_density 2 negative lines of 22 by duration = roughly 23; time_segment 33. Development split.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: no credentials anywhere. The clone is anonymous HTTPS from a public repo, nothing is pushed, no account is touched, Edge is not used. The pwsh prompt is shortened to the leaf directory in pre-flight so no user-profile path renders. Mic is live end to end, so no background conversation. REPRODUCIBILITY: npm install duration varies with cache state and network, so warm the cache before the first take; the express tag must be verified before recording; delete the clone directory between takes; VS Code must be launched fresh with all editors closed or the Explorer scroll position and open-tab set differ between takes. THE DRY-RUN GATE IS LOAD-BEARING: the 520 s line asserts a green suite, and express 4.x mocha under a very new Node is the most likely thing in this journey to fail - if it does, fix the environment, never the script. GROUND TRUTH: nothing is edited here so the VS Code dirty-dot artifact does not apply, but the Ctrl+P quick-open overlay changes the window title momentarily on some builds - check the first take's CSV for spurious switches at 238 s and 262 s and annotate them as an instrumentation class if present. Keep every Alt+Tab a single quick press-and-release so the switcher overlay is consistent across takes. FLASH COLLISION: mocha's spec reporter is near-white text on dark background - run the jem_eval flash detector on the first take before recording anything else and confirm the 64x36 grayscale mean never exceeds 245 during the test run, because the evaluator hard-aborts with 'sync alignment ambiguous' if it finds any bright run beyond the two sync flashes. Switch spacing: the closest pair is 20 s apart, well clear of the 500 ms match tolerance and the 10 s minimum segment.

journeys.expected_physical: Approximately 18 left clicks - Explorer tree selections, caret placement on lines 14 and 22, one Ctrl+click on a stack-trace path, and two focus clicks into the integrated terminal - excluding the two JEM button clicks on DISPLAY2. Approximately 245 keypresses, of which roughly 30 are editing or modifier category (four Backspaces, one Ctrl+Shift+K, two Ctrl+S, four Alt+Tab rows, one Ctrl+backtick). 4 to 5 wheel scroll bursts totalling roughly 16 notches, split across Code.exe and WindowsTerminal.exe.
journeys.stresses: UNCUED SEGMENTATION STRATUM - verified line by line against the real DEFAULT_CUES vocabulary (start: let's get started / lets get started / get started / to start / first / starting; next: okay next / next / moving on / now / then / after that; done: done / finished / complete / that's it / that is it / finally). Not one of those words or phrases appears anywhere in these eighteen lines, so all six human boundaries must be recovered from scene boundaries alone. This journey is also built around two deliberately opposed label-noise cases that nothing else in the corpus isolates. First, the integrated terminal: the Ctrl+backtick at 15 s and four `npm test` runs produce large bottom-band visual changes with ZERO JEM events, so every JAMS detection there scores as a false positive against JEM proxy labels while being a correct visual detection - the single cleanest demonstration that context_switch precision must be reported against human visual labels, not against JEM. Second, the VS Code dirty dot: four JEM switches at 178, 205, 345 and 365 s are caused solely by one character appearing or disappearing in the window title, with essentially no on-screen change, so they are guaranteed structural false negatives for any vision-based detector and belong in the report as instrumentation artifacts rather than JAMS defects. Also exercises terminal command enrichment (detail=uia:git diff at 265 s) and provides a fully deterministic fixture whose stack-trace text is byte-identical across takes, making it the best WER sample in the category for domain terms like 'priority dot js', 'type error on undefined' and 'line fourteen'. Lane arithmetic at a nominal 8.0 minute take: context_switch 12 = 1.50/min * 36.75 = 55; spoken_word roughly 270 words = 34 wpm * 2.47 = 83; neg_density 4 of 18 by duration = roughly 56; time_segment 27. Development split.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: entirely local, no network, no accounts, no credentials. The fixture's repo-local author identity keeps the git log at 420 s free of real identity - verify before the first take. Mic live throughout. REPRODUCIBILITY: reset.ps1 must run between takes; the two named line numbers are spoken aloud so any fixture edit that shifts them invalidates the WER reference; VS Code must open with no editors and the integrated terminal closed or the 15 s Ctrl+backtick beat produces a different visual delta. The Ctrl+click at 80 s depends on VS Code rendering the trace path as a link - if terminal link detection is off, the beat degrades to a manual Explorer click, the narration at 92 s still holds, and the click count is unchanged, but note the substitution in the take log. GROUND TRUTH: the four dirty-dot switches must be annotated as a separate class BEFORE scoring, or recall is understated by four events on a denominator of twelve, which is a 33 percent artificial penalty. SWITCH SPACING: this review moved the due-dates.js click from 310 s to 316 s because the original sat at exactly 10.000 s from the preceding switch, on the MIN_SEGMENT_MS boundary where the merge comparison is strictly-less-than and jitter flips the outcome; with the change the closest pair in the journey is 16 s apart and nothing approaches the 500 ms match tolerance. FLASH COLLISION: nothing here renders near-white full screen; confirm on the first take anyway.

journeys.expected_physical: Approximately 45 left clicks, the highest click count in the category, concentrated in the merge editor accept buttons, the Source Control and Explorer trees, and caret placement for the three Ctrl+Shift+K line deletions. Excludes the two JEM button clicks on DISPLAY2. Approximately 290 keypresses with an unusually high editing and modifier share: three Ctrl+Shift+K chords, three Ctrl+S, six Ctrl+W, four Alt+Tab rows, two Ctrl+Tab rows. 6 to 8 wheel scroll bursts totalling roughly 25 notches.
journeys.stresses: THE DESIGNATED SEGMENTATION ADVERSARIAL JOURNEY, and this review verified the attack against the real cue table rather than taking it on trust. Six cue words are planted in deliberately non-boundary positions - 'next' at 68 s, 'now' at 126 s, 'first' at 178 s, 'then' at 278 s, 'done' at 320 s and 'complete' at 482 s - and all six are genuine members of DEFAULT_CUES. Because _matches_cue applies a word-boundary regex against the whole utterance text rather than its opening, every one should fire a spurious boundary, and the greedy left-to-right MIN_SEGMENT_MS merge should then shadow genuine boundaries that follow within ten seconds. Meanwhile all seven real task boundaries were checked individually and carry no cue word at all. That yields a directly measurable cue false-positive rate and an over-segmentation figure on a journey where the human-meaningful segmentation is unambiguous. Secondarily it is the richest colour-versus-luma sample in the corpus: git conflict markers and the merge editor render as saturated red and green blocks at roughly constant luma, which the 64x36 grayscale proxy largely cannot see. The abort-and-redo detour reproduces an identical visual state twice, testing whether the adaptive trailing-mean trigger behaves the same on a repeat. It also carries the corpus's strongest negative-sentiment cluster - eight negative lines of twenty-seven against a genuinely frustrating task - which is the class the sentiment lane most needs and the one neg_density reacts to most. narration.line: The nightly report job fell over this morning, and the only thing in the log was a stack trace with no context around it at all.
To start, I'll reproduce it locally by running the report script by hand, because I would rather see it fail in front of me than guess.
A range error on an invalid time value, which is about as unhelpful as errors get, since it tells me nothing about which record caused it.
The trace walks through the format helper and lands on line thirty one of report dot js, so at least I have somewhere concrete to look.
Opening that file in the editor so I can read the surrounding function properly rather than squinting at a trace in the terminal.
The helper takes a raw due field straight off the task object and hands it to the date constructor without checking anything first.
There is no validation anywhere in this function, which is entirely my own fault, because I wrote it in a hurry back in June.
Moving on, I want to check what the specification actually says about invalid dates, rather than relying on what I think I remember.
The reference page for the ISO string method is where I usually begin with this kind of question, because it is precise about the throwing behaviour.
It says the method throws when the date value is not a finite number of milliseconds, which is the error I am seeing.
That confirms my reading of it, and the behaviour is documented rather than surprising, which makes me feel a lot better about the fix.
I'll follow the link across to the get time method to see what it returns for a date that could not be parsed.
Get time gives back not a number, which is the cheap check I was looking for and avoids me writing a regular expression.
Jumping down to the section further down the same page to read the exact wording on what counts as an invalid date.
Clear and unambiguous, which is more than I can say for most reference material I end up reading at this hour.
The runtime error documentation is open in my other tab, so I'll compare the two descriptions and make sure they agree with each other.
The runtime classes this as a range error the same way the language reference does, so a single guard will cover both paths.
Both sources agree with each other, so I can stop reading and go and write the actual fix.
Back to the reference tab briefly, because I want the exact method name in front of me before I leave the browser.
In the editor, I'll add a guard that parses the value and checks it before the formatter ever touches the ISO string method.
If the parsed value is not a number, the helper returns a visible placeholder instead of throwing and taking the whole report down with it.
That is a genuinely small change, and it keeps one bad row from destroying the entire nightly run, which is what should have happened originally.
Saving and running the script again to see whether the report gets all the way through to the end this time around.
It produced the full report with exactly one placeholder row in it, which is precisely the behaviour I was aiming for.
Next, I'll add a regression test so this particular bug cannot quietly come back the moment somebody refactors the helper.
The test feeds a deliberately broken due field into the formatter and asserts that the placeholder comes back out of it.
Writing the assertion the same way the other tests in this file are written, because consistency matters more than cleverness here.
The whole suite passes, including the new case, and it did not need any fiddling with the other tests to get there.
Committing the guard and the test together in one change so the history explains itself to whoever reads it in six months.
A documented failure with a test wrapped around it is a much better place to leave this than where I found it this morning.
I'll leave the editor sitting on the report file so I remember where I was when I pick this up again.

journeys.expected_physical: Approximately 40 left clicks split between Edge navigation links and the VS Code editor, excluding the two JEM button clicks on DISPLAY2. Approximately 290 keypresses dominated by two large hand-typed bursts of roughly 110 and 140 keys, with about 30 modifier or navigation rows. 9 to 10 wheel scroll bursts totalling roughly 40 notches, the heaviest scrolling in the category and almost all of it inside msedge.exe.
journeys.stresses: THE DESIGNATED SATURATION CONTROL, and the only browser-inclusive journey in the category. Narration runs roughly 744 words over a nominal 13 minute take, about 57 words per minute, comfortably above the 40.5 words per minute at which PER_MINUTE_SCALE of 2.47 drives the spoken_word lane past 100 and clamps it. Without one deliberately saturated example there is no way to demonstrate that the lane saturates rather than merely reads high, and the other six journeys sit between 12 and 36 words per minute to give the unsaturated comparison. It is also the corpus's Edge-enrichment probe, exercising three structurally distinct JEM identity paths: a foreground change into Edge at 135 s, a full sidebar navigation changing both URL and title at 232 s, and two Ctrl+Tab switches at 310 and 370 s that change only the title on the same hwnd through the NAMECHANGE coalescer with its measured 220 to 300 ms lag. That lag is a systematic offset a vision detector will appear to fire early against, it consumes roughly half the 500 ms jem_eval match tolerance on its own, and this journey is where it should be quantified so it can be subtracted rather than blamed. The in-page anchor jump at 272 s is a second, structurally different candidate JEM-blind case. Finally it is the densest sentiment sample in the category with 31 labelled lines across all three declared classes, including fourteen deliberately flat procedural lines for the neutral false-positive rate, which the measurement-gaps brief identifies as the single highest-value defect in the shipped score. Lane arithmetic at a nominal 13.0 minute take: context_switch 18 = 1.38/min * 36.75 = 51; spoken_word PINNED AT 100; neg_density 3 of 31 by duration = roughly 25; time_segment 43. Holdout split.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: Edge is the largest privacy surface in this category and JEM's video captures everything visible. It must run on a clean profile with no signed-in account, no favourites bar, no history dropdown opened, and exactly two tabs. Both target sites are public reference documentation requiring no login; nothing is submitted, nothing is downloaded, no credentials or personal data are entered anywhere. Mic live throughout. FLASH COLLISION IS THE TOP RISK IN THE WHOLE CATEGORY: a light-mode documentation page maximised approaches the 245 mean-luma threshold, jem_eval requires the detected bright-run count to equal exactly len(sync.flashes)+1, and a mismatch aborts the evaluation rather than degrading it. The dark-mode verification in setup is a gate, and the flash detector must be run on the first take before any further recording. REPRODUCIBILITY: MDN and the Node docs are maintained sites whose structure can change between takes. The narration deliberately never quotes page text verbatim and never names a section heading, only paraphrases, so a layout change costs a click target rather than the WER reference - but re-verify both pages before any re-record weeks later. Edge's UIA address-bar scrape is documented as brittle across Edge updates, so a browser update between takes can silently downgrade detail from uia:<url> to uia:<tab title>; record the Edge version in the take log. GROUND TRUTH: if the zero-width space is still present in Edge window titles on this machine, every Edge identity flows through the UIA workspace-recheck path at 750 ms cadence, which adds jitter to the two Ctrl+Tab timestamps - check the first take's CSV before treating any Edge timing error as a JAMS detector fault. The 272 s anchor click is explicitly UNRESOLVED as to whether JEM sees it, and the review's instruction is to classify it from take one's CSV rather than pre-declaring it blind, which is what the proposal did. COUNT CORRECTION: the proposal said 17 switches; the enumeration gives 18 because the final Alt+Tab at 675 s is followed by a Ctrl+P that changes the title. SWITCH SPACING: the 70 s and 512 s and 675 s beats each pair a foreground change with a title change a second or two later; pause deliberately between the two so they stay above the 500 ms match tolerance, and read the real spacing off take one.

journeys.title: Long production build with genuine dead time
journeys.setup: Run Standard Pre-Flight P1-P9 from category_notes. Deltas: (a) THE BUILD TARGET WAS CHANGED BY THIS REVIEW. The proposal built D:\git\jams\apps\web, which puts the product's own route names, source paths and any missing-environment-variable warnings on camera in a file that is then uploaded to the JAMS website for processing. Instead, build D:\jem-journeys\bigbuild, a generated Next.js fixture created once by the bootstrap script with enough static routes that a cold `npm run build` takes roughly eleven minutes on this machine; the bootstrap tunes the route count to hit that target and records the tuned count and the measured duration in the fixture README. Nothing proprietary appears on screen. (b) Run D:\jem-journeys\reset.ps1 for the taskboard fixture, which VS Code opens - VS Code must be on the taskboard fixture and NOT on any product repo; this is a privacy control, not a convenience. (c) Delete D:\jem-journeys\bigbuild\.next before every take so the build is never incremental. (d) `wt --title build -d D:\jem-journeys\bigbuild pwsh -NoLogo ; new-tab --title notes -d D:\jem-journeys\taskboard pwsh -NoLogo`, select the build tab. (f) Before recording, confirm the JAMS ingest file-size limit accepts a take of this length at 30 fps and CRF 23 at the DISPLAY1 resolution; measure the dry-run file size and check it against the limit. (g) The step timestamps below are NOMINAL. The operator follows the action order and the build's own milestones, not a clock; the narration card is keyed to milestones. CRITICAL: record DISPLAY1 only, single unpaused take - a long take with no pause is the whole point - and clap inside both flashes.

journeys.expected_physical: Approximately 4 left clicks - the fewest in the category, essentially one Explorer selection plus terminal focus - excluding the two JEM button clicks on DISPLAY2. Approximately 200 keypresses, of which roughly 90 are one continuous prose burst into a markdown file and the rest are short shell commands. 4 wheel scroll bursts totalling roughly 24 notches, all in WindowsTerminal.exe. Approximately 430 seconds of the take, over 43 percent of it, contains zero input events of any kind.
journeys.stresses: THE EVALUATOR CANARY AND THE DEAD-TIME REFERENCE. Three uninterrupted hands-off dwells of 135, 145 and 150 seconds make this the corpus's primary test of the evaluation-matrix rule that silence is reported as measured-and-empty rather than as zero effort: any lane that reads 0 here must be distinguishable in the report from a lane that was never run. It is also the only take long enough to stress jem_eval's subprocess caps - a seventeen minute 30 fps take is roughly 30,000 frames through the scale=64:36,format=gray flash decode under a 120 s cap and through the CFR re-encode under a 300 s cap - which is why it is recorded first and evaluated before anything else in the campaign. Because it is the longest take it also gives the most sensitive audio-to-video drift measurement, and the largest ingest file. Every scored lane sits at its corpus floor here, which is the point: context_switch 11 switches = 0.66/min * 36.75 = 24; spoken_word roughly 240 words = 14 wpm * 2.47 = 36; time_segment 17 minutes = 57, the only journey where the time lane dominates the weighted score. neg_density is the interesting one: with only 16 utterances, three negative lines produce a duration share of roughly 0.20 and a lane value near 50, and a single additional negative utterance moves the lane by roughly 15 points - so this journey is the corpus's low-utterance-count instability probe for the sentiment lane, demonstrating that neg_density is computed over narration duration only and is therefore completely unaffected by the 430 seconds of silence that dilute every per-minute lane. That divergence between a duration-weighted lane and a per-video-minute lane is the single most important scoring behaviour this journey exposes. Holdout split.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: the review changed the build target away from the product repo precisely because the original would have put proprietary route names, source paths and possible environment-variable warnings on camera and then uploaded that video for processing. As rewritten the journey touches only generated fixtures under D:\jem-journeys, VS Code is pinned to the taskboard fixture, and no account, credential or network service is involved beyond the local build. Mic live throughout. REPRODUCIBILITY: build duration varies with machine load, so the dwell timestamps are nominal and the operator follows build milestones; delete .next before each take; the fixture's route count is tuned once and recorded so a re-generated fixture can be checked against it. INGEST: this is the largest file the campaign produces - measure it on the dry run and confirm it is under the JAMS upload limit BEFORE recording, because discovering the cap after a seventeen minute take wastes the most expensive take in the corpus. TIMESTAMP INTEGRITY: ddagrab capturing a near-static screen for 135 seconds is the most likely place in the campaign for dropped or duplicated frames and for a variable frame rate to appear. Run ffprobe on the dry run, confirm what the probe provider's VFR to CFR normalization does to the timeline, and confirm the flash-derived offsets still map active time to video time correctly at the far end of the take - if normalization shifts timestamps here it invalidates every point match in the take, not just the long dwells. GROUND TRUTH: the route table appearing at roughly 800 s is a large genuine visual change with no JEM event behind it and must be labelled as a JEM-blind sample. SENTIMENT: with only 16 utterances the neg_density lane is unstable by construction; report it with the utterance count beside it rather than as a bare number.

journeys.expected_physical: Approximately 5 left clicks, excluding the two JEM button clicks on DISPLAY2. Approximately 200 keypresses, of which roughly 25 are modifier or editing rows (five Ctrl+P, two Ctrl+S, four Alt+Tab, one Backspace). 2 wheel scroll bursts totalling roughly 6 notches. The highest event density per minute in the category by a wide margin.
journeys.stresses: THE DOUBLE SATURATION-AND-FLOOR PROBE, and the shortest journey in the category, added by this review because the proposal contained nothing under seven minutes despite the brief asking for three to twenty. Three things are measured here that nothing else in the corpus isolates. First, CONTEXT_SWITCH SATURATION: 13 switches in a 3.9 minute take is 3.36 per minute, and PER_MINUTE_SCALE of 36.75 drives that to 124 before clamping, so this lane is PINNED AT 100. Together with dev-terminal-04's pinned spoken_word lane and dev-terminal-05's floor on every lane, the corpus now brackets both ends of two independent lanes, which is the minimum needed to show that the normalizers saturate rather than merely read high. Second, THE NEUTRAL-LINE POLARITY PROBE: the declared negative count here is exactly zero, so the true neg_density is exactly zero by construction. Because the shipped sentiment provider is Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX emitting positive_probability_minus_negative_probability, it is binary and confidently bimodal with no neutral output, and the neg_density threshold of -0.15 is far inside that bimodality - which means every declared-neutral line here lands at nearly full magnitude on one side or the other. Any neg_density above zero measured on this journey is therefore entirely model error on neutral lines, with no true-negative signal to confound it. With seven neutral lines, each misfire moves the lane by roughly 25 points. This is the cleanest available estimate of the largest error source in the shipped score and it did not exist in the proposed set. Third, SHORT-TAKE BEHAVIOUR: at 3.9 minutes the time_segment lane reads 13, four boundaries must be found in 234 seconds against a 10 second minimum segment, and four switch pairs are deliberately spaced 6 seconds apart - inside MIN_SEGMENT_MS so the greedy merge must shadow them, but well outside the 500 ms match tolerance so each remains individually attributable. Exactly one cue is planted, 'finally' at 192 s, at the genuine final boundary. Lane arithmetic: context_switch PINNED AT 100; spoken_word roughly 140 words = 36 wpm * 2.47 = 89; neg_density 0 by construction; time_segment 13. Holdout split.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: entirely local, no network, no accounts, no credentials, fixture identity only in git output. Mic live throughout. REPRODUCIBILITY: the hotfix patch must be reapplied between takes or the test already passes; the constant on line 9 and the failing test name are both spoken aloud so a fixture edit that moves them invalidates the WER reference; VS Code must open with no editors. PACE: this journey is deliberately brisk and a slow take destroys its purpose - if the take runs longer than about 4.5 minutes the switch rate drops below the 2.72 per minute pin threshold and the saturation probe is lost, so check the duration immediately after the take and re-record if it overran. GROUND TRUTH: four of the thirteen switches are dirty-dot or Ctrl+P title flips with little or no visual change and must be annotated in the same instrumentation class used in dev-terminal-02. The 6 second switch pairs at 34/40, 102/108, 134/140 and 166/172 are deliberate and must not be treated as timing errors. SENTIMENT: the zero-negative construction is load-bearing - do not let an operator ad-lib a frustrated aside during this take, because a single unscripted negative line destroys the probe. If one occurs, mark the take and re-record. FLASH COLLISION: nothing near-white; verify on the first take.
