narration.line: The pipeline went red overnight on a test that passes locally every single time.
I can reproduce it with the simulator, which at least gives me a fixed seed to work from.
It failed again, and it is the same timeout assertion that failed in the pipeline.
The tail of the log has the timing numbers I actually need.
Hopping between the tabs to get the run, the log and the repo side by side in my head.
The gap between the slowest pass and the failure is about forty milliseconds, which is nothing.
Moving on, I want to read the simulator and the test rather than guess at the timing.
The simulator adds a random delay inside a window that overlaps the test timeout.
So the test is not flaky. The timeout is just set too tight for the work it waits on.
Raising the timeout to two seconds gives the slow path room without hiding a real regression.
Saved, and I will run the same seed again to confirm the theory holds.
Watching it run, and it is already past the point it failed at last time.
I had to step away for a few minutes, and the run finished while I was gone.
It passed on the seed that was failing, which is the best news I have had all morning.
Checking the machine is not thrashing, because a loaded box would explain the whole thing on its own.
Running a different seed as well, because one green run proves almost nothing.
Going back to leave a comment, since the number on its own will confuse whoever reads this later.
Writing down why two seconds and not five, so nobody quietly doubles it again in six months.
Committing the timeout and the comment together.
The history reads cleanly, and the second seed came back green as well.
That is a genuinely fixed flaky test rather than a retry bolted on top of it.

journeys.expected_physical: Approximately 8 left clicks, excluding the three JEM button clicks on DISPLAY2 (Start, Pause, Resume and Save are four presses across two visits). Approximately 380 keypresses, with an unusually high navigation and tab-switching share: six Ctrl+Tab rows, seven Alt+Tab rows, two Ctrl+P, two Ctrl+S, one Ctrl+Shift+Esc, one Alt+F4, twelve editing keypresses. 5 wheel scroll bursts totalling roughly 32 notches, all in WindowsTerminal.exe and Code.exe. Note that the 24 expected switches include six from the two deliberate rapid bursts, which JEM's own coalescing may reduce - the authoritative count for those six is whatever take one's CSV records.
journeys.stresses: THE ONLY MULTI-SEGMENT JOURNEY IN THE CATEGORY, added by this review to close what is the largest single hole in the proposed set: every proposed journey specified a single unpaused take, so JEM's per-segment sync flashes and jem_eval's per-segment active-time to video-time offset mapping were never exercised at all, despite being the mechanism the whole alignment depends on. Here JEM is paused once for a genuine two to three minute break, producing two entries in sync.flashes plus the end flash, three bright runs total, and an active-time timeline that diverges from wall clock by the length of the break. If the offset mapping is wrong, every point match after 460 s is wrong, and this is the only take that will reveal it. Second, it is the only journey with deliberate SUB-TOLERANCE SWITCH CLUSTERS: three tab-title switches roughly 0.7 s apart at 130 s and three foreground switches roughly 0.8 s apart at 610 s, both below the 1.5 s that a 500 ms point matcher needs to attribute events individually, giving a direct measurement of how the matcher and PySceneDetect each degrade when events arrive faster than the instrumentation can separate them. Third, the 90 second FULLY SILENT BLOCK from 270 to 360 s is the corpus's only window with real visual and input activity and no speech whatsoever: no utterance, spoken_word or sentiment measures exist there while scroll spans and dwells do, which is the direct complement to dev-terminal-05's silence-with-no-activity case, and together they let the report distinguish 'the speaker was quiet' from 'the provider did not run'. It also demonstrates concretely that neg_density, being weighted by narration duration, is unaffected by the silent block while every per-video-minute lane is diluted by it. Fourth, the Task Manager beat at 500 s is one labelled sample of JEM's documented elevated and protected app enrichment limit, obtained deliberately without a UAC prompt. Lane arithmetic at a nominal 13.8 minutes of active time: context_switch 24 = 1.74/min * 36.75 = 64; spoken_word roughly 310 words = 22 wpm * 2.47 = 55; neg_density 3 of 21 by duration = roughly 38; time_segment 46. Two cues are planted, 'moving on' at 180 s and 'finished' at 476 s, both at genuine boundaries, the second of them at the interruption boundary. Holdout split.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: entirely local, no network, no accounts, no credentials, fixture identity only in git output. Task Manager's process list appears on camera, which is why pre-flight requires closing every process not part of the journey; review the Task Manager frames before uploading. Mic live throughout, including across the pause - the operator must not take a phone call or talk to anyone during the break, because the WAV keeps recording, and any speech during the break lands inside the excised window but would still be on disk in the raw WAV. If anything is said during the break, discard the raw WAV and re-record. THIS IS THE MOST FRAGILE JOURNEY IN THE CATEGORY AND IS RECORDED LAST BY DESIGN. The audio excision at M7 is the single most likely thing to go wrong: if the excised mux fails the closing-clap drift check, treat it as a known limitation of the multi-segment path and report it as such rather than as a JAMS defect, and fall back to scoring this take on the JEM side only. TIMESTAMP INTEGRITY: verify that JEM produces ONE continuous MP4 across pause and resume and that video time equals the concatenation of active segments; if it produces two files or if video time includes the paused interval, the whole M7 protocol changes and this journey must be re-specified before recording. COUNT AMBIGUITY IS DELIBERATE: the two rapid bursts are expected to produce fewer CSV rows than presses performed because of JEM's own coalescing, so expected_context_switches of 24 is an upper bound and take one's CSV is authoritative - this is the one place in the corpus where the ground truth is read off the instrument rather than declared in advance, and that must be stated in the report rather than quietly reconciled. GROUND TRUTH: four dirty-dot switches must be annotated in the usual instrumentation class. FLASH COLLISION: three bright runs are expected here rather than two, and jem_eval aborts if it finds any other number, so the flash detector must be run on this take before anything else is done with it. A brief white frame during the Task Manager open or the Alt+F4 close would break the count - check frames around 500 s and 535 s specifically.

journeys.expected_physical: ~7 clicks; ~160 keypresses (about 21 typed characters in the fixture field, ~47 and ~82 in the two shell commands, plus Ctrl+A, three Win+N pairs and two Enters); 3 scroll spans totalling ~16 wheel notches. Narration is 11 lines, ~118 words over 3.3 min = ~36 words/min of speech across the whole take, deliberately just BELOW the 40.5 wpm spoken_word saturation knee. Switch rate 2.4/min, just below the 2.72/min cognitive knee. Of the 8 truth switches, 1 is proxy-only by construction (the Win+1 focus grab at t=6) and 7 carry a real visual delta.
journeys.stresses: The small-n denominator problem, made explicit and unavoidable. With 8 truth switches a single miss moves recall by 0.125 and the Wilson 95% interval on recall 0.875 is roughly [0.53, 0.98]; this journey exists to PROVE that per-journey F1 at three minutes is statistically meaningless and must be pooled across the corpus before any claim is made. Secondary targets: (a) transcription fixed-cost overhead versus audio length, where model load and VAD setup dominate a ~198 s decode, the worst case for the RTF gate; (b) segmentation with ZERO audio cue words anywhere in the script (checked against the real cue vocabulary, which includes bare 'next', 'now', 'then', 'first', 'done' and 'complete', not just the headline phrases), forcing the scene-boundary-only path: the greedy 10 s merge over 7 visually-real switches should leave roughly 7 machine segments against 4 human ones; (c) two dark-on-dark app transitions and one editor-tab title change, the exact class the 9.6 candidate floor discards; (d) the proxy-only focus-grab switch at t=6, a truth event with no pixels attached, which is the cleanest single demonstration in the corpus of why proxy labels must be reported as a separate stratum. It is also the cheapest re-record in the corpus and the only journey that touches no live web page, so it is the corpus floor for duration AND the control for page-drift.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: VS Code must be opened on C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch only, never on D:\git\jams, which contains .env files and deployment secrets that the video would capture verbatim. Run Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing and Clear-Host before Start, or earlier commands (possibly containing tokens or paths) are on screen. Do Not Disturb must be on: a single Teams or mail toast is both a privacy leak and a spurious high-delta event. No real credentials anywhere; the fixture creates no account, order or payment and sends nothing over the network. The microphone WAV records the room, so record alone and keep the WAV out of Git alongside the other raw JEM outputs.
REPRODUCIBILITY: use Win+1 / Win+2 / Win+3 for every app switch, never Alt+Tab. journeys.stresses: Deliberate DOUBLE saturation inside the shortest practical take: at 4.3 switches/min the cognitive lane pins at 100 and at 68 wpm the spoken_word lane pins at 100, so the effort score collapses to a constant plus the sentiment term and becomes a pure function of the sentiment classifier. Paired against duration-extremes-05 (the low anchor) this is the corpus's direct measurement of whether the scoring lanes have ANY dynamic range; if the two do not separate, that is a headline finding independent of any detector. Second purpose: 15 fair-spacing truth switches in 4.2 minutes make this the cheapest source of matched-timing statistics per minute of recording in the corpus, and the cleanest place to measure p95 absolute timing error and to separate JEM's ~230 ms NAMECHANGE quiet-period lag from the JAMS proxy-grid lag. Third: one explicitly pre-labelled sub-2-second pair probes the min_gap_seconds=2.0 structural floor without contaminating the fair-spacing recall figure. Fourth: the script contains no segmentation cue word from the real cue vocabulary, so every boundary must come from the scene-boundary path, and the greedy 10 s merge over 15 detectable switches should collapse to far fewer machine segments than the 6 human ones, giving the largest machine/human segment divergence in the category. It is distinct from duration-extremes-01 on every axis that matters: four apps instead of three, live documentation pages instead of fixture-only, the checkout path instead of the onboarding path, above both knees instead of below both, and one deliberately unfair switch pair instead of uniformly fair spacing.

Narration is 36 lines, ~440 words over 17.4 min = ~25 words/min, comfortably BELOW the 40.5 wpm knee. Switch rate 2.41/min, below the 2.72/min knee. Both primary scoring lanes therefore stay in their linear range for the whole take. Of the 42 truth switches, 1 is proxy-only (the Win+1 focus grab at t=8) and 41 carry a visual delta.
journeys.stresses: The primary long-duration stress case, and the only journey in the category that keeps BOTH scoring lanes off their ceilings for seventeen minutes, so the effort score remains a live function of detector quality rather than a constant. Specific targets: (a) sync drift, which jem_eval measures at the end flash and then does NOT correct, applying a single constant offset from the start flash instead; over ~1045 s even the modest drift rate measured on this rig's pre-flight take eats a visible fraction of the 500 ms match tolerance late in the take, and this is the evidence needed to justify a two-anchor linear rate fit in map_active_ms (capture.audio_align already solves exactly this problem for the audio timeline, which is the precedent). Report the measured ppm rather than assuming one. (b) Whisper real-time factor on 17.4 minutes of narration on the 2-vCPU worker, where cpu_threads collapses to 2 and the benchmarked RTF degrades: the RTF gate's worst case. (c) jem_eval's own subprocess ceilings, the 300 s CFR re-encode and the 120 s full-decode-to-64x36 flash scan, both sized for 90-second calibration clips and the most likely cause of a total evaluation failure on this file. (d) Worker memory: thousands of proxy frames through PySceneDetect plus a large raw grayscale buffer held in one subprocess stdout. (e) Segmentation cue stratification inside a single take, scored against the REAL cue vocabulary: five announced boundaries using 'okay next' and 'moving on' at genuine round transitions, one unannounced boundary at round 5, and one deliberate mid-task trap at 380 s where 'complete' should fire a spurious done-boundary and give a direct cue false-positive measurement. It also yields 42 truth switches and ~440 reference words from one recording, the best events-per-minute-of-effort ratio in the category.
journeys.risks:
HARD DURATION RISK: probe.py raises a TERMINAL, non-retryable too_long PipelineError above 20:00, and a run that trips it is poisoned rather than retried. The script targets ~17:25; the Save press must follow the closing line within about five seconds, and any take whose mp4 exceeds 17:50 should be re-recorded rather than uploaded. Note that the muxed upload must be built with the video duration passed to the mux step, so a longer narration WAV cannot extend the file past the cap.
PRE-FLIGHT REQUIRED: do not record until a throwaway 17-minute capture has been pushed through jem_eval's CFR normalisation and flash detection to confirm neither the 300 s nor the 120 s subprocess timeout fires. At full desktop resolution both are likely to blow, which is the main argument for setting capture.scale to 0.5 for the whole corpus before any journey is recorded, and never changing it afterwards.
STORAGE: a 17.4-minute capture at full resolution can approach 2 GB, and the preview org cap is 10 GiB with declared bytes reserved even on failed uploads; two long journeys plus re-runs can exhaust it.
PRIVACY: seven public documentation tabs, no login anywhere, no personal data typed; the note lines are synthetic technical sentences. VS Code must stay on C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch, because seventeen minutes of concentration is long enough to drift into opening a real repo out of habit and D:\git\jams contains .env files. The round card must live on the non-recorded monitor or on paper.
REPRODUCIBILITY: seven live documentation pages can change between takes and the sidebar link targets can move; record which link was actually taken each round. Seventeen minutes makes a skipped beat likely, so log any deviation against the events.csv timestamps rather than pretending the script was followed exactly. Use Win+N for every app switch.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: one pause makes the session unscorable outright; one near-white full-screen frame does the same, and with this many navigations a brief flash of unstyled content on MDN or Python docs is a real if low phantom-flash risk, so verify the detected bright-run count is exactly 2 before accepting the take. Stay silent across both tones.

journeys.expected_physical: ~3 clicks (deliberately almost none: one header link, two editor tabs), ~180 keypresses (about 150 in the single typed note, plus 12 Page Down, Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End, 2 Ctrl+Tab, 2 Win+N pairs and Ctrl+S), and the heavy lane: ~36 scroll spans totalling ~230 wheel notches. Narration is 24 lines, ~300 words over 17.1 min = ~17.5 words/min, well BELOW the 40.5 wpm knee. Switch rate 0.53/min, far below the 2.72/min knee. Roughly 26 still dwells totalling about 8 minutes of literally zero input.
journeys.stresses: The scroll-truth workhorse and the sparse-cognition long take, with four distinct purposes. (a) It is the only journey in the category built to ground-truth physical.scrolls, the one physical provider that works from video alone (it reads the shared proxy-motion artifact, not audio) and that the current jem_eval does not score at all: ~36 JEM wheel spans over a fixed-line-height 4000-line local document give unambiguous span-IoU and notch-count truth, which is precisely the labelled data the recorded next-hillclimb target asks for. (b) It separates the two adversarial visual classes the context_switch post-filter conflates: smooth wheel translation, which should be suppressed, versus instantaneous viewport replacement from Ctrl+End, Ctrl+Home and Page Down, which is not translation-like, will not be suppressed, and should surface as JAMS-only detections that JEM structurally cannot see. All of these are pre-declared beats, so the resulting events go into a separate visual-change stratum rather than being silently counted as false positives against proxy labels, which is exactly the label-noise asymmetry the evaluation rules warn about. (c) It holds both scoring lanes low for seventeen minutes, making it the long-duration low-effort anchor and a direct test of whether the score has range. (d) Roughly 26 long still dwells give about eight minutes of unambiguous zero-event exposure: any detection inside a dwell is a false positive with no labelling judgement required, which is the cleanest false-positives-per-minute denominator available at length. It is distinct from duration-extremes-03 on purpose: same duration band, opposite density, two apps instead of three, scroll-dominated instead of switch-dominated, and adversarial-by-design instead of steady-state.
journeys.risks:
DURATION: the same terminal 20:00 probe cap as duration-extremes-03; target ~17:07 and re-record anything over 17:50. Same mandatory long-take pre-flight on the jem_eval 300 s CFR and 120 s flash-scan subprocess timeouts.
PRIVACY: longdoc.md is generated synthetic text with no personal content; MDN is public and requires no login; the four typed note lines are technical statements. No credentials appear at any point. VS Code must remain on C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch.
REPRODUCIBILITY: this journey's value depends entirely on scroll discipline. Inconsistent sweep speed or fidgeting during a dwell corrupts both the scroll span boundaries and the dwell precision test. The mouse wheel notch size must not change mid-corpus: do not adjust the Windows 'lines to scroll' setting between takes, and note that a free-spinning or high-resolution wheel emits different notch counts than a detented one, so the same mouse must be used for every take. MDN pages are live and their length can change between takes, shifting scroll extents; the VS Code phases are fully deterministic and should be treated as the primary scroll evidence, with the browser phases as the realistic-conditions secondary.
ALIGNMENT: with only about three clicks, the audio alignment's event-based offset refinement has to lean on keypress transients. The typed note at 790 s and the twelve evenly-spread Page Down presses are the two clusters that make this work; if either is skipped, the take falls back to tone-only alignment and that must be recorded in the take log rather than assumed away.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: a pause makes the session unscorable; a near-white frame does the same, and MDN in light mode would be exactly that, so confirm the dark toggle survived the browser restart. Long dwells make it tempting to check a phone or talk to someone: any off-script speech lands in the transcript and corrupts both the WER reference and the sentiment label set. Stay silent across both tones and do not clap.

journeys.title: Mostly waiting: the sparse-activity dwell journey
journeys.setup:
STANDARD RIG. Journey-specific:
(1) Create the deterministic wait script once, before the corpus, at C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch\fake-build.ps1 with exactly this content:
    1..15 | ForEach-Object {
        '[{0:00}/15] compiling synthetic module {0} ...' -f $_
        Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
    } | Tee-Object -FilePath build.log
    'build exited with code 0' | Tee-Object -FilePath build.log -Append
Run it once with the recorder off and confirm a line appears every 10 seconds and the whole thing takes 150 seconds. Determinism is the point: no network, no dependency resolution, identical on every take.
(2) Windows Terminal (Win+3), jem-shell, cwd C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch, history suppressed, cleared. This is the journey's first foreground app, which also makes it the only journey in the category whose truth set does not open on msedge.exe.
(3) VS Code (Win+2) on C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch with longdoc.md open and ACTIVE and notes.md (freshly emptied) in a second tab.
(4) Edge (Win+1) maximised, one tab, MDN HTTP Caching guide, dark, scrolled to the top.
(5) JEM Scenario 'duration-extremes-05'. Mic recorder, 3 s silence, Start, silent and still until t=10.

WAIT DISCIPLINE: during the three 150-second waits, hands come completely off the keyboard and mouse. No fidgeting, no cursor wiggling, no checking a phone, no talking to anyone. The stillness IS the measurement, and off-script speech destroys both the transcript reference and the sentiment labels.

journeys.expected_physical: ~1 click (the single editor-tab click at 350 s), ~185 keypresses (~18 + ~32 shell characters, ~124 typed note characters, three Win+N pairs, two Ctrl+S and Enters), 1 scroll span of 6 notches. Roughly 460 of the 665 seconds carry literally zero input events. Narration is 14 lines, ~170 words over 11.2 min = ~15 words/min, the lowest in the category and the corpus floor. Switch rate 0.54/min. Of the 6 truth switches, 1 is proxy-only (the Win+3 focus grab at t=10).
journeys.stresses: The deliberate LOW ANCHOR for the effort score, and the corpus's only genuine test of whether JAMS can represent waiting. Predicted lanes: cognitive 0.54 x 36.75 = 20, spoken_word 15 x 2.47 = 37, time 11.2/30 x 100 = 37, sentiment driven by 3 negative lines out of 14; predicted total in the high twenties against duration-extremes-02's predicted low sixties. If those two journeys do NOT separate, the scoring lane has no dynamic range, and that is a headline finding independent of any detector. Second target: three 150-second dwells on three different surfaces (a terminal with slow low-amplitude appends, a frozen editor, a frozen web page) give 450 seconds of unambiguous zero-event exposure, the cleanest false-positives-per-minute denominator in the whole corpus and one that needs no human labelling to interpret. Third: the 150-second slow-append phase is a genuinely hard intermediate case, real activity whose per-frame grayscale delta sits far below the 9.6 candidate floor, and it probes the documented dark-theme low-delta failure class without the confound of an application switch. Fourth: it is the only journey designed around the evaluation rule that missing data must be reported as missing rather than scored as zero effort, because waiting for a build is real cognitive load that every provider in the pipeline is structurally blind to. It is also the only journey whose truth set opens on WindowsTerminal.exe rather than msedge.exe, and the only one with a deterministic locally-generated timing source, which makes it the corpus's re-recordable mid-length control.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: fake-build.ps1 is synthetic and touches no real project, no network and no credentials; build.log contains only its own generated lines. MDN is public with no login. The three long waits are the highest-risk moments for accidental exposure: a Teams or mail toast arriving during 150 seconds of stillness is both a privacy leak and a large spurious delta event, so Do Not Disturb is not optional here. Record alone, because the microphone is running for the whole take and a passing conversation lands in the transcript.
REPRODUCIBILITY: the script's 150-second runtime is deterministic, but Start-Sleep is not a real-time guarantee, so verify the actual elapsed time from the events.csv and build.log timestamps rather than assuming exactly 150 s on every take. Run the script once before recording to confirm PowerShell streams a line every 10 s through Tee-Object rather than buffering. build.log must be deleted between takes, or the Tee-Object append makes the tail read at 565 s differ from take to take. notes.md must be emptied before every take. Use Win+N for every app switch, never Alt+Tab, and never press Win+N for the app that is already foreground.
ALIGNMENT: with one click in the whole take, the event-based offset refinement depends almost entirely on the keypress bursts at 356 s and 600 s; if either is skipped the take falls back to tone-only alignment and that must be recorded.
GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: any JEM pause makes the session unscorable; a near-white full-screen frame adds a phantom bright run and makes jem_eval raise 'sync alignment ambiguous'. Stay silent across both tones and do not clap: a broadband transient over the 1 kHz tone can drop the Goertzel dominance below 0.35, and losing an anchor makes every audio-dependent measure in this take unusable. Boredom is the real enemy of this journey: the temptation to wiggle the mouse or glance at a phone during 150 seconds of stillness is exactly what destroys the zero-event denominator that gives the take its value. Accept the take only after verifying exactly 2 bright runs, a non-null end_flash_log_ms, 6 non-recorder context_switch rows, and a successful align.

journeys.expected_physical: 12 truth context spans (possibly 13 if the double Ctrl+Tab at t=226 survives NAMECHANGE coalescing as two spans; record whichever actually occurred). Roughly 9 clicks, roughly 300 keypresses, 6 scroll spans totalling 28 wheel notches. Narration is 210 words over 450 s = 28.0 words/min, below the 40.5 wpm knee. Switch rate 1.60/min, below the 2.72/min knee. Negative narration share 0.457, above the 0.40 knee. Predicted lanes: context_switch 59, sentiment 100 (pinned), spoken_word 69, time 25; predicted total 70, the highest in the category.
journeys.stresses: Three jobs no other journey in this category does. (a) It is the sentiment HIGH anchor. The default weight profile gives sentiment a weight of 4 against context_switch 3, spoken_word 1 and time_segment 2, making it the heaviest lane, and this is the only journey that drives it to its ceiling. Paired against duration-extremes-05 (share 0.075, lane 19, total 25) it isolates the sentiment lane's contribution from every other lane, and together the pair demonstrates the category's real headline: the corpus spread of 25 to 70 is driven mostly by narration sentiment and only weakly by duration or activity, which is a finding about the scoring model rather than about any detector. Because the production sentiment provider is Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX with no neutral class (id2label is NEGATIVE and POSITIVE only, and value is positive minus negative probability), the heaviest lane in the product is decided by a binary classifier forced to take a side on ten neutral factual sentences; this journey is where that shows up largest and is the strongest argument for the VADER variant comparison. (b) It fills the four-to-eleven-minute duration gap the original set left empty, giving the time lane a mid point (25) between duration-extremes-02's 14 and duration-extremes-05's 37 so the lane can be checked for linearity across six points rather than a barbell. (c) LOOP REPEATABILITY: beats 24 to 172 and 240 to 390 are the same sequence performed twice inside ONE take, on the same machine, in the same lighting, with the same window geometry. Comparing the detector's output on the two loops gives a within-take variance estimate with every between-take confound removed, which is something no amount of re-recording can provide and which the corpus otherwise lacks entirely. It also gives six VISUAL_ONLY fixture beats including two navy-to-orange transitions, the fixture's error-recovery path, which no other journey exercises.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: the fixture is local, synthetic, creates no account, order or payment and sends nothing over the network; the uploads folder is one Chris creates and it stays empty; MDN and docs.python.org are public with no login. The typed note lines are synthetic statements about the fixture. No credentials appear at any point. VS Code must stay on C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch. TRUTHFULNESS OF THE SENTIMENT LABELS: seven of seventeen lines are labelled negative, which is only defensible because the task genuinely fails twice and leaves the folder empty both times. Do not perform frustration that the task does not produce; if the fixture behaves differently on the day, relabel the affected lines before upload and record that the labels were revised BEFORE any score was seen, never after. REPRODUCIBILITY: the two loops must be performed as identically as possible for the within-take comparison to mean anything, so rehearse the loop once before Start; if the second loop visibly diverges, note the divergence from events.csv rather than discarding it. The double Ctrl+Tab at t=226 is the one beat whose truth count is genuinely uncertain because of the 200 ms NAMECHANGE quiet period, so it is pre-labelled as a coalescing observation and must be excluded from the fair-spacing recall figure whichever way it lands. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: standard gates apply, namely exactly two detected bright runs, no pause, one monitor, JEM's own window never on the recorded monitor, and a non-null end_flash_log_ms.

narration.line: Okay, let's get started. I have a small summary script that turns a rows file into a printable list.
Let me run it and see what comes out.
And it blew up immediately. That is a great start.
Cannot read properties of undefined, reading toUpperCase.
Right, I will pull the source up, because that message on its own is useless to me.
Line five maps over the rows and calls toUpperCase on the sku.
So it assumes every single record actually has a sku.
Okay, next, let me check the data file.
There it is. The third record has a quantity and no sku at all.
Honestly, I am glad it failed loudly instead of silently.
Let me check how optional chaining handles a missing property.
Pulling up the MDN reference page.
Right, so the question mark dot just short circuits to undefined.
That should stop the crash.
Back to the editor to patch line five.
Saving, and let me try that again.
Okay, good, it does not crash anymore.
But the output says undefined times three, which is useless.
So I fixed the symptom and not the actual problem.
I need a default value, not just a safe access.
Looking up nullish coalescing, the double question mark.
That is exactly what I want. Fall back to a placeholder.
Applying it to the same line.
Wrapping the sku lookup and defaulting to unknown.
Saving and running it one more time.
And there we go. Four rows, one marked unknown, no crash.
That is genuinely satisfying after all that squinting.
Let me write the output to a file so I have a record of it.
Redirecting standard out to out dot text.
Opening the file to confirm it landed.
Clean output, all four rows, exactly what I expected.
Okay, that is it. I am happy with where this landed.

journeys.expected_physical: ~440 keypress rows across 11 bursts, dominated by two long URL types (~96 rows each, InPrivate so autocomplete cannot shorten them between takes); ~14 click rows, of which 9 are taskbar app switches and 5 are in-editor caret placements; 8 scroll rows totalling ~35 notches, split between terminal scrollback and two MDN pages. Keypress totals include modifier rows (Shift, Ctrl) and are subject to auto-repeat, so score by binned agreement, never exact match.
journeys.stresses: Context-switch provider on its two hardest classes at once: Windows Terminal dark <-> VS Code Dark+ foreground changes (low absolute grayscale delta, the documented false-negative class) and VS Code file-to-file title changes where JEM logs a switch but only the editor pane repaints. Segmentation stratum A, verified against the real DEFAULT_CUES list: exactly three cue-bearing lines ('let's get started' 5 s, 'next' 92 s, 'that is it' 576 s), each at a genuine boundary, so cue precision is a clean 3-for-3 measurement. Sentiment carries one sarcasm line (24 s, lexically positive 'great start'), one negation-as-relief line (254 s, 'does not crash'), and two neutral lines built from loaded tokens (36 s 'cannot read properties of undefined', 106 s 'no sku at all'). The three MDN scroll bursts at 175 s are a pure precision probe: large visual change, zero window change. Narration runs ~39 wpm and switches ~1.7/min, so neither the spoken_word nor the context_switch scoring lane saturates and the total effort score can still move.
journeys.risks: All data synthetic (four fabricated SKU records written by the setup script); no credentials, no accounts, no form submission, no personal data on screen. Edge runs InPrivate so nothing is written to history and autocomplete cannot vary keystroke counts between takes. MDN page content can change between takes, which is harmless because the WER reference is the narration, not the page. Requires network for the two MDN pages; if offline, substitute two local HTML copies saved during setup and adjust the URL keystroke counts. VS Code workspace trust must be pre-accepted or it injects an unscripted modal and two extra switches. The Edge tab memory-usage badge must be off. Node version changes the exact TypeError wording (cosmetic, the narration does not quote it verbatim beyond the first clause). Expect +/-1 switch around each Edge navigation depending on how many times Edge retitles during load; take the count from events.csv.

journeys.title: Thirty rows, by hand
journeys.setup:
COMMON PRE-FLIGHT as in journey 01.

JOURNEY SETUP:
$j='D:\git\temp\friction-lab\j03'; Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $j -EA SilentlyContinue; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $j | Out-Null
$rows = 1..30 | ForEach-Object { '{0},{1},{2}' -f ('SKU-{0:D4}' -f (1000+$_)), ("Widget $_"), ((($_*7) % 23) + 1) }
'sku,name,qty' | Set-Content "$j\skus-raw.csv"; $rows | Add-Content "$j\skus-raw.csv"
New-Item -ItemType File "$j\skus-fixed.txt" -Force | Out-Null
SOURCE VIEWER: Windows 11 Notepad, not Notepad++ - Notepad ships with the OS, so the journey has no third-party dependency, and it honours Windows dark mode. Close every existing Notepad tab first so exactly one tab is open on skus-raw.csv; the file is only ever read and scrolled, never edited, so no dirty-state title marker can appear. If Notepad refuses dark mode on this build, Notepad++ with the Obsidian theme is an acceptable substitute - what must NOT happen is a light-themed editor putting a near-white pane over half the screen, which risks a phantom flash detection and makes the session unscorable.
LAYOUT: Notepad on the LEFT half of the JEM-selected monitor showing skus-raw.csv, VS Code Dark+ on the RIGHT half showing skus-fixed.txt. Both fully visible, neither maximised, taskbar visible.
RULE FOR THE TAKE: no copy-paste, no multi-cursor, no find-and-replace, no snippets, no macros. Every character is typed. Target format per line, exactly: SKU-1001 | Widget 1 | qty=8
APP SWITCHING: three windows are open, so the Notepad hops are LEFT CLICKS into the Notepad window and the terminal hop is a LEFT CLICK on its taskbar button. No Alt+Tab in this take.

narration.line: Okay, let's get started. I have thirty rows to reformat by hand.
No copy paste, no multi cursor. I want to know how long this actually takes a person.
Row one. SKU one thousand and one, widget one, quantity eight.
This is fine. Four rows in, twenty six to go.
It is repetitive but it is not hard.
Scrolling the source so I can see the following block.
Eight rows in. I can feel my attention starting to slide.
The pipe separator is easy to fat finger.
Twelve rows. I have made two typos already and I caught both of them.
This is exactly the kind of work that should be a script.
Fifteen. Halfway. That is not as encouraging as I hoped.
My wrists are aching and I still have twelve rows to go.
Eighteen rows. I have stopped reading the widget numbers and I am just copying shapes.
Twenty one. I genuinely do not care what these SKUs mean anymore.
It is very quiet in here.
Twenty four rows, and I am just grinding through it.
Twenty seven. I can see the end of the file, which helps a little.
Twenty nine. Thirty. And that is it, the whole file is transposed.
Let me count the lines in the shell to make sure I did not drop one.
Thirty lines, which is exactly right.
The numbers are right and I am glad that is over.

journeys.expected_physical: ~1,150 keypress rows across 30 typed lines at ~38 rows each - overwhelmingly alphanumeric and whitespace, with a modifier tail from the three shifted letters of SKU and the two shifted pipes on every line, an editing tail from real typos, and a handful of navigation rows. ~12 click rows (8 Notepad hops, 2 taskbar switches, 2 incidental). 4 scroll rows in Notepad, 12 notches total. The richest physical ground truth in the category by an order of magnitude. Auto-repeat on held modifiers makes exact totals unstable take to take; expect roughly ten percent variance and score by binned agreement.
journeys.stresses: The only journey where BOTH scoring lanes are genuinely unsaturated: narration runs ~17 wpm against the 40.5 wpm ceiling and switches ~0.6/min against 2.72/min, so it is the one configuration in which the default weight profile's total score can actually respond to a detector change. It is also the negative control for false context switches: sixteen minutes of continuous in-editor typing with only ten real switches, testing whether proxy_motion's band-max metric over-fires on a single changing text line. Long inter-line silences of 45 to 55 s exercise Silero VAD and the 'report missing, never infer zero' rule. Sentiment is a slow gradient rather than a step - neutral at 0 to 4 min, drifting negative through 5 to 13 min, relief at the end - which tests whether a per-utterance classifier with no memory can track a trajectory. One pure-neutral line with zero affective vocabulary (725 s, 'It is very quiet in here') sits mid-way through the negative stretch as a context-contamination probe. Cue audit against the real DEFAULT_CUES list: exactly three lines fire - 'let's get started' (10 s, genuine), 'starting' (290 s, a deliberate false positive at a non-boundary) and 'that is it' (875 s, genuine).
journeys.risks: All SKU data is generated by the setup script and is entirely synthetic; nothing real or customer-derived appears on screen. The line count at 895 s is 30, not 31 - skus-fixed.txt carries no header row, only the thirty transposed lines. Both windows must sit on the JEM-selected monitor or clicks and scrolls outside it are silently dropped with no warning. At sixteen minutes this is the longest journey in the category, leaving only about two minutes of headroom under the eighteen-minute muxed cap, so stop promptly. Genuine typos are ground truth and must NOT trigger a re-record. Notepad must be dark-themed and must have exactly one tab open. Typing fatigue means take-to-take keypress totals vary; the metric must be binned-count agreement, never exact match.

Three false summits produce three positive-to-negative transitions inside twelve minutes, the strongest available test of whether sentiment tracks a trajectory or collapses to a global mood - a whole-session average would read roughly neutral and hide every one of them. Uniquely, the emotional low point at 478 to 502 s occurs while the SCREEN shows a fully successful run, so visual and audio evidence disagree by design; any effort model that infers sentiment from visual state rather than narration gets this journey exactly backwards. narration.line: Okay, let's get started. There is a verify script here and it runs twenty four checks.
Ten seconds a check, so four minutes of watching a progress line.
This is the first check of twenty four.
I am not going to sit and stare at this, so I will read something while it runs.
I have wanted to properly understand reduce for about three years.
The accumulator argument is the part I always get backwards.
Let me look at the flattening page as well.
Summing an array, which is the example everyone uses and nobody needs.
Flattening nested arrays is the one that is actually useful.
Back to the terminal. Check nineteen just threw a warning.
Cache staleness, forty one seconds. Wonderful.
And the remaining checks passed, so it is twenty three ok and one warning.
I have no idea whether forty one seconds is bad.
There is a thresholds file, which somebody was thoughtful enough to write.
Warn above thirty seconds, fail above three hundred.
So forty one is eleven seconds over a soft limit and nowhere near a hard one.
Which means this is fine and I spent four minutes watching it to find that out.
Writing that down so nobody else has to sit here for four minutes.
The note is saved and the warning is explained.
Okay, that is it. Nothing was broken, and I can prove it.

journeys.expected_physical: ~265 keypress rows in 6 bursts, dominated by one MDN URL (~88 rows) and one long quoted Set-Content line (~95 rows); ~6 click rows, all incidental; 8 scroll rows totalling ~33 notches. Roughly 190 seconds of the nine minutes carry ZERO input rows of any kind.
journeys.stresses: The low-density stratum, and the only journey in the category where waiting is the work. Switch rate is 0.55/min against the 2.72/min ceiling and narration runs ~29 wpm, so both scoring lanes sit near the floor rather than near saturation - the opposite end of the range from journeys 01 and 06, and the case where a scoring model is most likely to under-report effort simply because little was pressed. Three separate silences of 45, 50 and 50 seconds exercise Silero VAD and, more importantly, the 'report missing, never infer zero' rule: the operator was present, attentive and blocked, and a model that scores this session near zero has failed. The seven Edge scroll bursts change the viewport dramatically without changing any window title, giving the largest in-page precision probe in the category. Sentiment is a boredom curve rather than a friction curve: flat neutral, mild self-directed negativity while reading, sarcasm at the warning (245 s, 'Wonderful'), then a resolution that is positive about the outcome and negative about the cost (400 s), which is the hardest pair for a per-utterance classifier to keep apart. Cue audit against the real DEFAULT_CUES vocabulary: three lines fire - 'let's get started' (10 s, genuine), 'first' (55 s, a deliberate false positive at a non-boundary) and 'that is it' (515 s, genuine).
journeys.risks: Everything on screen is synthetic or public: a locally generated verify script, a locally generated thresholds file, and two MDN pages. No credentials, no accounts, no personal data, no real build system. Requires network for the two MDN pages; if offline, substitute two local HTML copies and adjust the URL keystroke counts. Edge runs InPrivate so autocomplete cannot vary keystroke counts between takes. The script's 240 s duration is fixed by Start-Sleep, so the WARN line lands at a predictable wall-clock offset, but the performer must be back in the Terminal by about 210 s or the warning scrolls past unremarked and the narration at 225 s no longer matches the screen. This journey generates the least ground truth per minute of any in the category, so it should be recorded twice rather than once if budget allows: with only five context switches, a single missed detection moves recall by twenty points.

journeys.title: Inventory transcribe: Excel to a localhost intake form
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A in full (it now includes the NEVER PAUSE rule and the flash-margin measurement), then:

1. Fixture data. Create D:\jem-scratch\inventory-fixture.xlsx. Row 1 headers: SKU, Description, Qty, UnitCost. Rows 2-7 entirely synthetic:
   AX-1042 | Bracket, steel, 40mm | 18 | 3.25
   CG-2210 | Cable gland, M20, grey | 40 | 1.10
   LD-0087 | Ladder tray, perforated, 3m, powder coated, with fixings | 4 | 62.00
   HN-5500 | Hex nut pack, M8, zinc | 100 | 0.40
   GS-0310 | Gasket set, EPDM | 6 | 11.00
   PB-7712 | Patch bar, anodised | 12 | 8.75
   No real supplier, customer, price or part data of any kind.
2. Fixture page. Create D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\intake.html served over localhost. Dark page, palette copied from the existing fixture (background #142d44, text #f5f7fb, card #24536d, button #e0f4ff on #638ea3). Four text inputs labelled SKU, Description, Qty, Unit cost; Description has maxlength="28" so long values visibly truncate; a 'Record line' button that appends a row to an on-page table and shows a small inline toast. CRITICAL: unlike the existing index.html fixture, this page must NOT call document.title, must NOT navigate, and must NOT submit anywhere. index.html sets document.title on every page() call, which is exactly why it emits JEM rows; this page must not, because the appended row is the deliberate JEM-invisible micro visual change being measured.
3. Serve it: python -m http.server 8099 --directory D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys, launched from a Windows Terminal window parked on DISPLAY2 and minimised before the take.
4. Taskbar pin order on DISPLAY1: position 1 = Edge, position 2 = Excel. Switching is by Win+1 / Win+2 only (no Alt-Tab overlay, fully deterministic, repeatable on a second take).
5. Excel: Office theme Black, Excel Options > General > 'Disable dark mode' UNCHECKED so the sheet canvas renders dark. Open the workbook, select A2, maximise on DISPLAY1. Freeze row 1. Turn AutoSave OFF and confirm the window title is static (see step 9).
6. Edge: dedicated 'JEM Fixture' profile, dark appearance, hover-card memory usage OFF, open http://localhost:8099/intake.html, maximised on DISPLAY1.
7. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-01', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause at any point during the take (see category_notes B4).
8. FLASH MARGIN, measured not guessed. With Excel maximised and the taskbar visible, run the section A ffmpeg one-liner that reports the 64x36 grey mean of a still capture. The evaluator's gate is a full-frame 64x36 grey mean above 245 sustained for at least 2 consecutive frames. A dark sheet canvas will read roughly 30 to 60, which is a margin of 185 or more. If the reading is above 200, stop and fix the theme; do not proceed on a white grid.
9. TITLE DRY RUN, 60 seconds, discarded. Record a throwaway JEM session, do one Win+2 / Win+1 pair, type three characters into the form, click Record line, and open events.csv. Confirm exactly two context_switch rows and no extra rows from Excel autosave state, from the form, or from the toast. If extra rows appear, fix the cause before the real take; the expected count below assumes none.

narration.line: Let's get started on the inventory intake for the pilot workspace.
The source workbook holds six synthetic rows of invented stock data.
Row two is a steel bracket, eighteen units, three dollars twenty five each.
The form accepted that without a single complaint, which I appreciate.
Okay next, I will work through the remaining five rows one at a time.
The cable gland line is forty units at one dollar ten.
Tabbing between these fields is smooth and I am making good time.
Row four has a very long description and I am worried it will overflow.
It truncated my description without any warning, which is genuinely annoying.
The field accepts twenty eight characters, so the short version is what fits.
Row five is a hex nut pack, one hundred units, forty cents each.
That row went in perfectly and the running table looks exactly right.
Row six is the gasket set, six units, eleven dollars.
Row seven is the anodised patch bar, twelve units, eight seventy five.
That's it for the transcription, so I will check all six lines against the sheet.
Every quantity and unit cost matches the workbook, which is a genuinely good result.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 16 click rows, all left button (12 form-field and Record-line clicks across six entries, plus 3 during the truncation repair, plus 1 spare). Roughly 315 keypress rows from actual typing: about 250 alphanumeric, about 20 whitespace, about 20 navigation (Tab), about 25 editing (Backspace). SEPARATELY, the 14 Win+number switches emit 14 modifier rows (Win is categorised modifier in KeyCategorizer) and 14 alphanumeric rows (the digit). That is 14 modifier rows, not 28; the earlier estimate double counted. Both the modifier rows and the 14 switch digits must be excluded from physical-effort counts, or the switching mechanism inflates the typing measure. Exactly 2 wheel-scroll spans totalling about 6 notches, valid only if the 800 ms scroll-idle rule in the step at 380 s is followed.
journeys.stresses: This is the clean calibration baseline for the whole multi-app category and the anchor every other journey is compared against. It exercises one thing well: full-window, high-luma-delta foreground switching between two maximised dark applications, at 1.75 switches per minute with every switch at least 18 seconds from its neighbour. That is clear of the single 2.0 s floor (min_gap_seconds 2.0 and min_scene_len_frames 10 at PROXY_FPS 5.0 are the same 2.0 s) and below the 2.72 switches-per-minute point where the cognitive lane pins to 100 (PER_MINUTE_SCALE context_switch is 36.75 and the score is clamped at 100), so recall here is genuinely diagnostic rather than saturated. Narration is about 200 words over 8 minutes, roughly 25 words per minute, which also keeps spoken_word off its 40.5 wpm ceiling (PER_MINUTE_SCALE spoken_word 2.47), so this is one of the few journeys where the effort score can actually move in both lanes at once. Secondary targets: the appended table row after each Record line is a deliberate sub-threshold change measured at PROXY_WIDTH 480, where it is a few pixels tall, so it tests precision against JEM-invisible micro-changes; the two Excel wheel bursts test that the translation post-filter suppresses scroll without eating the surrounding switches; and the 50 s single-app stretch from 140 s to 190 s confirms the detector does not manufacture cuts during heavy typing. SEGMENTATION, with one pre-registered prediction: the three intended cues are 'let's get started' at 6 s, 'okay next' at 80 s, and 'that's it' at 382 s. The 80 s cue lands on a switch and should snap exactly (SNAP_WINDOW_MS 3000); the 382 s cue is 2 s from the 380 s switch and should also snap, which is the only place in the category where snapping is directly observable. The 6 s cue is predicted to be DISCARDED, because _merge_short_boundaries drops any boundary less than MIN_SEGMENT_MS (10 s) after the video_start boundary at 0. That prediction is registered in advance and is the reason expected_segments is 3 rather than 4; journey 03 places its opening cue at 14 s specifically so the surviving case can be contrasted against this dropped one.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: the video records the entire monitor. The workbook, SKUs, prices and form contents are 100 percent synthetic and must stay that way. Excel's recent-files list and Edge's address-bar autocomplete are the two real leak vectors, and autocomplete history is the worse one because a resolved URL also lands in JEM's uia detail column as plaintext CSV, not only in the video. Use the dedicated 'JEM Fixture' Edge profile with no synced history and clear Excel's MRU before the take. No credentials are typed anywhere and the fixture page submits nothing over the network.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE. jem_eval._offsets raises 'paused sessions require per-segment ending anchors; not yet safe to score' whenever the manifest carries more than one start flash. A paused take is not merely degraded, it is unscoreable and must be re-recorded. (b) The flash gate is a full-frame 64x36 grey mean above 245 sustained for at least 2 consecutive frames, and the evaluator additionally aborts with 'sync alignment ambiguous' if the detected flash count is not exactly the logged count plus one. A dark Excel canvas leaves a margin of roughly 185, so this journey is safe, but measure it once in setup step 8 rather than assuming. (c) Any Win+number that lands on a window which has drifted to DISPLAY2 produces NO event at all (JEM ignores foreground windows off the selected monitor) and a wrongly long context span. Confirm both windows are on DISPLAY1 immediately before starting. (d) If the intake fixture is ever edited to set document.title, every Record line click starts emitting an extra JEM context_switch row and the expected count of 14 is wrong. The existing index.html fixture does exactly this, so do not copy its page() helper. (e) The dry run in setup step 9 is not optional; it is the only cheap way to catch an unexpected Excel or Edge title change before 8 minutes are spent.
REPRODUCIBILITY: high. Nothing depends on a public site, a login, or anything that changes daily. The only variance between takes is typing speed and read duration; the switch sequence is mechanically fixed by the Win+1 / Win+2 discipline.

journeys.title: Split-screen spec review: Acrobat beside Word, neither window ever on top
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A in full, then:

1. Fixture spec. Create D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\spec.html: a dark, six-section synthetic 'Intake field specification' using the same palette as the existing fixture. Sections: 1 SKU format, 2 Description handling (deliberately ambiguous about trimming), 3 Quantity range, 4 Unit cost precision (deliberately allows four decimals), 5 Error messages (deliberately three unhelpful strings), 6 Change log, plus a validation table. No real product, company or person named. This same page is reused by journeys 03 and 06, so build it once.
2. Print it to PDF: open http://localhost:8099/spec.html in Edge, Ctrl+P, destination 'Microsoft Print to PDF', Background graphics ON so the dark styling survives, save as D:\jem-scratch\intake-spec.pdf.
3. Open intake-spec.pdf in Acrobat. View > Display Theme > Dark Gray. Snap it to the LEFT half of DISPLAY1 with Win+Left. Set zoom so one page fills the pane. Dismiss every Acrobat banner, tool prompt and update notice before recording, and never return to the Home view during the take.
4. Create D:\jem-scratch\intake-notes.docx, open in Word, Office theme Black, View > Dark Mode ON. Snap it to the RIGHT half with Win+Right. Type a single heading line 'Spec review notes' and SAVE before the take, so the document is neither empty nor dirty. AutoSave OFF. AutoCorrect 'show options buttons' OFF.
5. FALLBACK if Acrobat will not render a dark page on this build: substitute Notepad++ in the Deep Black theme displaying D:\jem-scratch\intake-spec.md with identical content. The scientific payload is the side-by-side focus alternation, not the PDF. If the fallback is used, change the apps list to notepad++.exe and record the variant in the JEM scenario name so the two variants are never pooled.
6. Neither window is ever maximised and neither is ever moved during the take. Switching alternates between a single left-click into the other pane and a bare Alt+Tab tap, so both focus mechanisms are represented in one session.
7. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-02', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause.
8. TITLE AND SWITCHER DRY RUN, 60 seconds, discarded. Record a throwaway session. Do one click-switch and one Alt+Tab switch, type five characters in Word, and scroll the PDF three notches. Open events.csv and confirm: (a) exactly two context_switch rows, (b) no third row from Word retitling on edit, (c) no row attributable to the Alt+Tab task switcher taking foreground. Item (c) is the one genuinely unknown behaviour in this journey and it must be resolved before the take, because if the switcher does emit a row, the expected count of 22 becomes 32.
