narration.line: I have the field specification on the left and my review notes on the right.
Section one defines the SKU format as two letters, a dash, and four digits.
That rule is clearly written and easy to turn into a note.
Section two is vague about whether the description field is trimmed.
I am writing that ambiguity down because it will cause an argument later.
The quantity field is an integer between one and nine hundred ninety nine.
Scrolling down to the validation table on page three.
This validation table is excellent, it covers every case I was going to ask about.
The unit cost field allows four decimal places, which seems excessive.
My note says two decimals would match the workbook we actually use.
Page four covers the error messages shown for rejected rows.
The error text is unhelpful and a user would have no idea what to fix.
I am recording a concrete rewrite suggestion for each of the three messages.
Page five is the change log and it is short and clear.
The document does not say who owns the specification, which is a real gap.
I will add a line asking for an owner and a review date.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 12 window-activating left clicks plus about 8 in-document clicks, so about 20 click rows, every one of them inside the pane being activated. Roughly 900 keypress rows across the six note blocks: about 700 alphanumeric, about 90 whitespace, about 40 editing, about 30 navigation. SEPARATELY, the 10 bare Alt+Tab taps emit about 10 modifier rows (Alt) and about 10 navigation rows (Tab), which must be excluded from physical-effort counts; note this is one Alt row per tap, not two. Eight wheel-scroll spans in the PDF pane totalling roughly 35 notches, all confined to the left half of the frame, and all conditional on keeping notches under the 800 ms scroll-idle close.
journeys.stresses: This is the deliberate adversarial low-visual-delta stratum and it is the most scientifically valuable journey in the category precisely because it should fail. Both windows are visible simultaneously for the entire take, so every one of the 22 JEM foreground transitions changes almost no pixels. The correct threshold reference is min_content_val 12.0, not the 9.6 figure that was circulating; 9.6 is min_content_val multiplied by low_response_candidate_floor_factor 0.8, which is a different gate governing low-response candidate admission. On top of that the detector runs on a 480-pixel-wide proxy, so a title-bar highlight from a 3072-pixel source is sub-pixel before the threshold is even consulted. Expect close to zero detections against 22 truth events. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the earlier framing: this does NOT require a visual-annotation pass that nobody has built. jem_eval already decodes a grayscale delta profile at VISUAL_DELTA_FPS 10, records the peak frame-to-frame delta within the 500 ms match tolerance for every truth event, and reports three groups (all truth, visually corroborated at delta at least 0.30, and proxy-only). This journey's job is to populate the proxy-only stratum with 22 events at a known instant each, which converts a single anecdotal Outlook measurement of 0.039 into a properly powered sample. The calibration anchors already on record are 0.03 to 0.04 for a switch into an already-visible window, 1.13 to 1.89 for genuine transitions, 11.66 at the high end, and about 180 for a sync flash. Do NOT hillclimb min_content_val against this journey: dropping the floor far enough to catch a caret would flood every other journey, which is exactly what happened when min_content_val 4 scored 10/0/0 on the controlled replay but produced a website-scroll false positive on the IANA holdout. Its correct use is as the pre-registered known-limit sample that any candidate detector change must not regress elsewhere to improve here. Secondary target: eight half-frame wheel scrolls test whether the translation post-filter fires on coherent motion confined to one half of the frame, a case the full-frame phase-correlation test was never designed for. Segmentation: the narration was audited line by line against DEFAULT_CUES and contains none of the trigger words, including the easily-missed bare words 'now', 'then', 'first' and 'next', so segmentation must fall back entirely to scene boundaries. With almost no scene boundaries detected, expect close to one segment against a four-segment human annotation, the exact mirror image of the over-segmentation seen elsewhere. Sentiment skews negative, 5 of 16 lines, to feed the negative class that neutral-heavy narration starves.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: the spec PDF and the notes document are fully synthetic. Word's recent-documents list and Acrobat's recent-files list are the leak vectors; clear both before the take. Acrobat's Home view may show cloud-synced document names from a real Adobe account, so open the PDF directly into the document view and never navigate back to Home. No credentials, no email, no customer content.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE; a paused session is rejected outright by the evaluator. (b) This journey is unusually flash-safe because neither window ever occupies the full screen, but that safety depends on the no-maximise rule, so do not maximise either window mid-take to check something. (c) Acrobat banners are localised band changes that could manufacture a JAMS cut with no JEM row; dismiss all of them before starting. (d) The bare Alt+Tab tap toggles between the two most recent windows. With only two windows in play this is deterministic, but if any third window is activated at any point the toggle target becomes ambiguous and the sequence diverges. Close everything else on DISPLAY1. (e) OPEN QUESTION, resolve in the dry run: whether the Windows task switcher itself takes foreground on the recorded monitor and emits its own context_switch row. If it does, expected_context_switches becomes 32, not 22, and the click-switch and Alt+Tab-switch legs stop being comparable. Setup step 8 exists solely to settle this. (f) Word autosave or an AutoCorrect options popup would add unscripted visual change and possibly a title change; both are turned off in setup.
REPRODUCIBILITY: high, with one caveat. Typing volume and scroll depth vary between takes, so notch totals and keypress counts are approximate. The switch count and ordering are exact.

journeys.title: Email triage into a task list: Outlook fixture mailbox, Notepad++ and Edge
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A in full, then:

1. TENANT GATE, decide before anything else. If Outlook on this machine is signed into a work tenant with compliance or DLP tooling, do not record its window at all; record the section C Edge-fixture mailbox variant instead and rename the scenario accordingly. If you proceed with Outlook, File > Work Offline MUST be enabled for the whole take. Work Offline is a stronger mitigation than Do Not Disturb alone because it prevents new mail from arriving at all, rather than merely suppressing its toast.
2. Isolated mailbox. In Outlook classic: File > Account Settings > Data Files > Add, create D:\jem-scratch\JEM-Fixture.pst with display name 'JEM Fixture'. Seed its Inbox with exactly 10 synthetic messages. Every sender, subject and body is invented (suggested senders: Dana Okafor, Priya Raman, Sam Whitlock, Alerts Bot). Subjects in order: 1 'Intake row 14 rejected, no reason given', 2 'Intake row 14 rejected, no reason given (resend)', 3 'Screenshot of the truncated description field', 4 'Unit cost rounding, which rule applies?', 5 'This has been broken for a week and nobody answered', 6 'Nightly import finished', 7 'Nightly import finished', 8 'Spec link on the intake page is dead', 9 'Please confirm the quantity ceiling', 10 'Quantity ceiling question (from Sam)'. Seed by composing and dragging into the fixture Inbox, or with a short Outlook VBA loop. No message may leave the machine. Keep a pristine copy of the seeded PST and restore it before every take so message order and read state are identical.
3. HIDE THE REAL MAILBOX. Select the fixture Inbox, then View > Folder Pane > Minimized so the folder tree and the real account's address are never rendered. To-Do Bar off. Reading Pane ON, positioned Right; this is part of the specification, not a preference, because the repaint geometry is the measurement. Do not use Outlook search at any point; the suggestion dropdown surfaces real correspondents.
4. Notepad++ Deep Black theme, open D:\jem-scratch\triage-tasks.md containing a single heading line. SAVE EXACTLY ONCE, at the very end of the take.
5. Edge, 'JEM Fixture' profile, dark, on http://localhost:8099/spec.html (the same fixture spec page built for journey 02). Add a deliberately dead link at the bottom of that page whose click handler shows an INLINE error panel and neither navigates nor touches document.title.
6. Taskbar pin order on DISPLAY1: 1 = Edge, 2 = Outlook, 3 = Notepad++. Switch with Win+1 / Win+2 / Win+3 only.
7. All three windows maximised on DISPLAY1. Do Not Disturb ON in addition to Work Offline.
8. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-03', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause.
9. TITLE DRY RUN, 90 seconds, discarded, and mandatory here because two of this journey's three payloads are assumptions until it is run. Record a throwaway session and confirm from events.csv: (a) clicking a different message in the Outlook list emits NO context_switch row (some builds write 'Updating this folder' into the title bar, which would emit one); (b) the first keystroke into Notepad++ DOES emit a context_switch row, because JEM only writes a row when the derived ContextIdentity changes, and whether the dirty-flag asterisk changes the derived identity is build-dependent; (c) Ctrl+S emits the matching row back. If (b) and (c) do not hold, drop the two title-flip rows from the expected count and record that finding, because the absence is itself a result.
10. NOTE: OneNote was considered for the task list and rejected because its notebook navigation pane displays real notebook names. Notepad++ on a single scratch file leaks nothing.

steps.action: Flash cleared. Outlook foreground, fixture Inbox selected, message 1 already showing in the reading pane. Sit still four seconds.
steps.produces: Baseline dwell.

steps.action: Read message 1 in the reading pane. Click message 2 in the list.
steps.produces: 1 click row. NO JEM context_switch, because Outlook's window title does not change on message selection. But the reading pane repaints across roughly half the screen, which is a large delta even on the 480-pixel proxy. This is the designed JAMS-detectable, JEM-invisible change: counted as a false positive against JEM proxy labels while being a correct visual detection. Nine more of these are scattered through this journey.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Type task line 1 referencing message 1's sender and row number.
steps.produces: JEM context_switch OUTLOOK.EXE -> notepad++.exe (row 1). If dry-run item (b) held, the first keystroke also flips the title to '*triage-tasks.md' and emits a SECOND row (row 2) with essentially zero visual delta. Roughly 55 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read message 2, recognise it as a duplicate of message 1, click message 3.
steps.produces: Row 3; 1 click; another reading-pane repaint with no JEM row behind it.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Merge the duplicate into task line 1 rather than adding a new one.
steps.produces: Row 4; roughly 40 keypress rows including Backspace rows in the editing category. No further title flip, because the file is already dirty and the identity is unchanged.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read message 3 with its screenshot, click message 4.
steps.produces: Row 5; 1 click; a reading-pane repaint that includes an image, so a notably larger delta than the text-only ones and a useful within-journey delta gradient.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Add task line 2 for the truncation bug.
steps.produces: Row 6; roughly 60 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read message 4 asking about unit cost rounding.
steps.produces: Row 7.

steps.action: Win+1 to Edge. Scroll the spec page to section 4 and read the decimal rule, keeping notches under 800 ms apart.
steps.produces: Row 8, an OUTLOOK.EXE -> msedge.exe wholesale replacement and the highest-delta leg in the journey; one scroll span of about 8 notches down.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Add task line 3 with the answer quoted from the spec.
steps.produces: Row 9; roughly 70 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read message 5, the angry one, click message 6.
steps.produces: Row 10; 1 click; reading-pane repaint.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Add task line 4 capturing the underlying issue, not the tone.
steps.produces: Row 11; roughly 65 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read messages 6 and 7, the automated alerts. Click 6, then click 7, then press Ctrl+Q on each to mark them read.
steps.produces: Row 12; 2 click rows; 2 reading-pane repaints plus a list-row unbolding, which is a small localised change; and from the two Ctrl+Q presses, 2 modifier rows and 2 alphanumeric rows.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Type a one-line note that messages 6 and 7 need no task.
steps.produces: Row 13; roughly 40 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read message 8 about the dead spec link, click message 9.
steps.produces: Row 14; 1 click; reading-pane repaint.

steps.action: Win+1 to Edge. Click the deliberately dead link at the bottom of the spec fixture page and watch the inline error panel appear.
steps.produces: Row 15; 1 click; the inline error panel is neither a navigation nor a title change, so it is another JEM-invisible visual change with a precisely known instant.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Add task line 5 confirming the broken link.
steps.produces: Row 16; roughly 55 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook. Read messages 9 and 10, recognise them as the same request from two people. Click 10.
steps.produces: Row 17; 1 click; reading-pane repaint.

steps.action: Win+3 to Notepad++. Add task line 6 covering both, then scroll the whole task file top to bottom in three separated bursts and tidy the wording of three lines.
steps.produces: Row 18; roughly 120 keypress rows with a high editing-category share; 3 scroll spans, valid only if each burst is internally under 800 ms per notch and separated by at least 3 seconds. This is also the journey's deliberately SILENT human task boundary, with no cue word anywhere near it.

steps.action: Win+2 to Outlook, glance at the list, Win+3 back to Notepad++, add an owner to each of the six tasks.
steps.produces: Rows 19 and 20 at about 12 s spacing; roughly 90 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+1 to Edge to check one spec reference, Win+3 back to Notepad++, Ctrl+S to save.
steps.produces: Rows 21 and 22; Ctrl+S emits 1 modifier row and 1 alphanumeric row, and if dry-run item (c) held it also flips the title back and emits row 23 with essentially zero visual delta.

steps.action: Hands off for ten seconds reading the finished list, then move to DISPLAY2 and press Save in JEM.
steps.produces: Trailing quiet region, end sync flash.

narration.line: To start, I am working through a fixture mailbox of ten synthetic messages.
Message one is a rejected intake row with no explanation attached.
I am logging it as a task with the sender name and the row number.
Message two is a duplicate of message one, which wastes my time.
I will merge both into a single task instead of tracking them twice.
Message three actually includes a screenshot and a clear description.
That one is a pleasure to triage and takes about ten seconds.
Message four asks about the unit cost rounding rule again.
I am checking the specification page in the browser for the exact wording.
The spec says two decimals, so I can answer that with real confidence.
Message five is angry and I do not think the tone is warranted.
I am logging the underlying issue and ignoring the tone entirely.
Messages six and seven are automated alerts with no action required.
I am marking both as read and leaving them out of the task list.
Message eight reports that a link on the intake page does not open.
The link genuinely is broken and that is a poor experience for a customer.
Messages nine and ten are the same request from two different people.
The task list has six entries and I am tidying the wording.
Every task has an owner and a message reference, which feels solid.
That is it for the triage pass and the list is ready to share.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 12 click rows, nearly all left button, concentrated in the Outlook message list. Roughly 660 keypress rows from typing: about 500 alphanumeric, about 70 whitespace, about 50 editing, about 20 navigation. SEPARATELY, and to be excluded from physical-effort counts: 21 Win+number presses emit 21 modifier rows and 21 alphanumeric rows, two Ctrl+Q presses emit 2 modifier and 2 alphanumeric rows, and Ctrl+S emits 1 modifier and 1 alphanumeric row, so about 24 modifier rows in total. The earlier estimate of about 50 modifier rows counted each shortcut twice. Four wheel-scroll spans totalling roughly 20 notches.
journeys.stresses: This journey exists to quantify the label-noise asymmetry in both directions inside one take, at known instants, which no other journey in the category does. Ten times here, clicking a different message repaints roughly half the screen without changing Outlook's window title, so JEM logs nothing while JAMS very probably fires a cut. Under the context-switch-only evaluator those ten detections are scored as false positives, which is the wrong reading: they are correct visual detections of a change JEM is structurally blind to. Running this journey is how you demonstrate that JAMS precision measured against JEM proxy labels is an UNDERESTIMATE. Note the framing correction: the jem_eval visual-delta profile added on September 18 handles the opposite direction (JEM truth with no visual evidence) by stratifying truth events at delta 0.30, but it has no mechanism at all for this direction, because a detection with no truth row nearby is simply an unmatched cut. Quantifying JEM-invisible visual change is therefore the one genuinely missing piece of the harness, and this journey produces ten pre-registered instances of it. The second, separable payload is the inverse: the Notepad++ dirty-flag title flip should emit two rows with essentially zero visual delta, one at the first keystroke and one at Ctrl+S, which are JEM truth with no visual evidence and belong in the proxy-only stratum alongside journey 02. Both flips are conditional on the setup step 9 dry run, because JEM writes a row only when the derived ContextIdentity changes and the asterisk's effect on the derived identity is build-dependent; if they do not fire, expected_context_switches drops to 21 and that null result is worth recording. Third payload: three-way switching with one genuinely high-delta leg (Outlook to Edge) alongside two moderate-delta Office-to-editor legs, at 1.84 switches per minute, comfortably under the 2.72 cognitive saturation point, so recall stays diagnostic. SEGMENTATION uses a mixed cue strategy on purpose and every line was audited against the real DEFAULT_CUES lists, including the bare words 'now', 'then', 'first' and 'next' that are easy to trip accidentally: an explicit 'to start' at 14 s, a completely silent boundary at about 605 s, and an explicit 'that is it' at 692 s. The 14 s placement is deliberate and contrasts against journey 01, whose opening cue at 6 s is predicted to be discarded by the 10 s MIN_SEGMENT_MS merge against the video_start boundary; at 14 s this one should survive. One journey therefore scores the cued path, the silent fallback path and the greedy merge together.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: this is the highest-risk journey in the category and the mitigations are not optional. Work Offline MUST be on, so no new mail can arrive at all. The Folder Pane MUST be minimised so the real account's address is never rendered. Outlook search MUST NOT be used. Do Not Disturb MUST be on as a second layer. All ten fixture messages are invented; no real name, address, customer or incident may appear. If Outlook is signed into a work tenant with compliance tooling, do not record it; use the section C Edge-fixture mailbox variant, which needs no account of any kind.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE. (b) A toast notification would break privacy and ground truth in a single event, and could also steal foreground and corrupt the switch sequence; Work Offline plus Do Not Disturb is the belt-and-braces answer. (c) Reading Pane Right is part of the specification; with the pane off or at Bottom the repaint geometry changes completely and the ten JEM-invisible changes get different deltas. (d) Saving triage-tasks.md more than once multiplies the title-flip rows and invalidates the count. (e) Some Outlook builds write 'Updating this folder' into the title bar, which would emit unscripted NAMECHANGE rows; setup step 9 item (a) exists to catch this. Note that JEM coalesces NAMECHANGE bursts over hooks.namechange_quiet_ms = 200, so a rapid flicker collapses to one row rather than many, but one unexpected row still breaks the count. (f) The expected count of 23 is derived as 21 Win+number switches plus 2 title flips. The earlier figure of 28 was not derivable from the step list and has been corrected.
REPRODUCIBILITY: moderate. The ten fixture messages make the content deterministic, but Outlook's list rendering and read/unread state vary between takes. Restore the pristine PST before every take.

journeys.title: Rapid Alt-Tab triangle: Windows Terminal, VS Code and MDN, dark on dark on dark
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A in full, then:

1. Public sample repo, cloned once before the take: git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/expressjs/express D:\jem-scratch\express. Public, stable, MIT licensed, nothing of Chris's on screen.
2. VS Code Insiders open on D:\jem-scratch\express, theme Dark Modern, file lib/router/index.js open, minimap on, integrated terminal CLOSED (a second terminal surface inside Code muddies the switch taxonomy). REQUIRED: add "window.title": "VS Code Insiders" to settings.json so the window title stops changing with the active file and the dirty marker. Without it, every edit changes the derived ContextIdentity and emits an extra JEM row with zero visual delta.
3. Windows Terminal, PowerShell profile, Campbell or One Half Dark, acrylic and transparency OFF (transparency lets the window behind bleed through and manufactures continuous phantom motion), font 14pt, cwd D:\jem-scratch\express. REQUIRED: set "suppressApplicationTitle": true on the profile so running a command does not rename the tab. Journey 05 deliberately leaves this at the default so the two behaviours are measured separately; here it must be on.
4. Edge, 'JEM Fixture' profile, dark, on https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/find with MDN's own theme toggle set to Dark. Note the retrieval date in the scenario metadata. SCROLL ONLY: do not click any MDN link, including in-page section links, and do not use the search box. A navigation changes document.title, which changes the derived Edge ContextIdentity and emits extra rows. The earlier plan's 'a handful of Edge title-change rows on top' would have made the expected count indeterminate; the scroll-only rule makes 44 exact.
5. All three MAXIMISED on DISPLAY1. Switching is by HELD Alt+Tab (hold Alt, press Tab once or twice, release) so the switcher overlay is captured. That is deliberate here and nowhere else in the category.
6. Only read-only shell commands: git status, git log --oneline -12, dir lib, node -e "console.log([1,2,3,4].find(n => n > 2))", npm ls --depth 0. Nothing that writes, installs, deletes, pushes or authenticates.
7. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-04', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause.
8. SWITCHER DRY RUN, 45 seconds, discarded, and BLOCKING. Record a throwaway session, perform four held Alt+Tab switches around the triangle, and read events.csv. Count the context_switch rows. If there are four, the task switcher does not register as a foreground window on the recorded monitor and the expected count of 44 stands. If there are eight, the switcher registers too and the expected count is 88 with alternating near-zero-delta rows; record that and adjust before the real take rather than after. This is the single largest unknown in the journey and it is cheap to settle.
9. RECORD THIS SECOND, right after journey 01. It is short and its failure is expected, so it is the cheapest way to confirm the capture and upload chain works before committing to a long take.

steps.action: Flash cleared. VS Code foreground on lib/router/index.js. Sit still three seconds.
steps.produces: Baseline dwell, clean flash separation.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab to Windows Terminal. Type git status and press Enter.
steps.produces: JEM context_switch Code - Insiders.exe -> WindowsTerminal.exe. DARK ON DARK: a near-black editor replaced by a near-black terminal, the documented hard false-negative class. The switcher overlay is on screen for a few hundred ms first, which is itself a large delta; whether the 2.0 s min-gap absorbs it or it generates its own candidate is an open question this journey answers.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab back to VS Code. Scroll down about 15 lines in one burst.
steps.produces: Switch 2, only 5 s after switch 1. Above the 2.0 s floor but the tightest legal spacing in the calm phase; one scroll span.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab, Tab again to reach Edge. Read the Array.prototype.find signature.
steps.produces: Switch 3 at about 4 s spacing. MDN in Edge is dark but structurally very different from an editor, so this is the high-delta leg of the triangle and the within-journey control against the dark-on-dark legs.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab back to VS Code. Type a two-line comment above the router handler.
steps.produces: Switch 4 at about 4 s; roughly 70 keypress rows. The window.title override keeps the title fixed, so no extra rows.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab to Terminal. Run git log --oneline -12.
steps.produces: Switch 5 at about 5 s; roughly 25 keypress rows; a full-screen text repaint inside an already-dark window, which is a useful intermediate delta case.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab, Tab to Edge. Scroll to the examples section in two bursts.
steps.produces: Switch 6; scroll spans totalling about 10 notches.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab to VS Code. Adjust the comment.
steps.produces: Switch 7 at about 4 s; roughly 30 keypress rows.

steps.action: Repeat the Code to Terminal to Edge to Code cycle four more times over the next 100 seconds, spending 5 to 9 seconds in each window. In Terminal run dir lib, then node -e with the find example, then npm ls --depth 0, then git status again. In Edge scroll (never click) between the syntax and examples sections. In Code refine the comment each pass.
steps.produces: Switches 8 through 23, sixteen transitions at 5 to 9 s spacing. Roughly half are dark-on-dark Code to Terminal legs expected to be missed, roughly half involve Edge and should be detected. Pairing hard and easy legs at identical spacing inside one session is the controlled comparison that isolates the delta effect from the spacing effect.

steps.action: LABELLED VIOLATION BLOCK A: six Alt+Tab switches in fifteen seconds, Code to Terminal to Code to Edge to Code to Terminal, about 2.5 seconds in each window, reading one line in each. Do not narrate during this block.
steps.produces: Switches 24 through 29 at about 2.5 s spacing, just above the 2.0 s floor. Expect the greedy min-gap sweep to keep at most alternate cuts. Any misses here are harness artifacts, not detector defects, and must be reported under their own label.

steps.action: LABELLED VIOLATION BLOCK B: six more Alt+Tab switches in nine seconds, about 1.5 seconds per window. Do not narrate during this block.
steps.produces: Switches 30 through 35 at about 1.5 s spacing, BELOW the 2.0 s floor (min_gap_seconds 2.0, and min_scene_len_frames 10 at PROXY_FPS 5.0 is the same 2.0 s, so this is a single floor breached twice over, not two separate floors as earlier stated). At most one of every pair can ever be a true positive. This is the pre-registered unscoreable stratum; its recall must be reported separately and never folded into a headline number.

steps.action: Return to a calmer rhythm: five more cycles Code to Edge to Terminal at 6 to 8 seconds per window, running git status once more and re-reading the MDN return-value section by scrolling.
steps.produces: Switches 36 through 43 at 6 to 8 s spacing, back above the floor, giving a recovery tail so the journey does not end inside a violation block.

steps.action: Held Alt+Tab to Terminal, run node -e with the find example one final time and read the output.
steps.produces: Switch 44; roughly 45 keypress rows.

steps.action: Hands off for eight seconds, then move to DISPLAY2 and press Save.
steps.produces: Trailing quiet region, end sync flash.

narration.line: I am bouncing between the editor, the terminal and the reference page very fast.
This is the way I actually work when I am chasing a signature I half remember.
It is disorienting and I lose my place constantly.
The array find example on the reference page is exactly what I needed.
I am flipping back to confirm the argument order one more time.
Three windows in four minutes is genuinely exhausting to sustain.
The example returns the value I expected, which is a good place to stop.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 6 click rows only, because switching is entirely keyboard-driven and MDN is scroll-only. Roughly 250 keypress rows from typing: about 160 alphanumeric, about 30 whitespace, about 20 editing, about 10 navigation. SEPARATELY, and to be excluded from physical-effort counts: the 44 held Alt+Tab switches emit about 44 modifier rows (one Alt key-down per hold) and about 50 navigation rows (one Tab per press, with a second Tab on the legs that skip a window). Roughly 8 wheel-scroll spans totalling about 40 notches, subject to the 800 ms scroll-idle close. The whole physical profile of this journey is dominated by the switching mechanism rather than the work, which is itself the point.
journeys.stresses: Four failure modes are stacked deliberately in one short take, which is why it earns a slot despite being expected to score badly. First, DARK ON DARK: the Code-to-Terminal legs are two near-black surfaces whose absolute grayscale band-max delta plausibly sits under min_content_val 12.0 (the correct default; the 9.6 figure that was circulating is min_content_val multiplied by low_response_candidate_floor_factor 0.8, a different gate), and they are paired inside the same session against Edge legs at identical spacing so the delta effect is isolated from the spacing effect. Second, SPACING VIOLATION: two labelled blocks at 2.5 s and 1.5 s sit just above and clearly below the single 2.0 s floor, where at most one of each pair can be matched. Reporting that as a JAMS defect would be a measurement error, so this journey is the pre-registered evidence that the artifact exists and how large it is. Third, SATURATION: 44 switches in 4.1 minutes is about 10.7 per minute, nearly four times the 2.72 per minute point at which the cognitive lane pins to 100 at PER_MINUTE_SCALE 36.75, so it demonstrates concretely that the effort score cannot distinguish frantic work from merely busy work. Fourth, the held Alt+Tab overlay is captured on purpose: a large translucent full-screen change immediately preceding each real switch. Whether the 2.0 s min-gap absorbs it, whether it generates its own candidate, and whether the switcher window itself emits a JEM row are three separate unknowns, and setup step 8 settles the third before any of it matters. Finally, 44 switches against 2 human task segments is the most extreme switch-to-segment divergence in the category, and with zero DEFAULT_CUES words in the narration (audited, including the bare words 'now', 'then', 'first' and 'next') segmentation must run entirely on scene boundaries, which at MIN_SEGMENT_MS 10000 caps it near 24 segments for a 2-segment task. Do not hillclimb against this journey; use it as the regression sample that a candidate change must not make worse elsewhere. Narration is only 7 lines over 4.1 minutes, about 22 words per minute, deliberately sparse both because there is no breath to spare during the violation blocks and because spoken_word saturates at 40.5 wpm.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: low by design. The repo is a public MIT clone, MDN is a public docs site, and every shell command is read-only. Two leak vectors: VS Code's Recent list on the Welcome screen (open the folder directly, never show Welcome) and the PowerShell prompt showing a real path or an unrelated git branch (cwd is pinned to the scratch clone). No credentials are typed, no npm install, no git push, no authentication of any kind.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE. (b) If the "window.title" override is not set, VS Code retitles on every file switch and dirty-marker change, injecting extra rows with zero visual delta. (c) If suppressApplicationTitle is not set, Windows Terminal renames its tab per command and does the same; journey 05 deliberately measures that behaviour, this journey must exclude it. (d) Terminal acrylic and transparency must be off; a translucent window shows what is behind it and generates continuous phantom motion that will corrupt both the context-switch and scroll providers. (e) MDN must be scroll-only. A link click changes document.title, changes the derived Edge identity, and adds rows the expected count does not include. (f) Held Alt+Tab with three windows requires counting Tab presses; a miscount changes the destination. Accept a small divergence and log the actual sequence from JEM's own CSV rather than re-recording, since JEM's CSV is the truth for whatever actually happened. (g) MDN can restyle or move content; pin the exact URL, record the retrieval date, and if the dark toggle resets, do not proceed, because a maximised light MDN page is the one flash-detector hazard in this otherwise dark journey. (h) The setup step 8 switcher dry run is blocking, not advisory.
REPRODUCIBILITY: moderate. The fast blocks are inherently hard to reproduce to the second and a second take will not match switch for switch. That is acceptable: what must be reproducible is the CHARACTER of the take (spacing bands, dark-on-dark pairing, saturation), not the exact instants.

journeys.title: Three-zone reconciliation: the same two apps switched twice, once side by side and once maximised
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A in full, then:

1. PowerToys FancyZones: create a three-column layout on DISPLAY1, roughly 30 / 40 / 30 percent. Everything stays inside those zones except for two scripted whole-screen changes.
2. Fixture workbook D:\jem-scratch\reconcile-fixture.xlsx with two sheets. Sheet 'ledger': 40 rows, columns Ref, Amount, Currency, all synthetic (refs like REF-0001). Sheet 'feed': the same 40 refs with 5 deliberate amount mismatches, all 5 on rows whose Currency is EUR, each off by 2 or 3 cents. Office theme Black, dark sheet canvas on, AutoSave off. Snap to the LEFT zone.
3. Windows Terminal, PowerShell, dark, acrylic and transparency OFF, cwd D:\jem-scratch, snapped to the MIDDLE zone. DELIBERATELY LEAVE "suppressApplicationTitle" AT ITS DEFAULT (false) for this journey only. The tab-title changes it produces are a target measurement here, and journey 04 measures the suppressed case, so the pair is a controlled contrast.
4. Fixture page D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\reconcile-rules.html served on localhost: dark page listing six numbered matching rules, no document.title calls after load, no navigation. Rule 3 covers whitespace stripping; rule 6 covers banker's rounding and is deliberately precise. Edge on http://localhost:8099/reconcile-rules.html, 'JEM Fixture' profile, snapped to the RIGHT zone.
5. Export the two sheets to CSV during setup so the shell has something to sum. Only read-only shell commands during the take: Get-Content, Measure-Object, Select-Object, Write-Host, and plain arithmetic. Nothing that writes or deletes.
6. Switching is by single left-click into the target zone during the side-by-side phases, and by Win+2 / Win+3 / Win+1 during the maximised phase. Taskbar pin order 1 = Edge, 2 = Excel, 3 = Terminal.
7. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-05', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause. A 14.5 minute target against a 20 minute hard limit leaves 5.5 minutes of headroom; if the take overruns 17 minutes, stop and re-record rather than risk the probe rejecting the file with 'too_long'.
8. TITLE DRY RUN, 90 seconds, discarded. Confirm from events.csv that running one PowerShell command in the middle zone DOES emit a context_switch row from the tab-title change. JEM writes a row only when the derived ContextIdentity changes, and the terminal identity is built from the tab title, so this is likely but not certain. If it does not fire, drop 6 from the expected count and record the null result.
9. RECORD THIS ONE FIRST OF ALL SEVEN, as the pipeline timeout canary, and confirm it scores end to end before recording anything else. At 14.5 minutes and 3072x1728 it is the longest and largest media in the category, and three separate limits were sized for 90 second clips: jem_eval's CFR re-encode has a 300 second subprocess timeout, its flash detection decodes every frame to 64x36 gray with a 120 second timeout, and probe.py rejects anything over MAX_DURATION_SECONDS (20 minutes) with 'too_long'. If this journey blows any of them, every long journey in the whole corpus is at risk and that must be known before 50 takes are recorded, not after. Record the wall-clock of each stage.

steps.action: Flash cleared. Three zones populated, Excel focused. Sit still four seconds.
steps.produces: Baseline dwell, clean flash separation.

steps.action: Read the ledger Ref column. Click into the Edge zone on the right and read rule 3.
steps.produces: Row 1, EXCEL.EXE -> msedge.exe, plus 1 click. LOW DELTA: all three windows stay visible and only focus moves. Expected proxy-only truth event, same class as journey 02 but with three panes instead of two and a narrower focus target.

steps.action: Click into the Excel zone. Scroll the ledger down about 10 notches comparing refs, keeping the notches under 800 ms apart.
steps.produces: Row 2 plus 1 click; one scroll span confined to the left 30 percent of the frame, which tests the strip-based scroll detector on a narrow column rather than a full-width page.

steps.action: Click into the Terminal zone. Run a Get-Content piped to Measure-Object to count the feed rows.
steps.produces: Row 3 plus 1 click; roughly 60 keypress rows; AND, subject to the setup step 8 dry run, a Windows Terminal tab-title change emitting row 4, whose only visual evidence is a few characters of title text that are sub-pixel on the 480-pixel proxy. Another deliberate near-zero-delta truth event.

steps.action: Click into Excel. Widen column A by dragging the header divider until the full reference is visible.
steps.produces: Row 5 plus 1 click. NOTE: JEM logs the drag as a single click row at the press point and records no motion at all, so the column-resize animation is a visual change with only a point event behind it. This is the one place in the category where a physical gesture and its visual consequence are deliberately mismatched in the truth record.

steps.action: Click into Edge, read rule 3 again, click back into Excel and confirm the whitespace-stripped refs match.
steps.produces: Rows 6 and 7 plus 2 clicks, at about 20 s spacing, both low delta.

steps.action: Click into Terminal. Run a command that sums the feed Amount column.
steps.produces: Row 8 plus 1 click; roughly 70 keypress rows; plus tab-title row 9.

steps.action: MAXIMISE EXCEL with Win+Up. Read rows 15 to 25 at full width.
steps.produces: NO JEM context_switch, because maximising changes neither the foreground window nor its derived identity. But it is an enormous whole-screen visual change at a precisely known instant. A designed JAMS false positive against JEM proxy labels, and the counterpart to journey 03's reading-pane repaints. Also 1 modifier row and 1 navigation row from Win+Up.

steps.action: Win+3 to Terminal (now behind the maximised Excel), run a rounding comparison, Win+2 back to Excel.
steps.produces: Rows 10, 11 (tab title) and 12. HIGH DELTA: with Excel maximised these same two applications now switch by wholesale screen replacement. This is the matched pair against the low-delta rows 3 and 8 between the identical applications earlier in the same take, same session, same lighting, same content, same operator. It is the cleanest isolation of visual delta from every other variable available anywhere in this corpus.

steps.action: Win+1 to Edge (maximised), read rule 6 on banker's rounding, Win+2 back to Excel.
steps.produces: Rows 13 and 14, both high delta, matched against the low-delta rows 1 and 6 between the identical applications.

steps.action: Win+3 to Terminal, run the rounding calculation again applying the banker's rule, Win+2 to Excel.
steps.produces: Rows 15, 16 (tab title) and 17; roughly 80 keypress rows.

steps.action: RESTORE Excel with Win+Down back into its FancyZones left zone.
steps.produces: NO JEM row again, and another large whole-screen visual change. The second designed false positive against proxy labels, and the boundary that returns the journey to the low-delta regime.

steps.action: Click into the Edge zone, read rule 6 once more, click back into the Excel zone.
steps.produces: Rows 18 and 19 plus 2 clicks, back to low delta, matched directly against the high-delta rows 13 and 14 between the same two applications less than three minutes earlier.

steps.action: LONG DWELL: study the feed sheet for 90 seconds without switching, scrolling twice in separated bursts to find the five EUR mismatches. Read each mismatched ref aloud as you find it.
steps.produces: No context switches for 90 seconds; 2 scroll spans. A long no-cut region at the exact point where a naive detector is most likely to manufacture cuts from spreadsheet scrolling and cell-selection highlights.

steps.action: Click into Terminal, run the final comparison command, read the five mismatched refs from the output.
steps.produces: Row 20 plus 1 click; roughly 70 keypress rows; plus tab-title row 21.

steps.action: Click into Excel, select each of the five mismatched rows in turn with five separate clicks.
steps.produces: Row 22 plus 5 click rows. The five selection highlights are small localised changes confined to the left 30 percent that should not clear the floor, so this is a five-instance precision probe against selection artifacts.

steps.action: Click into Edge, read rule 6's rounding clause aloud, click back into Excel.
steps.produces: Rows 23 and 24 plus 2 clicks, low delta.

steps.action: Click into Terminal, run the rounding check on the five mismatches and read the result.
steps.produces: Row 25 plus 1 click; roughly 50 keypress rows; plus tab-title row 26.

steps.action: Hands off for fifteen seconds, then move to DISPLAY2 and press Save in JEM.
steps.produces: Trailing quiet region, end sync flash, end_flash_log_ms. Total wall clock about 14.4 minutes, within the 20 minute probe limit with 5.5 minutes of headroom.

narration.line: I am reconciling a synthetic ledger against a synthetic feed of forty references.
Rule three says leading and trailing whitespace is stripped before matching.
The feed has exactly forty rows, so nothing has been dropped in transit.
Column A was too narrow to read, which made the comparison harder than it should be.
With the column widened the references line up cleanly against the ledger.
The feed total and the ledger total differ by about eleven cents.
I am opening the sheet full width so I can read a block of rows at once.
Rule six specifies banker's rounding, which I had assumed was ordinary rounding.
Getting that wrong would have produced five false mismatches in the report.
Applying the correct rule brings the difference down to the five real cases.
Back in the three column layout I can see the rules and the sheet together.
Every one of the five mismatches is on a euro denominated row.
A currency specific bug is much easier to explain than a random one.
The shell confirms the same five references I found by eye in the sheet.
I am highlighting each mismatched row so the screenshot is unambiguous.
The rounding clause is buried in a long paragraph and is easy to miss.
All five differences are two or three cents, which fits the rounding theory.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 21 click rows, all left button: about 15 zone-activating clicks, 5 row-selection clicks in Excel, and 1 column-divider drag which JEM records as a single click row at the press point with no motion. Roughly 330 keypress rows from typing six shell commands and reading: about 260 alphanumeric, about 30 whitespace, about 25 editing, about 15 navigation. SEPARATELY, and to be excluded from physical-effort counts: 6 Win+number presses emit 6 modifier and 6 alphanumeric rows, and Win+Up and Win+Down emit 2 modifier and 2 navigation rows. Roughly 5 wheel-scroll spans, three of them confined to the left 30 percent of the frame, totalling about 30 notches, all subject to the 800 ms scroll-idle close.
journeys.stresses: This is the best-designed experiment in the category because it is the only one with a genuine within-session control. The SAME two application pairs are switched twice under two visual regimes, minutes apart, with everything else held constant: Excel to Terminal at low delta (rows 3, 8) against Excel to Terminal at high delta (rows 10, 12, 15, 17), and Excel to Edge at low delta (rows 1, 6, 18, 19, 23, 24) against Excel to Edge at high delta (rows 13, 14). Same session, same operator, same content, same lighting, same fatigue level, same detector parameters. Every other comparison in the corpus confounds delta with session. The evaluator's per-truth-event visual delta profile means this comparison can be read directly out of one report rather than inferred across runs, and the expected result is a step function in recall at the maximise boundary at 260 s. Second payload: the maximise at 260 s and the restore at 455 s are two enormous whole-screen changes with NO JEM row behind either of them, at instants known to the second. They are designed false positives against proxy labels and they complement journey 03's ten reading-pane repaints, giving the corpus twelve pre-registered instances of JEM-blind visual change. Third payload: six terminal tab-title rows in the opposite direction, JEM truth with essentially no visual evidence, which pairs against journey 04's deliberately suppressed titles to isolate that behaviour. Fourth: the 90 second no-switch dwell from 540 s and the five selection-highlight clicks at 700 s are precision probes against the two artifact classes most likely to generate spurious cuts in spreadsheet work. Fifth: at 1.8 switches per minute this sits below the 2.72 cognitive saturation point, so the score can move. Sixth and separately from all the science, it is the pipeline timeout canary; see setup step 9. Segmentation: four human task segments (survey, maximised deep dive, mismatch hunt, verification) with cue words deliberately absent from the narration, so this journey scores the silent fallback path over a long duration where the 10 s greedy merge has the most room to over-generate.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: everything is synthetic. The refs, amounts and currencies are invented, the shell commands are read-only, and the rules page is a local fixture. Excel's MRU and the PowerShell prompt path are the only leak vectors; clear the MRU and keep cwd pinned to D:\jem-scratch.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE. (b) THE MAXIMISE AT 260 s IS THE FLASH RISK IN THIS JOURNEY. A maximised dark Excel canvas is safe, but if the dark sheet canvas is unavailable on this build a maximised white grid is the one configuration in the whole category that could approach the 64x36 full-frame grey mean of 245 for 2 consecutive frames. Measure it in the section A preflight with Excel actually maximised, not merely zoned, and if the reading exceeds 200 do not record this journey until the theme is fixed. A phantom flash does not degrade the score, it aborts the evaluation with 'sync alignment ambiguous' and the whole 14.5 minutes is wasted. (c) THE 20 MINUTE HARD LIMIT. probe.py raises 'too_long' above 20 minutes with no partial result. Budget 14.5, abort at 17. (d) The three timeouts in setup step 9 are the reason this is recorded first; do not batch-record other long journeys until this one has scored end to end. (e) The six terminal tab-title rows are conditional on the setup step 8 dry run; if they do not fire, expected_context_switches is 20. (f) Any window that drifts out of its FancyZone onto DISPLAY2 produces no JEM event at all and a wrongly long span; verify zone occupancy immediately before starting. (g) Do not maximise anything other than Excel at 260 s, and restore it at 455 s exactly as scripted, because the low-delta and high-delta strata are defined by those two instants.
REPRODUCIBILITY: moderate to high. The mismatch positions are fixed by the fixture, the switch sequence is scripted, and the maximise and restore are mechanical. Dwell durations and typing speed vary.

journeys.title: Light on light: three white windows, six switches in ten minutes, and the flash-detector margin
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A, EXCEPT section A's dark-theme defaults, which this journey deliberately inverts. Then:

1. WHY THIS EXISTS: every other journey in this category is dark on dark, which means the entire corpus is biased to one luma regime and the detector has never been measured on the other. This journey is the light-theme stratum and the direct matched contrast to journey 01, which runs the same Excel-and-Edge pairing in the dark.
2. THE FLASH MARGIN IS THE FIRST DELIVERABLE, before any recording. For each of the three windows in turn, maximise it on DISPLAY1 and run the section A one-liner that reports the 64x36 full-frame grey mean. Write the three numbers into the scenario notes. The evaluator's gate is a mean above 245 sustained for at least 2 consecutive frames, and the taskbar, the Office ribbon and the window chrome all pull the mean down, so a white Word page typically reads in the 210 to 235 range. GATE: if any of the three readings is 240 or above, do not record this journey with that window maximised; un-maximise it to about 85 percent width over a dark wallpaper, re-measure, and record the adjusted figure. This measurement is itself a result worth keeping, because it is the only empirical answer anyone has to the question of how close a normal light desktop actually gets to the flash threshold.
3. Fixture workbook D:\jem-scratch\intake-review.xlsx: the six rows from journey 01's fixture, already transcribed, with three deliberate errors seeded (one wrong quantity, one wrong unit cost, one description truncated at 28 characters). Office theme Colorful, dark mode OFF, white sheet canvas. AutoSave OFF. Maximised on DISPLAY1.
4. D:\jem-scratch\review-memo.docx in Word: Office theme Colorful, Dark Mode OFF, white page, a single saved heading line 'Intake review memo'. AutoSave OFF, AutoCorrect options button OFF. Maximised on DISPLAY1.
5. Edge, 'JEM Fixture' profile, appearance LIGHT, on http://localhost:8099/spec.html with the fixture page's light-variant stylesheet enabled (add a ?theme=light query the page reads once at load and never changes document.title for). Maximised on DISPLAY1.
6. Taskbar pin order on DISPLAY1: 1 = Edge, 2 = Excel, 3 = Word. Switching is by Win+1 / Win+2 / Win+3 only.
7. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-06-light', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause.
8. TITLE DRY RUN, 60 seconds, discarded. Confirm Excel and Word do not retitle on edit with AutoSave off, and that the light Edge fixture does not retitle. Six switches is a small number and a single unexpected row is a 17 percent count error here, so the dry run matters more in this journey than in the busy ones.

steps.action: Flash cleared. Excel maximised and focused on the transcribed review sheet. Sit still five seconds.
steps.produces: Baseline dwell. Note that in this journey the start flash has the smallest margin in the corpus, because the flash is white and the content behind it is also light. The flash is still a full-screen 255 against a content mean measured at step 2, so the run-of-2 test should still separate them cleanly, but this is exactly the configuration where that assumption is worth verifying against the detected flash count in the report.

steps.action: Read all six transcribed rows in the sheet aloud, comparing quantities and unit costs against memory. Scroll once, in one burst.
steps.produces: No switches for the opening 100 seconds; one scroll span. A long single-app opening that establishes the low-rate character of the journey before any transition exists to detect.

steps.action: Win+3 to Word. Write a three-line opening paragraph of the review memo naming the workbook and the date.
steps.produces: Switch 1, EXCEL.EXE -> WINWORD.EXE. HIGH-LUMA, LOW-DELTA: a white spreadsheet grid replaced by a white document page. Structurally different (grid lines and a ribbon versus a page and margins) but with a much smaller grayscale magnitude than any dark-to-dark or dark-to-light transition in the corpus. This is the untested regime the journey exists for. Roughly 180 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+2 to Excel. Find the first seeded error (the wrong quantity) by reading down the Qty column, scrolling once.
steps.produces: Switch 2; one scroll span; then a long dwell. Spacing to switch 1 is 105 seconds, the widest in the category.

steps.action: Win+3 to Word. Write up the quantity error as review point one, with the row reference and both values.
steps.produces: Switch 3; roughly 200 keypress rows.

steps.action: Win+1 to Edge. Read section 3 of the light spec page to confirm the permitted quantity range, scrolling twice in separated bursts.
steps.produces: Switch 4, WINWORD.EXE -> msedge.exe. This is the highest-delta leg available in an all-light journey, because a browser page has a different layout skeleton from a Word page, and it is the within-journey control against the Excel-to-Word legs. Two scroll spans.

steps.action: Win+2 to Excel. Find the second and third seeded errors (the wrong unit cost and the truncated description), selecting each cell with a click.
steps.produces: Switch 5; 2 click rows; two cell-selection highlights that are small localised changes and should not clear the floor.

steps.action: Win+3 to Word. Write up review points two and three, then read the whole memo back from the top, scrolling once.
steps.produces: Switch 6, the last one; roughly 320 keypress rows; one scroll span. A 240 second closing block with no switching at all.

steps.action: (Overlaps the block above by design; this is a within-block note, not a separate switch.) While still in Excel at about 575 s, widen the Description column so the truncation is unmistakable.
steps.produces: 1 click row for the divider drag, with no motion recorded, and a visual change with only a point event behind it. No context switch.

steps.action: Hands off for fifteen seconds looking at the finished memo, then move to DISPLAY2 and press Save in JEM.
steps.produces: Trailing quiet region, end sync flash. Total wall clock about 15 minutes of elapsed screen time compressed into a 10 minute target; see the timing note in stresses.

narration.line: I am reviewing six intake rows that were transcribed earlier against the source workbook.
Three of these six rows look wrong to me on a quick read.
I am writing the memo in a plain white document so it prints cleanly.
Working in light mode all day gives me a headache by the afternoon.
The quantity on the hex nut row reads ten and the source says one hundred.
A missing zero on a hundred unit line is a costly mistake to ship.
Review point one records the row, the entered value and the correct value.
Writing it out this carefully makes the correction trivial for whoever fixes it.
The specification confirms the quantity ceiling is nine hundred ninety nine.
So one hundred is perfectly valid and the entered ten was simply a typing slip.
The unit cost on the gasket row is out by a factor of ten as well.
Two decimal slips in six rows is a poor error rate for this process.
The ladder tray description was cut off at twenty eight characters as expected.
That third one is a known field limit rather than an operator error.
The memo has three clear review points with references and corrected values.
Two real errors out of six rows is worth escalating to whoever owns the form.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 5 click rows only: 2 cell selections, 1 column-divider drag recorded as a single click at the press point with no motion, and 2 spare. Roughly 700 keypress rows from writing the memo: about 540 alphanumeric, about 90 whitespace, about 45 editing, about 25 navigation. SEPARATELY, and to be excluded from physical-effort counts: 6 Win+number presses emit 6 modifier rows and 6 alphanumeric rows, the smallest switching overhead in the category. Roughly 6 wheel-scroll spans totalling about 25 notches, subject to the 800 ms scroll-idle close. The physical profile is dominated by sustained typing rather than by switching, which is the deliberate inverse of journey 04.
journeys.stresses: Three things this journey measures that nothing else in the category can. FIRST, THE LIGHT REGIME. Every other journey here is dark on dark, so the corpus as a whole cannot distinguish 'the detector struggles with low delta' from 'the detector struggles with dark content'. This journey holds the task shape close to journey 01's and inverts only the luma regime, using the same Excel and Edge pairing, so the two can be read against each other. The specific untested case is white-grid to white-page (switch 1, 3 and 6), which has a small grayscale magnitude for a structurally large change, and it is paired inside the same session against Word to Edge (switch 4), which is the largest structural change available in an all-light take. SECOND, THE FLASH MARGIN, MEASURED. Setup step 2 produces the first empirical numbers anyone has for how close a normal maximised light window gets to the 245 full-frame gate, for three different applications. The gate has been treated as a folk hazard across the whole plan; this turns it into three numbers with a documented method. It also makes this the one journey where the start-flash separation itself is genuinely worth checking in the report, because the flash and the content behind it are both light. THIRD, THE LOW END OF THE COGNITIVE LANE. Six switches in 10 minutes is 0.6 per minute, less than a quarter of the 2.72 per minute saturation point at PER_MINUTE_SCALE 36.75, and roughly one eighteenth of journey 04's rate. Together the two journeys bracket the lane end to end: if the score cannot separate 0.6 from 10.7 switches per minute in a way that matches how the two takes actually felt, the cognitive lane is not measuring anything useful, and that is a cheap and decisive test. The long dwells (105 seconds between switch 1 and 2, and 240 seconds after switch 6) are also the longest no-cut regions in the corpus and the strongest available precision probe. Segmentation: the narration was audited against DEFAULT_CUES and contains no trigger words, including the bare 'now', 'then', 'first' and 'next', so with only 6 scene-boundary candidates against a 3-segment human annotation this is the one journey where segmentation could plausibly UNDER-generate rather than over-generate, which is the opposite failure from everywhere else. Sentiment leans negative (6 of 16 lines) and the negativity is about genuine data errors rather than about the tooling, which gives the negative class some topical variety instead of 'the software annoyed me' every time. TIMING NOTE: the step list runs to about 905 seconds, which is 15 minutes, not 10. The 10 minute target is the intended pace and the step timestamps are the generous upper bound; hold the take under 16 minutes so the 20 minute probe limit is never in play, and prefer trimming the closing memo block if it runs long.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: everything is synthetic and carried over from journey 01's fixture. Excel's and Word's recent-files lists are the leak vectors and both must be cleared, and with light themes the recent-files panes are more legible in the recording than in the dark journeys, so this matters more here. No credentials, no network submission.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE. (b) THE FLASH GATE IS THE HEADLINE RISK OF THIS JOURNEY and it is the reason setup step 2 is a blocking gate with a numeric threshold rather than a suggestion. A phantom bright run of 2 frames anywhere in the take makes the detected flash count exceed the logged count plus one, and jem_eval aborts with 'sync alignment ambiguous', discarding the whole take. Measure all three windows, write the numbers down, and fall back to 85 percent width over a dark wallpaper for any window reading 240 or above. (c) Do not open any full-screen white dialog, print preview or Backstage view during the take, because those are brighter than the working views that were measured. (d) With only 6 expected switches, a single unscripted title change is a 17 percent count error, so the setup step 8 dry run is proportionally more important here than in the busy journeys. (e) Keep AutoSave off in both Office apps; an autosave state change in the title bar would add rows.
REPRODUCIBILITY: high. Six mechanical Win+number switches, a fixed fixture with three seeded errors, and no dependency on any public site. The only real variance is how long the memo takes to write, which is why the closing block is the designated place to trim.

journeys.title: Imposed switches: a local interrupter steals foreground at pre-declared instants
journeys.setup:
Run the shared preflight in category_notes section A in full, then:

1. WHY THIS EXISTS: in all six other journeys every switch is initiated by Chris, and is therefore immediately preceded by a click or a keypress. Any future heuristic that infers context switches from physical events would score perfectly on those six for entirely the wrong reason. This journey supplies switches with NO preceding operator input at all, which is the only way to tell a real visual or foreground detector apart from an input-correlation shortcut.
2. THE INTERRUPTER. Write D:\jem-scratch\interrupter.ps1: a fully local PowerShell script that sleeps to each of eight pre-declared offsets, and at each one opens a small Notepad window on DISPLAY1 containing a single synthetic line ('Interrupt 1 of 8: please confirm the quantity ceiling', and so on), brings it to the foreground, and appends the interrupt index and the script's own high-resolution timestamp to D:\jem-scratch\interrupter-log.csv. The script must not touch the network, must not read any real file, and must not use the Windows notification system (a real toast could be intercepted by, or confused with, a genuine notification and is also a privacy hazard). Eight synthetic interrupt lines, all invented, none referencing a real person or incident.
3. THE THIRD CLOCK. interrupter-log.csv is the point of the design: it is an INDEPENDENT timestamp source for eight events, produced by neither JEM nor JAMS. Every other journey in the corpus can only cross-check JEM active-time against JAMS video time. This one adds a third clock, so a three-way agreement (or disagreement) can be measured on the same events. Start the script from a Windows Terminal window on DISPLAY2, minimised, immediately before pressing Record in JEM, and write the offset between the JEM start-flash wall clock and the script start into the scenario notes.
4. THE FOCUS TASK. D:\jem-scratch\interrupt-notes.docx in Word, Office theme Black, Dark Mode ON, a saved heading line, AutoSave OFF, maximised on DISPLAY1. The task is to write a continuous 8 minute narrative summary of the fixture spec, so the interruptions cut into genuinely sustained work rather than into idle time.
5. THE REFERENCE. Edge, 'JEM Fixture' profile, dark, on http://localhost:8099/spec.html, maximised on DISPLAY1. Scroll only, no link clicks, no navigation.
6. Notepad: dark mode ON so the interrupter window matches the rest of the take's luma regime, positioned so it opens at roughly 40 percent of screen width in the centre of DISPLAY1. Sized deliberately: large enough to be a clear visual change, small enough that it is not a full-screen replacement, which puts these eight events in a middle delta band that nothing else in the corpus occupies.
7. Voluntary switching is by Win+1 (Edge) and Win+2 (Word) only. Taskbar pin order 1 = Edge, 2 = Word. Do not pin Notepad; it must only ever appear because the script raised it.
8. JEM: Project 'JAMS golden set', Scenario 'multi-app-switching-07', monitor = DISPLAY1. Do NOT press Pause.
9. DRY RUN, 2 minutes, discarded, and BLOCKING. Run the interrupter with two interrupts and confirm from events.csv that (a) the script raising Notepad DOES emit a context_switch row into notepad.exe with no preceding click or keypress row, and (b) dismissing it with Alt+F4 emits the return row. If the script's window does not take foreground reliably (Windows foreground-stealing restrictions can block a background process from activating a window), fix the activation method before recording; a script that raises a window without giving it foreground produces a visual change with NO JEM row, which would silently turn this journey into a copy of journey 03's payload instead of its own.

steps.produces: Baseline dwell.

A middle-band visual delta: a 40 percent centre window appearing over a dark page, larger than a caret and smaller than a full-screen replacement, and at an instant independently recorded in interrupter-log.csv.
