narration.line: I am writing a continuous summary of the field specification for the review pack.
This is the kind of writing that only works if I am left alone for ten minutes.
Something just jumped in front of my document and I have lost my sentence.
I am back in the document and trying to pick up where I left off.
That is the second interruption in under two minutes of actual writing.
Checking the specification myself is fine, because I chose to go and look.
That one landed in the middle of a sentence and I have no idea where I was.
I have rewritten the same paragraph twice because of these interruptions.
The fourth interrupt carries a question I have already answered in writing.
Going to the error messages section was my own decision and it went smoothly.
Another one, twelve seconds after I got back to the document.
I am ignoring the content of these and just clearing them off the screen.
Two of them stacked on top of each other, which is genuinely absurd.
The paragraph I am writing has taken four times as long as it should have.
That is eight interruptions in a task that needed one unbroken half hour.
The summary is finished and it reads reasonably well despite all of that.

journeys.expected_physical: Roughly 2 click rows only, which is the lowest in the category and deliberate: all voluntary switching is by Win+number and all dismissals are by Alt+F4, so almost nothing is clicked. Roughly 1300 keypress rows, overwhelmingly sustained prose typing: about 1000 alphanumeric, about 190 whitespace, about 70 editing, about 40 navigation. SEPARATELY, and to be excluded from physical-effort counts: 6 Win+number presses emit 6 modifier and 6 alphanumeric rows, and 9 Alt+F4 dismissals emit 9 modifier rows and 9 navigation rows. Roughly 3 wheel-scroll spans totalling about 15 notches. THE KEY PHYSICAL SIGNATURE is not a count at all: it is that 10 of the 22 context_switch rows (the imposed ones) have NO click or keypress row within the second preceding them, while all 12 voluntary ones do. That asymmetry is the measurement.
journeys.stresses: This journey supplies the one thing the other six structurally cannot: switches that Chris did not initiate. In every other journey a context switch is immediately preceded by a Win+number press, an Alt+Tab, or a click, which means an input-correlation heuristic dressed up as a detector would score near-perfectly on the whole rest of the corpus without looking at a single pixel. Here 10 of 22 switches have no preceding input at all, so this journey is the discriminator between a real detector and that shortcut, and it should be a mandatory member of the holdout split for exactly that reason. Second payload, and the reason the interrupter is a script rather than a person: interrupter-log.csv is an INDEPENDENT THIRD CLOCK for eight of the events. Everywhere else the corpus can only compare JEM active-time against JAMS video-time, with the sync flash as the sole bridge. Here a source that is neither JEM nor JAMS timestamps eight events, so a three-way agreement can be computed and the flash-offset mapping itself can be validated rather than assumed. Given that timestamp integrity is patent-core, having one journey in the corpus that can falsify the mapping independently is worth more than another journey that exercises the detector. Third payload: the interrupter window is deliberately sized at about 40 percent of screen width, which puts these eight events in a MIDDLE delta band that nothing else occupies. The corpus otherwise has near-zero delta (journeys 02 and 05's low phase), full replacement (journeys 01 and 05's high phase), and half-screen repaints (journey 03), with nothing in between; a partial overlay is both the commonest real-world interruption shape and the untested one. Fourth: the stacked pair at 565 s, where a second interrupter window is raised over the first, produces a notepad-to-notepad transition, which is the only same-process context switch in the whole category and a good test of whether identity-based coalescing does the right thing. Fifth: sentiment here is genuinely and defensibly negative, 8 of 16 lines, because the frustration is real and caused by the journey's own design rather than acted. That makes this the strongest negative-class contributor in the category and a useful counterweight to the neutral-heavy scripts elsewhere; it also pairs the negative lines to specific known instants, so sentiment timing can be checked and not just sentiment labels. Segmentation: 3 human segments (drafting, interrupted middle, recovery and close) with no DEFAULT_CUES words anywhere in the narration (audited, including bare 'now', 'then', 'first' and 'next'), so this scores the silent fallback path against 22 switch candidates.
journeys.risks:
PRIVACY: high safety by construction. The interrupter is a local script writing invented lines into Notepad; it touches no network, no mailbox, no real notification channel and no real file. This is why a scripted Notepad window was chosen over a genuine toast: a real notification would put real sender content into the golden dataset and would also be indistinguishable in the recording from a privacy incident. The eight interrupt lines are invented and must reference no real person or ticket. Word's recent-documents list is the only leak vector; clear it.
GROUND TRUTH: (a) NEVER PRESS PAUSE. (b) THE BLOCKING RISK is Windows foreground-stealing prevention: a background process is not always permitted to activate a window, and if the script raises Notepad WITHOUT giving it foreground, JEM logs nothing while the screen changes, which silently converts this journey into a weaker duplicate of journey 03 and destroys its entire reason for existing. Setup step 9 exists solely to settle this before recording, and if activation proves unreliable the fallback is to have the script use a method that reliably takes foreground, not to proceed and hope. (c) The stacked interrupt pair at 565 s produces a notepad-to-notepad transition whose exact row sequence depends on how JEM derives ContextIdentity for two windows of the same process; read the actual sequence out of events.csv rather than trusting the expected count, and if same-process windows coalesce into one identity the count drops from 22 to 20. (d) interrupter-log.csv MUST be archived with the session; without it the third-clock payload, which is the most novel thing this journey produces, is simply lost. (e) All windows are dark and none is a full-screen white surface, so flash risk is low, but the Notepad window must be in dark mode or eight white rectangles appear over a dark page and the delta band shifts. (f) Do not pin Notepad to the taskbar; if it can be raised voluntarily the imposed-versus-voluntary distinction is no longer clean.
REPRODUCIBILITY: high, and the highest in the category for the interrupt instants specifically, because they are produced by a script rather than by a human. The voluntary switches and the typing volume vary between takes in the usual way, but the eight imposed events land at the same offsets every time and carry their own timestamps.

journeys.title: Word long-form drafting in a single window (the visual/physical dissociation reference case)
apps: ffmpeg (D:\git\jem\vendor\ffmpeg\ffmpeg.exe) as a SEPARATE audio-only recorder on DISPLAY2
journeys.setup:
COMMON RIG applies (full text in category_notes) — in particular the SEPARATE AUDIO RECORDER, because JEM captures no audio at all. Read category_notes before the first take of the day.

JOURNEY SPECIFIC: Scenario = 'office-content-01-word-longform'. Create D:\golden\office-content-01\ containing outline.txt and narration.txt. outline.txt holds a six-bullet outline for fictional release notes titled 'Northwind Trace 2.4' (a wholly invented internal tool; no real product, customer, vendor or person is named anywhere). narration.txt holds the 19 narration lines below, one per line, in order, in a large font so they can be read at a glance — keep it OPEN ON DISPLAY2 so reading it produces no DISPLAY1 events. Open outline.txt in Notepad++ with the Obsidian theme active (Settings > Style Configurator > Select theme: Obsidian) and confirm the editor background is dark. In Word: File > New > Blank document, then immediately File > Save a Copy / Save As to D:\golden\office-content-01\release-notes-draft.docx so the title bar is stable for the whole take; set AutoSave OFF (no OneDrive); View tab > Dark Mode ON so the page canvas is dark grey rather than white; set zoom to 120%; close every other Word document so no other window can steal focus or churn the title. Clear Word's recent-documents list (File > Options > Advanced > Display > 'Show this number of Recent Documents' = 0) before recording. Leave AutoCorrect at Windows defaults. Maximise Word and Notepad++ on DISPLAY1. PRE-FLIGHT: take a screenshot of both windows and confirm no large white region exists in either; a light page canvas at 120% zoom can push mean frame luma over the 245 flash threshold and make the whole take unscoreable.

steps.action: Confirm the audio ffmpeg on DISPLAY2 is already running and printing a growing 'size=' line. Then press Start in JEM on DISPLAY2. A full-screen white flash appears on DISPLAY1. Clap once, hard and short, at the instant the screen goes white.
steps.produces: sync_flash row and session start anchor in session.json; the clap transient in narration.wav is the ONLY thing that ties the separately-recorded audio to the video, so it is load-bearing, not decorative

steps.action: Hands off keyboard and mouse until the flash has cleared and the desktop is stable.
steps.produces: the leading recorder-noise window; JEM's own flash window is a Jem.App.exe context span ON DISPLAY1, which jem_eval drops by process name, so it must not contain journey events

steps.action: Click once in the body of the Word window on DISPLAY1.
steps.produces: opens the FIRST customer-app context span (process WINWORD.EXE). Note: this is not a Jem.App.exe -> WINWORD.EXE transition in the scored data, because jem_eval filters jem.app.exe rows out entirely. 1 left click row with monitor-relative x,y.

steps.action: Type the heading 'Northwind Trace 2.4 release notes' and press Enter.
steps.produces: ~36 keypress rows: ~31 alphanumeric, 1 whitespace (Enter), ~3 modifier (Shift held for capitals; JEM suppresses auto-repeat so a held Shift is ONE row). Essentially no JAMS-visible luma delta.

steps.action: Type the 60-word summary paragraph from outline.txt continuously, without stopping to correct.
steps.produces: sustained burst of ~365 keypress rows over ~70 s; frame-to-frame band-max delta from growing dark-on-dark text stays far below the 9.6 low-response candidate floor (min_content_val 12.0 x low_response_candidate_floor_factor 0.8) — the core dissociation beat

steps.action: Press Alt+Tab once to bring Notepad++ forward.
steps.produces: context span #2 opens (notepad++.exe). 2 keypress rows: Alt (modifier) + Tab (navigation). This is the main source of navigation-category keys in this journey.

steps.action: Scroll the outline down five wheel notches in one continuous sweep lasting about 1.5 s, then take hands off and read for six seconds without touching anything.
steps.produces: ONE scroll row (t_start = first notch, t_end = last notch, value_num = 5, value_text = down). Over 400 ms so it should also be visible to the JAMS scrolls provider at PROXY_FPS 5. The six-second dwell is a true zero-activity window.

steps.action: Press Alt+Tab to return to Word.
steps.produces: context span #3 opens (WINWORD.EXE)

steps.action: Type the second body paragraph, about 70 words, from outline.txt, letting roughly fifteen genuine typos stand and correcting them with Backspace as you go.
steps.produces: ~440 keypress rows over ~85 s, of which ~15 are editing-category (Backspace)

steps.action: Press Enter, type a hyphen then a space to trigger Word's bullet autoformat, then type six bullet lines of fixed-defect descriptions, pressing Enter between each.
steps.produces: ~340 keypress rows. The bullet autoformat causes a small left-margin reflow — a labelled low-delta layout-change probe that JAMS may or may not see.

steps.action: Press Alt+Tab to Notepad++ for a second reference check.
steps.produces: context span #4 opens (notepad++.exe)

steps.action: Scroll down four notches in one sweep, then hands off and read for six seconds.
steps.produces: second scroll row; second true dwell window

steps.action: Press Alt+Tab back to Word.
steps.produces: context span #5 opens (WINWORD.EXE)

steps.action: Type five more bullet lines continuing the defect list.
steps.produces: ~280 keypress rows

steps.action: Apply Heading 2 to the three section headings ONE AT A TIME: click anywhere in the first heading line, click Heading 2 in the Home ribbon Styles gallery; repeat for the second and third heading. (Do NOT attempt Ctrl+click multi-select — in Word Ctrl+click selects a sentence, not a line, so the original multi-select instruction is not performable as written.)
steps.produces: 6 click rows and a genuine mid-frame visual reflow with NO window change and NO title change. JEM records the clicks but no context_switch, so any JAMS context_switch in this window is a labelled expected false positive.

steps.action: Type the closing paragraph, about 50 words.
steps.produces: ~300 keypress rows

steps.produces: four separate scroll rows, because the 1.5 s gaps exceed hooks.scroll_idle_close_ms (800 ms). Page content translates coherently, which the JAMS context_switch phase-correlation post-filter should suppress as translation-like.

steps.action: Hands off the keyboard and mouse. Do not touch anything.
steps.produces: clean tail with no journey events before the recorder noise

steps.action: Move to DISPLAY2, press Save in JEM, and clap once at the instant the closing white flash appears on DISPLAY1. Then press q in the audio ffmpeg terminal to close narration.wav cleanly.
steps.produces: end_flash_log_ms anchor plus the second clap. Two claps give a two-point linear fit that cancels both constant offset and USB-clock drift between the audio recorder and the video recorder.

narration.line: I have a blank Word document open and the page is in dark mode.
I am typing the heading for the Northwind Trace release notes.
The words are coming out easily, which is a real relief.
I need to check my outline, so I am switching to the text editor.

Back in Word I am writing the second body paragraph.
This keyboard feels great for long stretches of writing.
The cursor is sitting at the end of the second paragraph.

journeys.expected_physical: ~1,800 keypress rows: roughly 1,480 alphanumeric, 230 whitespace (Enter/Space), 50 editing (Backspace), 30 modifier and 8 navigation (the four Alt+Tab Tabs and a few arrows). ~8 left clicks. 6 scroll rows (two in Notepad++ of 4-5 notches, four in Word during the read-back). Click-to-keypress ratio about 1 to 225, the most typing-dominant journey in the corpus.
journeys.stresses: The category's reference case for deliberate dissociation between visual and physical signal. For roughly seven of the nine minutes the screen shows a dark Word page with text slowly growing on it, so the grayscale band-max delta stays far below the 9.6 low-response candidate floor and JAMS should emit almost nothing visually while JEM records ~1,800 gold keypresses. Every context_switch JAMS emits during a typing stretch is therefore a clean, unambiguous false positive against JEM truth, which makes this the best journey in the corpus for measuring context_switch precision on a low-delta background. Second, it is the designated NO-CUE segmentation stratum: the 19 narration lines have been re-checked word by word against DEFAULT_CUES using the same word-boundary regex _matches_cue applies, and contain zero matches for first / starting / to start / get started / next / okay next / moving on / now / then / after that / done / finished / complete / that is it / finally. (The earlier draft's closing line 'the draft is finished' would have matched the done cue and has been rewritten.) Segmentation must therefore fall back entirely to scene boundaries; the prediction is gross under-segmentation, one or two segments against six human-meaningful ones, and that gap is the measurement. Third, narration is deliberately sparse at about 23 words per minute, comfortably below the point at which the spoken_word lane pins to its ceiling, so the physical component of the effort score can actually vary. Fourth, the customer-span rate of 0.56 per minute is far below the rate at which the cognitive lane saturates, so the score can respond to detector changes. Fifth, the two Notepad++ scrolls and the four Word read-back scrolls give paired scroll truth on a low-delta page.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: all content is invented ('Northwind Trace 2.4'); no real product, customer, employee, vendor or credential data appears. No cloud sign-in, AutoSave off, no OneDrive. Word's recent-documents list is set to zero and unrelated documents are closed so no real filename reaches the video. privacy.capture_key_text stays FALSE so typed text does not also land in the plaintext CSV. The microphone is live for the entire take: nobody else should be in the room and nothing else should be audible. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: if Word Dark Mode is not actually on, a light page canvas at 120% zoom can exceed the 245 mean-luma flash threshold and the session becomes unscoreable with 'sync alignment ambiguous' — verify visually before Start and run flash detection on the MP4 immediately after Save rather than discovering it hours later. If AutoSave is left on, or another document is open, Word's title bar churns and NAMECHANGE coalescing adds unplanned context_switch rows; always count switches from events.csv rather than trusting the predicted number. CORRECTED CLAIM: the earlier draft said to 'rely on ffmpeg muxing both streams in one process for the real A/V anchor'. That is impossible — JEM's ffmpeg invocation has no audio input at all, and its config has no audio keys. Audio comes from a second, independent ffmpeg process and the claps are the only alignment fiducial, so a missed or soft clap costs the whole take's sentiment and transcription ground truth. REPRODUCIBILITY: keep AutoCorrect at defaults and use the identical outline.txt, otherwise the keypress and editing-key counts shift between takes. A second take will differ in typing speed by 10-20%, so compare key-category proportions rather than absolute counts.

journeys.title: PowerPoint deck build: heavy in-app visual change that JEM is structurally blind to
journeys.setup:
COMMON RIG applies (category_notes), including the separate audio recorder.

JOURNEY SPECIFIC: Scenario = 'office-content-02-powerpoint-deck'. Create D:\golden\office-content-02\ and put narration.txt there, open on DISPLAY2. Open PowerPoint, File > New, choose the Ion Boardroom design and pick its DARK colour variant, and confirm the slide canvas itself renders dark rather than white — this is mandatory for flash safety because the canvas occupies most of the frame. Immediately Save As D:\golden\office-content-02\quarterly-tooling-review.pptx so the title bar is stable, and set AutoSave OFF. Maximise PowerPoint on DISPLAY1 with the slide thumbnail pane visible on the left and the notes pane closed (View > Notes toggled off). In Edge, open exactly one tab at http://localhost:8080/office-content/rate-card.html, served by 'python -m http.server 8080' run from D:\git\jams\fixtures in a terminal on DISPLAY2, started BEFORE JEM so no terminal switch pollutes the take. In Edge Settings > System and performance, turn OFF 'Show memory usage in tab hover' and any sleeping-tab or performance badge, because Edge's UIA tab name otherwise carries a volatile '- Memory usage - NN MB' decoration that makes JEM emit spurious context switches. Hide the favourites bar and close all other tabs. All deck content is fabricated: an invented internal 'quarterly tooling review' with made-up build times and no real team, tool, vendor or metric.

journeys.expected_physical: ~500 keypress rows in short placeholder-sized bursts of 8 to 45 keys, with an unusually high whitespace and navigation share from Enter and Tab between placeholders and table cells (~380 alphanumeric, ~70 whitespace, ~20 navigation, ~25 modifier). ~45 click rows including 1 right-click, 1 double-click (which JEM writes as 2 rows) and 2 press-drag-release moves that JEM writes as single click rows with no movement. 2 scroll rows in Edge. The most click-dominant journey in the category, the inverse of office-content-01.
journeys.stresses: This journey quantifies the label-noise asymmetry that makes context_switch precision of 1.000 on the old browser-calibration session weak evidence of a clean detector. PowerPoint repaints the entire slide canvas on every Ctrl+M, every layout change and every thumbnail click, all inside one hwnd with an unchanging window title, so JEM logs nothing while JAMS is predicted to fire 15 to 20 times. The truth denominator is deliberately tiny (3 customer spans), so this journey must NOT be scored for recall: it contributes false-positives-per-minute against JEM exposure, and precision against the human visual-label pass, which is the label set the pre-registered precision gate needs and which does not exist anywhere in the corpus today. It is the precise structural mirror of office-content-06, where in-app document switches DO change the window title and JEM therefore sees changes JAMS is likely to miss. It is also the designated ALL-CUE segmentation stratum: a cue phrase opens each of the six slide boundaries at 25 s ('First'), 70 s ('Okay next'), 145 s ('Now'), 220 s ('Moving on'), 310 s ('Then') and 370 s ('After that'), each at least 45 s from its neighbour and therefore far beyond MIN_SEGMENT_MS of 10,000 ms, so all six should survive the greedy merge and the intended cue path is exercised cleanly. (The earlier draft listed these cue times as 21/73/151/229/281/333, which did not match its own narration array; the numbers above are read off the corrected array.) Narration is dense at about 47 words per minute, above the saturation knee, making this a saturated spoken_word exemplar to pair against office-content-01's 23 wpm. The Format Shape pane slide-in and the layout gallery flyout are large transient overlays that test whether the phase-correlation post-filter suppresses a sliding pane.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: the deck is entirely fabricated — invented build times, invented tool names, no real team, vendor, customer or metric. No account sign-in, AutoSave off. Verify no other PowerPoint file is open so the recent-files pane does not expose real filenames. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: a light PowerPoint design theme would put a near-white slide canvas across most of the frame and trip the 245 mean-luma flash detector, destroying the session with 'sync alignment ambiguous' — confirm the dark design variant visually before Start. Edge's memory-usage tab badge must be off or JEM will emit spurious context switches from volatile UIA tab names. The Ctrl+M repaints at 70, 148, 225, 312 and 366 s are all more than three seconds apart, so none are lost to the 2.0 s min_gap_seconds floor; do not compress them if the take runs long. REPRODUCIBILITY: PowerPoint's autofit behaviour differs between templates, so a second take must use the same Ion Boardroom dark variant; a different template changes both the click count and the visual-delta profile. The thumbnail click-through must hold each slide for a full three seconds — clicking faster collapses several true visual transitions into one detectable event and corrupts the false-positive-rate measurement. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: because JEM cannot see any slide change, this journey's JAMS false positives are expected and correct behaviour for a real customer, not detector defects; they must be reported against human visual labels and never folded into a JEM-only F1.

journeys.title: Excel row-wise data entry: the navigation-key and paired long/short scroll probe
journeys.setup:
COMMON RIG applies (category_notes), including the separate audio recorder.

JOURNEY SPECIFIC: Scenario = 'office-content-03-excel-entry'. Create D:\golden\office-content-03\ with narration.txt and source-data.txt (the twenty synthetic rows to key in), both open on DISPLAY2. Open Excel, create a blank workbook and immediately Save As D:\golden\office-content-03\project-hours.xlsx with AutoSave OFF so the title bar is stable. In Edge open one tab at http://localhost:8080/office-content/rate-card.html, served by 'python -m http.server 8080' from D:\git\jams\fixtures, started from a terminal on DISPLAY2 BEFORE JEM. Turn off Edge's memory-usage tab badge, hide the favourites bar, close all other tabs. journeys.expected_physical: ~1,000 keypress rows with by far the highest NAVIGATION SHARE in the corpus: roughly 780 alphanumeric (including all number-pad digits, which JEM maps to alphanumeric), 30 whitespace, 70 navigation (60 Tabs from the row-wise rhythm plus the Ctrl+arrow walks), 25 editing and 50 modifier — about 7% navigation against roughly 0.5% in office-content-01 and 0% in the existing calibration session. ~35 click rows, including two click-drag range selections that JEM records as single click rows. 10 scroll rows deliberately split into 6 long sustained sweeps of 2 to 4 seconds and 4 sub-200-millisecond single-notch flicks. NOTE: the earlier draft claimed ~2,600 keypresses with 380 navigation and 420 whitespace; those numbers were roughly five times the content actually being typed and the navigation figure was unreachable with the column-wise entry pattern it specified. The entry pattern has been changed from column-wise (Enter per cell) to row-wise (Tab across, Enter at row end) specifically so the navigation coverage the journey exists to provide is actually produced, and the counts above are derived from the twenty rows of source-data.txt.
journeys.stresses: Three things this journey is the only source of. First, navigation-key coverage: the prior 825-keypress session contained ZERO navigation-category keys, so JEM's navigation taxonomy has never been exercised on real data; the row-wise Tab rhythm plus the Ctrl+arrow walks produce about 70 navigation rows against roughly 780 alphanumeric, giving the first meaningful distribution across four of the five key categories. Second, the corpus's only designed PAIRED SCROLL PROBE: four sub-200-millisecond single-notch flicks that JEM records perfectly and the JAMS scrolls provider is predicted to miss entirely (it needs two consecutive proxy frames at PROXY_FPS 5), set against six long two-to-four-second sweeps it should detect. That pairing turns scrolls from an untested provider into a measurable one, and scrolls is the only physical provider with a plausible path to JEM-scoreable accuracy today, which is the concrete justification for extending jem_eval with an interval-IoU scroll matcher. Third, the long sweeps are coherent whole-frame translation and should be suppressed by the context_switch phase-correlation post-filter; if they leak through as context switches, that reproduces exactly the scroll false positive that killed the min_content_val=4 variant, on labelled data this time. The Format Cells modal, the twenty-cell fill-down, the chart insert and the chart drag are four large in-app visual changes with no JEM switch, adding controlled false-positive material. At twelve minutes and 3072x1728 this is also the journey that validates jem_eval's 120-second flash-decode and 300-second CFR-normalisation subprocess caps before the rest of the corpus is recorded. Segmentation stratum: PARTIAL CUES — exactly three of the eight human task boundaries carry a cue word ('First' at 36 s, 'Now' at 296 s, 'Finally' at 580 s) and the other five carry none, so this measures cue recall against a mixed background, a condition neither office-content-01 (no cues) nor office-content-02 (all cues) produces. Narration sits at about 31 words per minute, below the saturation knee.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: every task name, owner label, hour value and rate band is invented; no real project, client, employee, salary or financial data appears. No sign-in, AutoSave off, no OneDrive. Confirm no other workbook is open so the recent-files list does not expose real filenames, and close any Excel add-in panes that display account identity. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: Excel's grid is white by default and this is the highest flash risk in the category. Office Black theme plus a maximised window gives roughly 18% dark chrome and mean luma near 213, which is safe, but if the theme reverts to Colorful, or the window is made borderless or full-screen, the margin collapses and the session fails with 'sync alignment ambiguous'. Screenshot and check before Start, and run flash detection on the MP4 immediately after Save. The four fast flicks must be at least 2.5 s apart or the 800 ms scroll-idle-close rule merges them into one span and destroys the negative probe. No long sweep or flick may straddle a context switch, because ScrollAggregator closes an open span when the context identity changes, which would split a truth row mid-sweep. REPRODUCIBILITY: NumLock must be ON. With it off, VK_NUMPAD0-9 arrive as VK_HOME/VK_END/arrow codes and JEM categorises them navigation, which silently inverts the entire key-category profile between takes — check the NumLock LED before Start and note it in the session notes. Excel's slash-to-date conversion depends on the Windows regional format, so record the locale; on a locale where 3/4 does not convert, the Format Cells beat produces no visible change and must be reported as not-fired rather than quietly dropped. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: JAMS emits scrolls as percent-of-viewport while JEM emits wheel-notch counts; only the span timing is directly comparable, and any value comparison needs a declared unit reconciliation or must be dropped from scoring.

journeys.title: Form fill with a paired dual-visible / JEM-blind validation probe
apps: localhost fixture server (python -m http.server 8080 from D:\git\jams\fixtures)
journeys.setup:
COMMON RIG applies (category_notes), including the separate audio recorder.

JOURNEY SPECIFIC: Scenario = 'office-content-04-form-fill'. This journey needs THREE new, version-controlled fixture pages under D:\git\jams\fixtures\office-content\, built in the same dark style as the existing D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\index.html (background #142d44, text #f5f7fb):
(a) intake-form.html — fourteen fields: contact name, organisation, email, phone, address line, city, postcode, a country select, project name, a budget select, a date field, a 150-character description textarea, two checkboxes, and a submit button.
(b) blocked.html — the PROBE A target: dark #663c28 background, <title>Submission blocked | Intake fixture</title>, an error summary and a 'Back to form' link pointing at intake-form.html.
(c) confirmed.html — dark #244831 background, <title>Submission received | Intake fixture</title>.
CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE EARLIER DESIGN: PROBE A must be a REAL SAME-TAB NAVIGATION to blocked.html, not an in-page view swap with a document.title assignment. JEM's Edge ContextIdentity is (msedge.exe, address-bar URL) whenever Edge's UIA address bar resolves to an absolute http URL, and only falls back to the parsed tab TITLE when it does not. An in-page title change with an unchanged URL therefore produces a context_switch on one resolution path and NOTHING on the other, which is exactly the non-determinism that would make the paired probe unscoreable. A real navigation changes the URL AND the window title, so identity changes under both paths. The existing jem-journeys fixture uses the in-page pattern and must NOT be copied here.
PROBE B (JAMS-only, JEM-blind) stays in-page: blurring the phone field with a malformed value reveals an inline validation banner about 200 pixels tall in the top sixth of the viewport that persists, touching NEITHER document.title NOR location (no hash, no query, no pushState). JEM must record nothing, so any JAMS context_switch at that timestamp is a controlled, pre-declared expected false positive. Fire PROBE B twice, each at least three seconds clear of any PROBE A event.
Serve with 'python -m http.server 8080' from D:\git\jams\fixtures in a terminal on DISPLAY2, started BEFORE JEM. Turn off Edge's memory-usage tab badge, hide the favourites bar, close all other tabs, use a clean Edge profile. Maximise Edge on DISPLAY1. Put narration.txt on DISPLAY2.
MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT (do this with JEM recording a throwaway 60-second session, then read events.csv): trigger PROBE A once and confirm a context_switch row appears; trigger PROBE B twice and confirm NO context_switch row appears. If either check fails, fix the fixture before recording the real take — the journey has no scientific value otherwise.
Every value typed is synthetic: 'Dana Fictional', 'Northwind Trace Pilot', an RFC 5737 documentation-style address, and an email on the reserved .invalid top-level domain so it can never be delivered anywhere.

journeys.expected_physical: ~330 keypress rows in fourteen short field-sized bursts of 8 to 40 keys separated by Tab, giving the densest burst-boundary structure in the category (the JAMS keypresses provider splits bursts at 800 ms, so this journey directly tests that split rule against JEM's per-key truth). Navigation share about 6%: roughly 20 Tab presses, not the 90 the earlier draft claimed — there are only fourteen fields and one Tab between each. ~14 click rows. 3 scroll rows, one inside a native dropdown.
journeys.stresses: The most surgical measurement in the category and the shortest journey, so it is cheap to re-record if a take fails. It carries the corpus's only pre-registered PAIRED PROBE: PROBE A is a real same-tab navigation visible to BOTH tools (URL change, title change, large luma delta), PROBE B is a 200-pixel in-page banner visible ONLY to JAMS (no title, no location, no navigation). Firing both twice inside four minutes, more than three seconds apart, isolates the question that cannot currently be answered: how much of JAMS's apparent false-positive rate is genuine in-page transition that JEM is structurally blind to, rather than detector error. Without this controlled pairing every precision number against JEM proxy labels is uninterpretable. The design only works because PROBE A was changed from an in-page title swap to a real navigation — JEM's Edge identity is the address-bar URL when UIA resolves it and the parsed tab title when it does not, so a title-only change fires on one path and not the other and the pair would have collapsed into noise. Second, it is the designated CUE-AS-DISTRACTOR segmentation stratum: the cue words 'then' and 'after that' appear mid-line at 24, 94 and 192 seconds where there is NO real task boundary, while the two genuine boundaries at 150 and 220 seconds carry no cue word at all. That inversion measures the segmentation cue false-positive rate directly, which no existing recording does. Third, narration runs at about 60 words per minute, the densest in the category and well above the saturation knee, giving a clearly saturated spoken_word exemplar at the opposite end from office-content-01's 23 wpm. Fourth, serving over http rather than file:// is the only way Edge's UIA address bar can yield an absolute http URL at all, which no prior recording achieved.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: nothing real is entered. The email uses the reserved .invalid top-level domain so it can never resolve or be delivered; the address is documentation-style; the name and organisation are invented. No credentials, no payment details, no account. The fixture is local and static and submits nothing over any network — it is entirely client-side, so no data leaves the machine even when Submit is pressed. Edge's tab strip, favourites bar and profile avatar can expose personal context on camera: hide the favourites bar, close all other tabs and use a clean Edge profile. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: the fixture MUST keep a dark background in every state including blocked.html and confirmed.html, because a near-white full-viewport page would trip the 245 mean-luma flash detector and abort the whole evaluation. PROBE B must genuinely touch neither document.title nor location — verify this in the mandatory pre-flight by reading events.csv, not by watching the tab caption, because a pushState or hash assignment changes the address-bar value without changing the visible caption and would silently collapse the paired design into two identical probes. PROBE A at 146 s and the return navigation at 166 s are 20 s apart, comfortably beyond min_gap_seconds; do not compress them. REPRODUCIBILITY: all three fixture pages must be committed to the repo so a second take uses byte-identical markup; an ad-hoc regenerated page shifts the banner height and changes the luma delta. Native select dropdown rendering is Edge-version-dependent, so record the Edge version in the session notes. KNOWN FRAGILITY: JEM's Edge URL enrichment is documented as brittle across Edge updates and the omnibox ValuePattern may return a scheme-less string such as 'localhost:8080/...', which EdgeUrlParser.TryGetHttpHost rejects; the journey is designed to survive that by changing the title as well, but the detail field's contents must be reported as observed rather than assumed.

journeys.title: Screenshot capture and annotation: drag-heavy, keypress-light, four-app hop
journeys.setup:
COMMON RIG applies (category_notes), including the separate audio recorder.

JOURNEY SPECIFIC: Scenario = 'office-content-05-screenshot-annotate'. This journey needs one new version-controlled fixture at D:\git\jams\fixtures\office-content\capture-target.html, in the same dark style as the jem-journeys fixture: a dark page carrying a summary card with one large fabricated headline number and three short supporting lines, tall enough that two wheel notches move it meaningfully. Serve it at http://localhost:8080/office-content/capture-target.html via 'python -m http.server 8080' from D:\git\jams\fixtures, started from a terminal on DISPLAY2 BEFORE JEM.

journeys.expected_physical: ~260 keypress rows, the lightest keyboard load in the category (~205 alphanumeric, ~15 whitespace, ~8 navigation from the Alt+Tab Tabs, ~28 modifier from the six Ctrl and two Win+Shift combinations, ~4 editing). ~14 click rows, THREE of which are complete press-drag-release gestures that JEM reduces to one row each: two snip rectangles and one text selection. 5 scroll rows. The defining ratio is that the three most visually dramatic gestures in the journey (two snip drags and five annotation strokes) produce only 8 JEM rows between them.
journeys.stresses: The corpus's drag-heavy, keypress-light extreme and its only four-application journey, so it carries the highest customer-span rate at about 1.8 per minute against office-content-01's 0.56. Three things it uniquely provides. First, the Win+Shift+S overlay is a genuine FULL-FRAME luma change that coincides exactly with a real JEM context switch — an aligned positive control, which the corpus otherwise lacks entirely because every other large visual change here is deliberately JEM-invisible. Without at least one aligned event, a detector that fires on nothing at all would score identically to a good one on precision. Second, it concentrates JEM's documented drag blind spot: two snip rectangles and one text selection, each a multi-second gesture producing exactly one click row at the press point (the low-level hook writes WM_LBUTTONDOWN only and never logs movement or button-up), so physical-effort ground truth systematically UNDER-counts the work done, and that under-count is measurable here rather than merely asserted. Third, the two Ctrl+V pastes are the largest instantaneous frame deltas in the whole category with no window change and no title change, giving the cleanest possible JAMS-only material at a precisely known timestamp. Segmentation stratum: CUES TOO CLOSE TOGETHER — the narration deliberately places no cue words at all near the six human boundaries but that is incidental; what this journey tests is the greedy merge under a high scene-boundary density, since eleven real context switches in under six minutes will feed many switch-derived boundaries into the union and several fall inside MIN_SEGMENT_MS of each other. The prediction is that the 10-second floor merges genuinely distinct tasks, and the size of that over-merge is the measurement. Narration is 17 lines at about 38 words per minute, just under the saturation knee, which is the third distinct point on the density curve after office-content-01 and office-content-04.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: the fixture card holds one fabricated headline number and three invented supporting lines; no real metric, customer or person appears. The Snipping Tool captures only a region of the fixture page, never the taskbar, never another window, and never a file dialog showing unrelated paths. Set Word's Recent Documents to zero and close all other Edge tabs. The microphone is live throughout. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION AND KNOWN FRAGILITY: the capture overlay and Snipping Tool editor process names are Windows-build dependent and a protected surface may resolve as 'unknown' unless JEM is running elevated; the mandatory pre-flight exists to record what this build actually emits, and expected_context_switches of 11 must be treated as an estimate to be reconciled against events.csv rather than a target. Paint is excluded on purpose for flash safety — do not substitute it. The Save As dialog in step 122 is a separate top-level window and may or may not be attributed to the Snipping Tool process depending on build; count the spans it produces from the CSV. REPRODUCIBILITY: the two snip rectangles must be drawn slowly enough (about one second each) that the growing selection spans at least five proxy frames at PROXY_FPS 5, otherwise the JAMS-visible half of the drag probe does not exist and only the JEM-invisible half is measured. Annotation stroke shapes will differ between takes, so compare stroke COUNTS and click-row counts, never pixel deltas. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: this journey should not be used for context_switch precision, because eleven real switches in six minutes give JAMS many genuinely correct firings; use office-content-02 for precision on a sparse-truth background and this one for recall on a dense-truth background.

journeys.expected_physical: ~620 keypress rows (~500 alphanumeric, ~25 whitespace, ~20 navigation from the eleven Tab presses in the Ctrl+Tab combinations, ~55 modifier from those same combinations plus Ctrl+F6 and Ctrl+Shift+S, ~20 editing). ~5 click rows only — the second-lightest mouse load in the category after office-content-01. 2 scroll rows. The distinguishing shape is a very high modifier share (about 9%) from the switching shortcuts, against roughly 2% elsewhere.
journeys.stresses: This is the precise structural mirror of office-content-02 and the journey that finally gives context_switch RECALL a real denominator. Fourteen genuine JEM context switches in eight minutes, of which ten are IN-APP document changes that alter only the window title and a small amount of body text: two near-identical dark Markdown files or two near-identical dark Word briefs. The visual delta across those transitions is predicted to sit below the 9.6 low-response candidate floor (min_content_val 12.0 x low_response_candidate_floor_factor 0.8), so JAMS should miss most of them, and every miss is a clean false negative against unambiguous JEM truth. Nothing else in the corpus can produce that: office-content-02 has a truth denominator of three and is scored for precision only, and office-content-01's five switches are all Alt+Tab process changes that any detector gets right. Four beats here are process changes and serve as the in-journey aligned control, so a detector that simply fires more often cannot win by accident — it would have to gain on the ten hard in-app cases without losing the four easy ones. The double Ctrl+Tab at 200 s is a designed recall-suppression probe with a pre-declared ceiling: two real switches one second apart cannot both survive min_gap_seconds of 2.0, so 50% recall on that pair is the best any tuning can achieve and it must be excluded from any claim that recall is improvable. The same logical transition is performed twice by different modalities (Ctrl+F6 at 274 s, View > Switch Windows at 356 s) to separate 'detected the document change' from 'detected the menu flyout'. Segmentation stratum: DONE-FAMILY CUES ONLY — the lines at 440 s ('I am done with this pass') and 456 s ('the work is complete') are the corpus's only exercise of the done branch of DEFAULT_CUES, which nothing else in the category touches, and they sit 16 seconds apart, just above MIN_SEGMENT_MS, so the merge behaviour at the floor is tested too. Narration is 19 lines at about 30 words per minute.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: all five Markdown files and both Word briefs are invented release-planning notes for a fictional tool; no real product, customer, employee or vendor appears. If the Notepad++ title bar is set to show full paths then D:\golden\office-content-06\... lands in events.csv value_text and on camera, which is acceptable, but confirm no unrelated files are open in either app. Recent Documents set to zero in Word. The microphone is live throughout. GROUND-TRUTH INVALIDATION: the entire journey depends on the window title actually changing on every in-app switch. If Notepad++ is configured to show only the application name, or if Word is in a single-window mode where Ctrl+F6 does not change the title, JEM emits nothing and the journey has no truth at all — this is what the mandatory pre-flight checks, and it must be repeated after any Notepad++ or Office update. Unsaved-change markers (the asterisk or red icon) also alter the title, so an incidental save or autosave mid-take can insert unplanned context_switch rows; always count from events.csv. Keep the files dark-themed and similar in layout, because if they differ visually the journey stops being a recall stress and becomes an easy case. REPRODUCIBILITY: the double Ctrl+Tab at 200 s must be about one second apart — if it drifts beyond two seconds the suppression probe ceases to be a suppression probe and silently becomes two ordinary switches, which would make a tuning run look like it had improved recall when nothing changed. Use a metronome or count it deliberately. MEASUREMENT CAVEAT: the ten in-app switches are proxy labels for visual context derived from foreground-and-title spans, not human task-boundary annotations, and must be reported separately from the human annotation pass per the evaluation matrix. A JAMS miss here is a genuine detector limitation, not label noise, which is exactly why this journey and office-content-02 must always be reported as a pair — neither number means anything on its own.

journeys.title: Cold start in VS Code: editing a small site for the first time
journeys.setup: GLOBAL SETUP v2 (applies to every journey in this category; stated here in full, referenced by the others). AUDIO — this is the corrected part, the original plan was unworkable. JEM records SILENT video and cannot be clapped into sync: its flash is 300 ms and fires 500 ms after Start, which no human can hit reliably. JEM already ships the right mechanism. Edit jem.config.json and set sync.sync_tone=true, sync.sync_tone_hz=1000, sync.sync_tone_ms=150, sync.end_flash=true, capture.record_video=true, capture.scale=1.0, capture.fps=30, privacy.capture_key_text=false, and leave hooks at defaults (scroll_idle_close_ms=800, namechange_quiet_ms=200, foreground_resolve_timeout_ms=200). JEM then plays a 1 kHz 150 ms tone at the instant it paints each flash. DO NOT WEAR HEADPHONES — the tone must reach the microphone or there is no anchor. Use desktop speakers at a normal conversational level. NO CLAPS ANYWHERE. Capture narration as a separate file: get the device string once with `ffmpeg -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy`, then BEFORE pressing JEM Start run `ffmpeg -f dshow -i audio="<device>" -ac 1 -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_s16le D:\jem-scratch\audio\<scenario>.wav` and leave it running until AFTER JEM Save, so both tones are inside the WAV. After the take: `python -m capture.audio_align align --video <jem>.mp4 --audio <scenario>.wav` (expect two anchors, residual well under 20 ms, drift under a few hundred ppm), then `python -m capture.audio_align mux --video <jem>.mp4 --audio <scenario>.wav --out <scenario>-muxed.mp4`. The MUXED file is what gets uploaded to JAMS; the raw JEM mp4 is silent and would make the transcription and sentiment providers skip. JEM HANDOFF — JEM does not minimise itself, so jem.app.exe IS the foreground window when you press Start. Every journey therefore begins with an explicit beat that brings the first application forward; that leading jem.app.exe span is dropped by jem_eval (it filters process=='jem.app.exe') and neither it nor the transition out of it is scored. The same applies at the end when you click back to JEM to press Save. MONITOR — one monitor for the whole take, the one JEM is recording. JEM drops clicks and scrolls whose coordinates fall outside the selected monitor rect but CANNOT drop keypresses (they carry no coordinates), so a stray keystroke on a second monitor silently contaminates the physical ground truth. Nothing goes on the second monitor at all. SPACING — separate scroll bursts by at least 1.5 s (scroll_idle_close_ms is 800 ms) so each burst becomes its own JEM scroll span, and separate any two intended context switches by at least 5 s (JAMS's context_switch detector has a 2.0 s min_gap, so closer switches are a harness artifact, not a detector defect). DISPLAY — Windows dark mode, taskbar visible and not auto-hidden, Do-not-disturb on, Teams/Zoom/Discord closed so nothing steals the microphone. Nothing light-coloured may ever fill the screen: JEM's flash detector looks for near-white full frames and a stray light theme makes the session unscoreable. Edge: dark theme, new-tab page set to Custom with content off, and the tab-hover memory-usage badge OFF (its mutating UIA text emits spurious context_switch rows). One unbroken take, never Pause. JOURNEY-SPECIFIC. Create D:\jem-scratch\hello-site with three pre-authored synthetic files: index.html (title 'Hello site', body background #12181f, an h1, one paragraph, a <link> to styles.css), styles.css (about 40 lines, body{background:#12181f}, deliberately unsorted), notes.md (one '# Notes' heading and nothing else). Edge must be the Windows default browser (the File Explorer double-click beat depends on it). VS Code: a profile named 'JEM-Subject' reset to defaults, Dark Modern, no folder open, Welcome page enabled, integrated terminal closed, pinned to the taskbar. Edge: one tab on https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Structuring_content with the MDN theme switcher set to Dark, maximised, no other tabs, no profile or sync banner visible. PRE-FLIGHT (60 s throwaway JEM session, then read events.csv): (a) confirm VS Code's window title gains a leading bullet when a file is dirty and loses it on save — the default window.title template includes ${dirty}, so each edit/save pair emits TWO extra JEM context_switch rows, and the predicted count below assumes it; if this machine's template has been customised, re-predict before recording rather than recording blind. (b) Confirm https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/named-color resolves; if MDN has moved it, pin whatever it redirects to and type that literal instead. (c) Confirm Edge context_switch rows carry detail=uia:<full https url>.

journeys.expected_physical: About 22 click rows (20 left, 1 right, and the double-click counts as 2 MouseButtonDown rows), roughly 310 non-modifier keypress rows across five typing bursts (80 / 50 / 13 / 140 plus shortcut keys), and 7 scroll spans totalling about 35 notches. Modifier rows (Ctrl, Shift, Alt) are emitted by JEM with key_category set and must be excluded from any physical-effort denominator. Predicted switch count breaks down as: 6 foreground process changes, 9 title changes from navigation or file selection, and 6 dirty/clean title flips from three edit-and-save pairs. Treat the total as 21 plus or minus 2 - the VS Code window reload and Edge's intermediate loading title are the two sources of jitter.
journeys.stresses: Primary target is the context_switch provider's dark-on-dark failure class plus the JEM-blind / CV-visible divergence, and this journey is the anchor for building the human visual-change annotation pass. Nine of the twenty-one JEM switches are VS Code title changes between two dark editor states, and six of those nine are the dirty/clean bullet flips, where the ONLY pixel difference is a bullet glyph in the title bar and tab - far below min_content_val 12.0 and its effective 9.6 floor, so recall on that sub-class is predicted near zero. Simultaneously three large visual events (the command palette overlay, the three-theme live preview cycle, the Ctrl+F5 repaint) and the terminal panel reveal produce NO JEM rows, so any JAMS detection there is a false positive against proxy truth and a true positive against human labels. The journey therefore measures the label-noise asymmetry from both directions inside one take. Secondary: the Ctrl+Tab beat isolates the EVENT_OBJECT_NAMECHANGE path and its 200 ms coalescing lag; the file:// beat is the only Edge span in the category whose identity comes from the tab title rather than the URL, which exercises the fallback path; the 22-second hands-off dwell gives clean zero-motion and zero-speech; the narration plants four real segmentation cues ('let's get started', 'okay next', 'moving on', "that's it") at four genuine task boundaries, making this stratum A for the cue path.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: no credentials, no accounts, no network submission, no personal data. All three edited files are pre-authored synthetic content on a scratch drive; the two MDN pages are public and read-only. Confirm the Edge tab strip is clean and no profile avatar, sync banner or autofill prompt is visible before Start - JEM records the whole screen. REPRODUCIBILITY: MDN revises articles without notice, which shifts scroll extents but not switch structure; the 'JEM-Subject' VS Code profile must be reset to defaults before every take or the Welcome page and theme list differ; delete and recreate hello-site between takes so styles.css starts from the same messy state. GROUND TRUTH, in priority order: (a) the predicted count of 21 depends on VS Code's default ${dirty} window title - run the pre-flight and re-predict rather than record blind if it has been customised; (b) selecting a LIGHT theme by mistake makes the whole session unscoreable via the flash detector, so the palette is restricted to Dark+, Monokai and Abyss; (c) the file:// preview page and the Ctrl+T new-tab page must both render dark for the same reason; (d) an Edge tab-hover memory-usage badge mutates the UIA text and emits spurious context_switch rows that are instrumentation artifacts, not task events - turn it off and verify in the pre-flight; (e) the Open Folder dialog and the File Explorer window must both open on the recorded monitor or JEM's monitor filter drops the foreground event entirely and leaves the previous span wrongly open; (f) if the parallel microphone WAV does not contain exactly two 1 kHz tones, audio_align cannot fit offset and rate and the take must be rerecorded - check with `python -m capture.audio_align tones --audio <file>.wav` before deleting anything.

journeys.title: Checkout flow, two passes: confused first attempt then a clean run
journeys.setup: Apply GLOBAL SETUP v2 from realistic-mixed-01 (sync tone on, speakers not headphones, parallel microphone WAV, no claps, JEM handoff beat, single monitor, 1.5 s scroll gaps, 5 s switch gaps, everything dark). MANDATORY FIXTURE REPAIR - the journey as originally written could not work. fixtures/jem-journeys/index.html is a single-page app that swaps innerHTML and sets document.title but NEVER changes its URL. JEM's Edge branch resolves the address-bar URL first and, when it parses as http(s), uses the FULL URL STRING as the ContextIdentity, ignoring the title entirely. Served unmodified at http://localhost:8080/ the entire six-minute session collapses into ONE context span and yields ZERO ground-truth switches. Before recording, add hash routing to the fixture: give page() a slug argument and set location.hash to it ('#home', '#shop', '#cart', '#receipt', '#onboard', '#welcome', '#fail', '#recovered'). Each page then has a distinct URL, so the identity changes whichever branch JEM takes - by URL if Edge's UIA exposes the full address, by parsed tab title if it exposes a scheme-less one and TryGetHttpHost falls through. Commit that change and pin the fixture at that git revision for the whole corpus; its page colours (#142d44, #24536d, #244831, #4d304c, #663c28) are load-bearing for the luma deltas. SERVE IT: run `python -m http.server 8080` inside D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys, confirm http://localhost:8080/#home loads, then MINIMISE that terminal and do not touch it again for the whole take. Serving over http rather than file:// is deliberate - it makes the Edge UIA enrichment resolve so every context_switch row carries detail=uia:<url> and the ground truth is self-describing. Edge maximized, dark theme, exactly one tab, on the fixture landing page. No other application is touched. SCROLL CAVEAT, correcting the original: every fixture page's content fits on one screen, so there is nothing to scroll. Wheel input still produces JEM scroll rows (they come from the low-level hook, not from the page) but produces ZERO visual change in the video. Two such beats are kept ON PURPOSE as the 'physical input with no video evidence' stratum, which bounds what any video-inferred scroll detector can ever achieve; they are not padding and must not be re-described as ordinary scrolling. PRE-FLIGHT: record a 60 s throwaway session clicking Checkout then Add to cart, and confirm events.csv contains two non-jem context_switch rows with distinct value_text. If it contains one, the hash routing did not take effect and the take is worthless.

narration.line: I'm on the landing page of a test store and I'm going to behave like someone who has never seen it.
There are three big buttons and honestly I have no idea which one is the shop.
I'm clicking the middle one, the checkout one, because that sounds closest to buying something.
Oh good, that is the product page, the workbook is right there.
Twelve dollars, and it says clearly that no actual purchase happens, which I appreciate.
Adding it to the cart, and the page has gone purple on me, which is jarring.
I want to see what cancel does, so I'm clicking cancel instead of checking out.
And it dumped me all the way back to the beginning, which is not what I wanted at all.
I've clicked onboarding by mistake, this is the wrong flow entirely.
It is asking me for a workspace name, which has nothing to do with buying a book.
Going back to the landing page so I can try the shop again.
Product page again, and the button labels are much clearer the second time through.
Adding to cart, reviewing the cart, and the total still reads twelve dollars.
Clicking simulate checkout without reading anything, the way a real shopper would.
The receipt says no charge and no order were created, which is exactly right.
Returning home, and I'll walk the whole thing a second time cleanly.
Shop, add to cart, review, checkout. Four clicks and no surprises.
That was much faster, and the flow itself is genuinely fine once you know where things are.
My only real complaint is that cancel throws away the whole cart without warning.
I'd want a confirmation step there, or at least a way back to the product.
I'm going to stop the walkthrough there.

journeys.expected_physical: About 15 click rows, all left button, all inside the browser viewport. Roughly 18 keypress rows in a single burst (the workspace name field, including one Ctrl+A modifier pair). Three scroll spans totalling about 13 notches, NONE of which move a single pixel on screen. Deliberately the lightest physical load in the category, which makes JEM's click rows cheap to audit by hand against the video frame by frame.
journeys.stresses: This is the single-application, single-window journey: zero foreground process changes, fourteen context switches arriving entirely through the NAMECHANGE and URL-change path on one hwnd. That isolates JEM's 200 ms namechange_quiet_ms coalescing lag as an uncontaminated timing-bias measurement: every switch is caused by a logged click, so click-to-boundary lag is computable directly from events.csv and comparable against JAMS's detection-frame bias. It also stresses segmentation hard - fourteen scene boundaries inside six minutes against four human-meaningful task segments - which forces the MIN_SEGMENT_MS=10000 greedy merge to do real work and exposes the over-segmentation rate. The three no-motion scroll beats are the corpus's only clean measurement of the recall ceiling for video-inferred scroll detection, which is zero by construction. The 'Simulate checkout' to receipt transition is a hue-dominant change at near-constant luma, a known false-negative class, and it appears TWICE in one take so recall on it can be estimated from a single recording. The narration is stratum C for the cue matcher: it contains no deliberate boundary cues, but 'now' at 300 s and 'complete' in ordinary usage are the kind of bare substrings DEFAULT_CUES matches on a word boundary, so this take measures the cue false-positive rate on genuinely cue-free speech. Finally the two-pass structure records every transition type twice within one session, giving a free within-take reproducibility check independent of a second recording.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: the fixture is local, synthetic, and its own banner states that no account, payment or network submission occurs. 'Pilot Study Two' is throwaway text; no real name, card, address or email is typed anywhere. Close every personal Edge tab and confirm no profile avatar or sync prompt is visible before Start. REPRODUCIBILITY: the Python http.server must be up BEFORE Start or every page 404s and the session is worthless - load http://localhost:8080/#home and confirm it renders before pressing Start. The serving terminal stays minimised; alt-tabbing to it mid-take injects a context switch that is an instrumentation artifact. Pin the fixture at the git revision that contains the hash routing, because its page colours determine every luma delta in the predicted results. GROUND TRUTH: (a) without the hash-routing repair this journey produces ONE context span and no usable ground truth at all - the pre-flight exists to catch exactly that, and a take that shows fewer than fourteen non-jem rows must be discarded rather than reinterpreted; (b) clicks closer than three seconds would put two true switches inside JAMS's 2.0 s min_gap and manufacture a structural false negative that is a harness artifact, so the beat spacing above (never under ten seconds) must not be compressed; (c) if Edge's UIA address-bar value ever comes back empty the identity silently falls back to the tab title - the detail column tells you which branch ran, so check it after the take and record which regime applied.

journeys.title: Device setup walkthrough in Windows Settings
journeys.setup: Apply GLOBAL SETUP v2 from realistic-mixed-01. MANDATORY PRE-FLIGHT: record a throwaway 60-second JEM session in which you open Settings and navigate three pages, then read events.csv. This journey's entire premise is that the Windows 11 Settings window title stays literally 'Settings' across in-app page navigation, so JEM logs ONE long span while a human sees a dozen distinct screens. If the pre-flight shows a title change per page, the journey still runs but expected_context_switches must be re-predicted BEFORE recording, not reinterpreted afterwards. Settings is pinned to the taskbar and CLOSED before the take. Edge is open with exactly two tabs already loaded: tab 1 on https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/ and tab 2 on https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/print/, both with the Learn theme switcher set to Dark; tab 1 is the active tab. NOTHING IS CHANGED ON THE MACHINE. No Bluetooth device is paired, no printer added, no toggle flipped. CORRECTION to the original plan: the pointer-size slider in Accessibility applies IMMEDIATELY with no Apply button, so dragging it is a real persistent personalisation change - that beat is removed. Only the TEXT SIZE slider is touched, because it live-previews without applying and is discarded by clicking Back instead of Apply, leaving the machine byte-identical. Confirm Windows dark mode is genuinely applied to Settings before Start (System > Personalisation > Colours), because several Settings surfaces are near-white in light mode and would trip JEM's flash detector.

This documentation is dense and it does not answer my question in the section I landed on.

journeys.stresses: This journey exists to quantify the label-noise asymmetry that makes a single context_switch F1 number meaningless. Windows Settings is a single-window app: NINE genuine full-pane screen replacements happen inside two JEM context spans, so every JAMS detection there scores as a false positive against JEM proxy truth while being a correct detection against human visual labels. Recording it forces the evaluation to grow the second label set that the 2026-09-09 hillclimb already named as the open next step, and this journey should be annotated first because its divergence events are unambiguous and easy for a human to timestamp. It is also the deliberately LOW switch-rate journey at roughly 0.85 switches per minute, which keeps the cognitive lane far from its 2.72/min saturation point - the only journey in the category where that lane can actually move in response to a detector change, and the necessary low-end bracket against realistic-mixed-07's saturating high end. Secondary stresses: the text-size drag proves JEM logs no mouse travel at all, which hard-bounds what any physical-effort provider can ever be validated against; the live text reflow during that drag is a whole-frame change with no JEM row and is the journey's largest false-positive trap; the search dropdown covers about one sixth of the frame and directly tests proxy_motion's band-max amplification; the reflowing card layout during scroll is the ambiguous case where translation-like motion and genuine content change coexist. The narration is stratum B: it contains no deliberate segmentation cues, so all six task boundaries must be recovered from scene boundaries alone with no audio-cue assistance.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: this journey displays system configuration, so the exclusions are strict. The Settings ACCOUNTS page is never opened (it renders the real Microsoft account name and email address). The Network and Wi-Fi pages are never opened. Before Start, confirm no Bluetooth device in the list carries a personal device name and that the printer entry is a generic office printer rather than anything carrying a home address. Nothing is paired, added, signed into or toggled; the text size slider is returned to its exact original value and Back is clicked instead of Apply, so no setting is written. No system or security setting is modified anywhere in this journey. REPRODUCIBILITY: Windows Settings is redesigned between feature updates, so left-rail entries and page layouts shift - record the Windows build number in the session notes. Microsoft Learn articles are revised without notice, which changes scroll extents but not switch structure. The printer's presence and readiness state is machine-specific; if the printer is offline the narration line at 206 s becomes factually false and the take must be rerecorded rather than left mislabelled. GROUND TRUTH: (a) the whole premise fails if Settings does change its title per page - run the mandatory pre-flight and re-predict before recording if it does; (b) if any Settings surface renders near-white the flash detector can fire a phantom flash and abort evaluation, so verify dark mode is genuinely applied before Start; (c) both taskbar excursions must land on the recorded monitor or JEM's monitor filter drops the foreground event and leaves the previous span wrongly open; (d) the live slider preview re-renders all on-screen text with no JEM row behind it, and it WILL look like a large false positive - it must be marked in the human annotation pass or it will be misread as a detector defect and drive a wrong hillclimb decision.

journeys.title: Following a git branching tutorial across editor, terminal and browser
journeys.setup: Apply GLOBAL SETUP v2 from realistic-mixed-01. MANDATORY MECHANISM REPAIR - the original plan's central claim was false. It asserted that JEM turns every terminal command into a ContextIdentity change. It does not. JEM only re-resolves a window's identity on a FOREGROUND change or a window-title NAMECHANGE; there is no periodic re-scrape for terminals. With a stock PowerShell prompt the window title never changes, so nine commands would produce ZERO context_switch rows and the journey's headline stress would not exist. The repair is to make the title track the command. After opening Windows Terminal and cd'ing to the working folder, and BEFORE pressing Start, paste this one line into the session (it is session-scoped, touches no profile script, and disappears when the tab closes): function prompt { $h = Get-History -Count 1; if ($h) { $Host.UI.RawUI.WindowTitle = $h.CommandLine }; "PS $($ExecutionContext.SessionState.Path.CurrentLocation)> " }  — after each command completes the title becomes that command, JEM sees a NAMECHANGE, and BuildTerminalContext resolves an identity. Note the resolution detail: at the moment the title settles the terminal's last line is a fresh empty prompt, so the UIA command scrape returns nothing and JEM falls back to the window title, meaning the detail column will read title:<command> rather than uia:<command>. That is correct behaviour, not a failure, and the original plan's claim that all nine would carry uia: was wrong. WORKING TREE: create D:\jem-scratch\git-demo with exactly two pre-authored synthetic files and NO .git directory - TUTORIAL.md (a ten-step markdown walkthrough of init, commit, branch, merge and conflict resolution, written so the journey runs verbatim with no improvising) and README.md (about fifteen lines of placeholder notes containing one line reading exactly 'Colour tokens: TBD'). DELETE any .git directory from a previous take before every run or the history diverges and the conflict does not reproduce. Set a repo-local identity before Start so no real address is rendered on screen: git config user.name 'JEM Subject' and git config user.email 'subject@example.invalid', then verify with git log in the pre-flight. WINDOWS: VS Code foreground with git-demo open, TUTORIAL.md active, JEM-Subject profile, Dark Modern, integrated terminal CLOSED (this journey uses the separate Windows Terminal app on purpose so app switches are real foreground changes). Windows Terminal behind it, dark scheme, cd'd to D:\jem-scratch\git-demo, with the prompt function already pasted in. Edge behind both, dark theme, one tab on https://github.com/git/git, LOGGED OUT (GitHub follows the system colour scheme for signed-out visitors, and logging out also keeps avatars, usernames and private repo lists off screen). git on PATH. PRE-FLIGHT: confirm (a) the VS Code dirty-title bullet behaviour as in realistic-mixed-01, (b) that running one command in the terminal produces exactly one context_switch row whose value_text is that command.
