narration.line: I've got a tutorial markdown file open and an empty terminal behind it, and I'm going to work through it.
Let's get started with the setup section, which wants me to make a fresh repository.
Typing the init command, and it created the repository without any fuss at all. Good.
Staging everything and committing it with a message.
The output tells me two files changed, which matches what is in the folder. I'm happy with that.
The tutorial says to check the log, so I'm running that.
One commit, a hash, and my configured name on it.
Okay next, the branching section, which is the part I actually care about.
Creating a branch called feature colours and switching onto it.
Back in the editor to change the readme on this branch.
Typing a few colour tokens onto that line, nothing clever.
Saving it, and the sidebar marks the file as modified.
Committing that on the branch, and the message went through cleanly. I like that it just works.
Moving on to the merge section, which is where these tutorials usually go wrong for me.
Switching back to the main branch, and all my colour changes have vanished from the file.
That is expected behaviour and it is still genuinely alarming every single time.
The tutorial wants me to edit the same line on main so there is a conflict.
Committing on main, and running the merge command.
And there it is, an automatic merge failed message in red.
I really dislike conflict markers, they always look far worse than the actual problem is.
Opening the tutorial again to re-read what it says about resolving them.
Both versions are in the file with the arrows and the equals signs between them.
I cannot tell which side is mine and which side came from the branch, and that is frustrating.
Let me check the documentation folder in the git repository itself.
Pulling up the documentation listing to find the section on conflicts.
Okay, the top block is the current branch and the bottom is the incoming one. That's much clearer.
Back in the editor, deleting the markers and keeping the colour sentence.
Saving the resolved file.
Staging it and committing the resolution.
The merge went through and the history shows both commits. I'm pleased with that.
Honestly that is a relief, conflicts usually cost me twenty minutes of panic.
Running the log with the graph flag to see the shape of the history.
That's it, the tutorial worked end to end and I understood every step of it.

journeys.expected_physical: About 14 click rows - by far the fewest per minute in the category - and roughly 700 non-modifier keypress rows across fourteen bursts (nine terminal commands totalling about 285 keys, four editor bursts totalling about 340, one URL burst of about 46). That makes this the keypress-heaviest journey in the corpus and the best single source of JEM keypress ground truth for a binned-count metric, but it also means it will dominate any corpus-wide keypress denominator and must not be pooled naively with the lighter journeys. About 6 scroll spans totalling roughly 36 notches. Mechanical keyboard clatter is audible under continuous speech, which is deliberate: this is the only journey that could in principle support an audio-onset keypress detector and simultaneously the worst case for one.
journeys.stresses: Two distinct stresses, both of which only exist because of the prompt-hook repair. First, the terminal-command path: nine commands each produce a context_switch row with essentially no whole-frame luma change, on a dark surface, and several of them scroll output at the same instant - which is translation-like and therefore actively SUPPRESSED by the JAMS post-filter. Predicted recall on this sub-class is near zero, and that is the point: it isolates a failure mode the browser-only calibration corpus could never surface, and it is the strongest available evidence that JEM's foreground and title spans are a proxy label set rather than a shared referent. Second, the dark-to-dark app switching: ten taskbar switches between two dark surfaces, squarely in the content-floor failure class. Additional targeted stresses: the red merge-failure text and VS Code's coloured conflict decorations are hue-dominant changes at near-constant luma that a grayscale proxy is structurally blind to; the branch-switch beat at 306 s changes the editor content underneath the user with no separate row; six of the thirty switches are dirty/clean title bullets with sub-pixel-scale visual evidence; the 30-second conflict dwell gives a static-screen and near-silence window. At roughly 2.3 switches per minute this journey sits just under the cognitive lane's 2.72/min saturation point, which is deliberately the most sensitive operating point in the corpus. The narration is stratum A with four explicit cues ('let's get started', 'okay next', 'moving on', "that's it") placed at real boundaries, and seven human task segments against thirty switches gives a strong segmentation divergence.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: git log renders the configured user.name and user.email on screen, so the repo-local identity (JEM Subject / subject@example.invalid) must be set inside git-demo before the take and verified with git log in the pre-flight. GitHub is browsed LOGGED OUT so no avatar, username, notification count or private repository list appears. No credentials, no SSH keys, no tokens, no push, no remote - the repository is local-only and never gains an origin. REPRODUCIBILITY: the .git directory MUST be deleted between takes or the history diverges and the conflict does not reproduce. github.com/git/git front matter changes with upstream activity, which shifts scroll extents but not switch structure. If the prompt function is not pasted in before Start, or is pasted into a different tab, the nine terminal switches silently do not happen and the take is scientifically empty - confirm with the pre-flight, not afterwards. GROUND TRUTH: (a) the detail column for terminal switches will read title:<command>, not uia:<command>, because the UIA scrape sees a fresh empty prompt at the instant the title settles - do not treat that as enrichment failure; (b) a light terminal colour scheme would create a large bright surface and risk a phantom flash, so the dark scheme is mandatory; (c) the predicted 30 rows assume the VS Code dirty-title bullet is active, so re-predict if the pre-flight shows otherwise; (d) the beat spacing already keeps every pair of switches above five seconds, and it must not be compressed - the tightest pair in the journey is the 374 s to 384 s terminal re-entry and first command.

journeys.title: Troubleshooting an unreadable terminal colour scheme
journeys.setup: Apply GLOBAL SETUP v2 from realistic-mixed-01. OPERATOR CONFIRMATION REQUIRED BEFORE THIS TAKE: this is the ONLY journey in the category that writes to an application's own settings file, so Chris should agree to it explicitly rather than have it happen as a side effect of the plan. It is additive and reversible: back up Windows Terminal's settings.json first (copy it to settings.json.jem-bak), then add a throwaway profile named exactly 'JEM Sandbox' that duplicates the PowerShell profile with colorScheme set to the built-in 'Vintage' (genuinely low contrast, which is what makes the frustration in the narration real) and fontSize 11. The real default profile is never touched, and the sandbox profile is deleted afterwards or simply left in place. DELIBERATE CONTRAST WITH realistic-mixed-04: that journey installs a prompt hook so terminal commands become visible to JEM. This one installs NOTHING - the Windows Terminal title stays fixed at the tab name for the whole session, which is the DEFAULT behaviour on any untouched machine. The two journeys together bracket both terminal regimes, and the commands run here are deliberately invisible to JEM as a result. Do not paste the prompt function into this session. WINDOWS: Windows Terminal foreground on the JEM Sandbox profile, cd'd to D:\jem-scratch\git-demo (a folder with a mix of directories, scripts and text files so 'dir' output is colourful). Windows Terminal's 'Open JSON file' action must open settings.json in VS CODE, not in the Settings UI and not in Notepad - verify this in the pre-flight, because if it opens anything else the entire app-switch structure of the journey changes. VS Code runs the JEM-Subject profile, Dark Modern. Edge behind both, dark theme, one tab on https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/terminal/customize-settings/color-schemes with the theme switcher set to Dark. The Learn URL is typed directly rather than searched for, which trades a little realism for reproducibility - search result pages change daily and would make a second take non-comparable. PRE-FLIGHT: confirm (a) Ctrl+comma in Windows Terminal opens settings.json in VS Code and that the resulting VS Code window title is stable and predictable, (b) the VS Code dirty-title bullet behaviour, (c) that saving settings.json makes Windows Terminal live-reload without any title change.

narration.line: I set up a sandbox terminal profile yesterday and the colours in it are unreadable.
Look at this, the directory names and the file names are almost the same shade of grey.
I'm opening the settings JSON directly rather than fighting with the settings screen.
It opened straight into my editor, which I did not expect but genuinely appreciate.
Scrolling down to the sandbox profile, it is the third entry in the list.
I'm changing the colour scheme value to one half dark and saving it.
Oh that is so much better, I can actually tell the folders apart at a glance.
The reload happened without me restarting anything, which is a great touch.
I'm going to remove a comma on purpose to see what a broken settings file does.
There's the warning bar, and it does not tell me which line the problem is on.
Wonderful. An error message about a syntax error that will not say where the syntax error is.
Putting the comma back and saving again.
The warning has cleared itself and the terminal is back to normal.
I want the full list of built-in scheme names, so I'm reading the documentation.
There are about a dozen schemes here with proper screenshots of each one, this is well done.
Campbell Powershell is the one I actually want, the blue is much darker.
Back in the editor to set that scheme and bump the font size up two points.
Eleven point was far too small for this monitor anyway.
And there it is, readable at a normal distance for the first time all week.
Running the directory listing again to check the folder colour against the file colour.
That contrast is genuinely fine, I'm pleased with it.
Checking the git status output too, since that uses a different part of the palette.
Red for modified, green for staged, both perfectly legible.
Scrolling back to the top of the documentation to note the scheme name down later.
I'll stop there, that problem is sorted.

journeys.expected_physical: About 12 click rows, all taskbar and editor clicks. Roughly 100 non-modifier keypress rows across eight small bursts - deliberately an order of magnitude lighter than realistic-mixed-04 despite using the same three applications, so the two journeys separate typing volume from application structure. About 6 scroll spans totalling roughly 40 notches. Four terminal commands are run and NONE of them produces a context_switch row.
journeys.stresses: The deliberate counterpart to realistic-mixed-04: identical application set, opposite terminal regime. With no prompt hook installed the Windows Terminal title is frozen, so four commands and every screenful of their output are completely invisible to JEM. Together the two journeys let the evaluation state precisely how much of the terminal ground truth is an artifact of the operator's shell configuration rather than a property of the tool - which is a claim about JEM's validity that no single-regime corpus can make. The journey's second stress is the live-reload feedback loop: saving settings.json makes Windows Terminal repaint its entire surface, and the settings-error warning bar appears and disappears, all without a single title change, so three of the largest visual events in the take have no ground-truth row. Eight of the nineteen switches are VS Code dirty/clean title bullets with essentially no visual evidence, including two pairs only six seconds apart that sit close to the 2.0 s detector floor and test whether rapid low-evidence pairs are resolved or merged. The Ctrl+comma beat is the only foreground change in the category initiated by one application launching another rather than by a deliberate user switch. Emotionally this is the richest journey in the set - a genuine frustration to relief arc - and it carries the category's only two DECLARED IRONIC lines (232 s 'Wonderful. An error message about a syntax error that will not say where the syntax error is' and, more mildly, 404 s), labelled negative because that is what a human rater assigns to the intent. A text-only twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) model is expected to score the 232 s line positive, which makes it the cleanest single demonstration in the corpus that sentiment from transcript text alone has a ceiling and that prosody would be needed to close it. Do not scatter more irony elsewhere: it is confined here on purpose so the effect is measurable rather than diffuse.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: no credentials, no accounts, no personal data. The working folder is synthetic scratch content. The one Microsoft Learn page is public and read-only. CONFIGURATION: this is the only journey that writes to an application's settings file. Back up settings.json before the take, get the operator's explicit agreement first, restrict every edit to the JEM Sandbox profile, and leave the default profile untouched. Nothing else on the machine is modified and no system or security setting is involved. REPRODUCIBILITY: the take depends on Ctrl+comma opening settings.json in VS Code - if Windows Terminal is configured to open the Settings UI instead, the app-switch structure collapses and the journey must be re-predicted, which is exactly what the pre-flight is for. Windows Terminal's built-in scheme list changes between releases, so pin the Terminal version in the session notes. The Learn documentation page is revised without notice, which shifts scroll extents but not switch structure. journeys.expected_physical: About 20 click rows including one right-click, one double-click (two MouseButtonDown rows) and three click-drags in Paint that produce exactly one row each with no travel recorded. Roughly 230 non-modifier keypress rows, of which 13 are bare arrow keys with no accompanying click at all - a physical pattern that appears nowhere else in the category and that no video-inferred keypress detector has any plausible signal for. ZERO scroll spans: this is the only journey in the category with no wheel input whatsoever, which makes it the clean control for the scroll post-filter's false-positive rate on genuinely scroll-free footage.
journeys.stresses: The deliberate easy-class control and the corpus's high-contrast bracket. Nine of the twelve switches are foreground process changes between three visually unlike applications with enormous frame deltas, so recall here should be near 1.0 - and if it is not, the problem is the detector rather than the corpus. That gives the hillclimb a journey where regressions are unambiguous, which none of the other six provide. Against that easy baseline it sets the single largest JEM-blind block in the whole category: thirteen full-frame image repaints in the Explorer preview pane, every one of them driven by a bare arrow key, none of them producing a context_switch row. That is the cleanest possible proof that JEM's foreground and title spans cannot serve as the sole referent for a visual-change detector, because here the visual change is maximal and the ground truth is empty. The four-arrow burst at 70 s is spaced about two seconds apart on purpose, right at the detector's min_gap floor, so consecutive detections must merge and the merge behaviour becomes measurable. Two smaller stresses: the red annotation rectangles are hue-dominant changes at near-constant luma over a small image region, the weakest signal a grayscale proxy could be asked to find; and three Paint drags confirm again that JEM records the press point and nothing else, which bounds any physical-effort provider. Narration is stratum B - no deliberate cue words - so all five task boundaries must come from scene boundaries alone. Sentiment is a balanced 9 neutral, 6 positive, 4 negative with no irony anywhere, which makes this the reference journey for measuring how much of the sentiment error in realistic-mixed-05 is attributable to irony specifically.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: this is the reason the images are synthetic rather than real screenshots. Do NOT point this journey at a real screenshots folder - real screen captures routinely contain email addresses, account names, tokens, customer data and open document titles, and JEM records the preview pane at full size. All six PNGs are generated shapes and lorem text, the notes file is throwaway, and nothing leaves the scratch drive. REPRODUCIBILITY: the Explorer preview pane must be ON and the view must be Details before Start, or the arrow-key beats produce no image repaint and the journey's main stress silently disappears. Paint's tool defaults persist between takes, so reset the brush width and colour before each run. Delete and regenerate the six PNGs between takes, because the annotated versions are saved over the originals. GROUND TRUTH: (a) the predicted twelve rows assume Notepad marks dirty state with a leading asterisk and that Paint does NOT mark dirty state at all - the pre-flight checks both, and if Paint does mark it the count rises by up to three and must be re-predicted before recording; (b) the two Paint spans carry different filenames and are therefore genuinely different identities despite being the same process, so do not collapse them when auditing; (c) all six images must be dark-dominant, because a bright full-screen image would trip the flash detector and make the session unscoreable; (d) if any image ever fails to render in the preview pane the corresponding narration line becomes false and the take must be rerecorded rather than relabelled.

journeys.title: Rapid three-way comparison against a checklist
journeys.setup: Apply GLOBAL SETUP v2 from realistic-mixed-01. This is the short, deliberately HIGH switch-rate journey and it exists to bracket realistic-mixed-03's 0.85 switches per minute from the opposite end. At roughly eight switches per minute it drives the cognitive effort lane far past its 2.72/min saturation point, which is the only way to confirm where the lane actually clips and whether the score stops responding to real increases in switching. PREPARE: D:\jem-scratch\compare\checklist.txt containing eight short synthetic checklist lines (for example 'heading size matches spec', 'button radius matches spec', 'empty state text present'), and D:\jem-scratch\compare\spec-a.md containing about thirty lines of synthetic specification text with values that some of the checklist lines match and some do not. Serve the pinned hash-routed fixture from realistic-mixed-02 at http://localhost:8080/#shop and MINIMISE the serving terminal. WINDOWS: exactly three, all on the recorded monitor, all maximised, all dark - Notepad on checklist.txt, VS Code (JEM-Subject profile, Dark Modern) on spec-a.md, and Edge on the fixture product page. The rotation is driven by TASKBAR CLICKS, not by Alt+Tab: Alt+Tab with three windows requires holding and re-tabbing, which is fiddly and produces inconsistent dwell times, whereas three fixed taskbar buttons are unambiguous and additionally give clean click rows at a known screen row for physical-effort auditing. Rotate Notepad, VS Code, Edge, Notepad, and so on, dwelling about six seconds in each window. Six seconds is chosen on purpose: comfortably above JAMS's 2.0 s min_gap so every switch is resolvable in principle, and fast enough that the take is genuinely demanding to perform. Keep narration sparse - you cannot speak continuously at this pace and the sparseness is itself part of the design. PRE-FLIGHT: confirm the Notepad dirty-asterisk and VS Code dirty-bullet title behaviours, and confirm all three taskbar buttons are visible without any grouping or overflow menu.

journeys.expected_physical: About 31 click rows, nearly all of them on taskbar buttons at a single known screen row, which makes them unusually cheap to verify against the video and gives a clean spatial cluster for any click-position analysis. Roughly 108 non-modifier keypress rows across three short bursts. ZERO scroll spans. The click-to-switch ratio is close to one to one, which is the inverse of realistic-mixed-03 where sixteen clicks produced seven switches - the two journeys therefore bracket that ratio from both ends.
journeys.stresses: The high-rate bracket. At roughly nine switches per minute the cognitive lane is driven far past its 2.72/min saturation point, so this take is the one that shows where the lane clips and whether the effort score stops responding to genuine increases in switching - a question no other journey in the category can answer, and one that matters because a saturating lane makes the headline score insensitive to exactly the behaviour it is meant to measure. It is also the hardest test of the segmentation provider in the corpus: 36 scene boundaries against 3 human task segments is a twelve to one over-segmentation ratio, and with MIN_SEGMENT_MS at 10000 and switches arriving every six to eight seconds the greedy left-to-right merge is forced to discard most boundaries, which is precisely the regime where its behaviour is least characterised. The narration contains no deliberate cue words at all, so the segmenter gets no audio assistance whatsoever and must rely on the merge rule alone. The single eighteen-second dwell at 238 s is the only rhythm break in an otherwise uniform sequence and is the one boundary a competent segmenter should find. Six of the thirty-six switches are dirty/clean title flips with near-zero visual evidence, deliberately embedded mid-rotation so they sit between two high-evidence switches and can be confused with them. Finally, at four minutes this is the short end of the category's duration spread, which lets per-minute rate metrics be checked for length dependence against the thirteen-minute realistic-mixed-04.
journeys.risks: PRIVACY: three local synthetic files and one local fixture page. No accounts, no credentials, no network submission, no personal data anywhere. Close every unrelated window before Start - with rapid taskbar clicking it is easy to click the wrong button and bring something unplanned on screen, and JEM records the whole frame. REPRODUCIBILITY: the serving terminal must be up and minimised before Start, and all three taskbar buttons must be visible without grouping or an overflow menu, or the rotation breaks mid-take. Delete and recreate the two scratch files between takes since the journey appends to both. PERFORMABILITY: this take is genuinely demanding and mis-clicks are likely at this pace - a mis-click that lands on the wrong window still produces a valid JEM row, so it does not invalidate the session, but it does change the predicted count and must be reconciled against events.csv afterwards rather than assumed away. Do not compress the six-second dwells: at four seconds the switches approach the 2.0 s detector floor and any resulting misses become harness artifacts rather than detector findings. GROUND TRUTH: (a) the predicted 36 rows assume both the Notepad asterisk and the VS Code bullet dirty-title behaviours, so re-predict if the pre-flight disagrees; (b) because nearly every switch is a foreground process change between three visually distinct dark windows, recall should be high here despite the pace - if recall drops as the rate rises, that is a rate-dependent detector effect and is exactly the finding this journey was built to surface; (c) the narration is intentionally sparse, so the sentiment sample from this take is small and must not be pooled with the longer journeys without weighting.

category_notes.office-content:
CORRECTED COMMON RIG (applies to all six office-content journeys; read before the first take of the day)

THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT CORRECTION: JEM CAPTURES NO AUDIO. The proposed set repeatedly implied otherwise — it raised sync.pre_flash_delay_ms "because audio is enabled and the dshow device needs time to open", and office-content-01's risks told the operator to "rely on ffmpeg muxing both streams in one process for the real A/V anchor". Neither is possible. JEM's ffmpeg invocation has no audio input and jem.config.json has no audio keys; it produces silent MP4. Narration must be captured by a SECOND, INDEPENDENT recorder and muxed afterwards, and the claps are therefore load-bearing alignment fiducials, not sanity checks. The corrected procedure, identical for every journey:
1. On DISPLAY2, once per machine, run `D:\git\jem\vendor\ffmpeg\ffmpeg.exe -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy` and record the exact microphone device string in the session notes.
2. Per take, on DISPLAY2: `ffmpeg -f dshow -i audio="<device string>" -ac 1 -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_s16le D:\golden\<journey-id>\narration.wav`
3. Wait until ffmpeg prints a growing `size=` line — the dshow device needs two to three seconds to open. Do NOT press Start in JEM before that.
4. Press Start in JEM. CLAP ONCE, hard and short, at the instant the white flash appears.
5. Perform the journey.
6. Press Save in JEM. CLAP ONCE at the instant the closing flash appears. Then press `q` in the ffmpeg terminal.
7. Post-capture: locate flash run #1 in the MP4 (the same mean-luma > 245 test jem_eval's detect_flash_runs uses), locate clap #1 in the WAV by peak detection, compute the offset, and mux: `ffmpeg -i <jem>.mp4 -itsoffset <offset> -i narration.wav -map 0:v -map 1:a -c:v copy -c:a aac journey.mp4`. The two claps give a two-point linear fit that cancels both constant offset and USB-clock drift; a single clap only cancels offset. A missed or soft clap costs the entire take's transcription and sentiment ground truth, so re-record rather than guess.
Because JEM opens no audio device, sync.pre_flash_delay_ms does NOT need raising for audio reasons. Keep it at 1500 anyway, but for the honest reason: it gives the operator time to get hands clear of the keyboard before the flash.

RIG. Windows dark mode already on (AppsUseLightTheme=0, SystemUsesLightTheme=0); Office UI Theme = "Use system setting" so Office renders Black. Record DISPLAY1 (3072x1728, primary, at 0,0). Keep the JEM control window, the fixture server terminal, the audio ffmpeg terminal and narration.txt all on DISPLAY2 (at 0,-1728). JEM Project = "JAMS golden set". capture.record_video=true, capture.scale=1.0, privacy.capture_key_text=FALSE, sync.end_flash=true. One unbroken take, never Pause. Close Teams/Zoom/Discord so the microphone is free.

WHAT THE DISPLAY2 PLACEMENT ACTUALLY BUYS (the proposed setup overstated it). JEM's ContextSwitchConsumer ignores any foreground window whose monitor is not the recorded one, so windows on DISPLAY2 emit no context switches — correct. InputEventConsumer likewise drops clicks and scrolls whose cursor position falls outside the monitor rect, so pressing Start and Save on DISPLAY2 costs nothing. BUT keypresses are NOT monitor-filtered: HandleKeyDown has no coordinate test, so any key pressed anywhere lands in events.csv. Never type on DISPLAY2 during a take. AND JEM's sync-flash window is displayed ON DISPLAY1, so a Jem.App.exe context span does appear in events.csv; jem_eval drops it by process name (`row.get("process","").casefold() != "jem.app.exe"`), which is why several journeys' "Jem.App.exe -> APP.EXE" switch annotations were wrong and have been rewritten as "opens the first customer-app span".

DEFINITION OF expected_context_switches. It is the number of customer-app `context_switch` ROWS in events.csv — that is, SPANS, with jem.app.exe rows excluded — because that is exactly what jem_eval takes as truth (it uses each row's t_start_ms as a truth point). Going Word to Notepad++ and back twice yields five spans, not four transitions. office-content-03's proposed value of 6 contradicted its own steps, which described three spans; it is corrected to 3.

FLASH SAFETY IS AN ABSOLUTE GATE. detect_flash_runs thresholds on mean frame luma > 245 and _offsets raises "sync alignment ambiguous" if the detected flash count does not equal the manifest count plus the end flash. A near-white application surface filling the frame can therefore destroy a take retrospectively. Every journey mandates a dark canvas (Word Dark Mode, dark PowerPoint design variant, Office Black chrome for Excel, dark fixture pages including every error and confirmation state, Snipping Tool dark) and Paint is deliberately excluded. Run detect_flash_runs on the MP4 immediately after Save, before starting the next journey — not hours later.

EDGE IDENTITY IS TWO-PATH AND THIS CHANGES FIXTURE DESIGN. For msedge.exe, JEM builds ContextIdentity from the UIA address-bar ValuePattern when EdgeUrlParser.TryGetHttpHost accepts it as an absolute http/https URL, and falls back to the PARSED TAB TITLE when it does not (scheme-less omnibox text such as "localhost:8080/..." is rejected). An in-page view swap that changes only document.title therefore produces a context switch on the title path and NOTHING on the URL path. The existing fixture at D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys\index.html uses exactly that in-page pattern, and office-content-04 as proposed copied it for PROBE A — which would have made the paired probe non-deterministic and scientifically worthless. PROBE A is corrected to a REAL same-tab navigation to a separate blocked.html, changing URL and title together. PROBE B stays strictly in-page and must touch neither. office-content-04 now carries a mandatory pre-flight that verifies both behaviours against events.csv before the real take.

JEM SIGNAL FACTS THE JOURNEYS NOW RELY ON, ALL VERIFIED IN SOURCE.
- Clicks: WM_LBUTTONDOWN/RBUTTONDOWN/MBUTTONDOWN/XBUTTONDOWN only. Mouse movement and button-up are never written. A press-drag-release of any length is exactly ONE click row at the press point; a double-click is two rows. The drag blind-spot probes in journeys 02 and 05 are valid.
- Keypresses: key-down only, OS auto-repeat suppressed, one row per key. Key categories (KeyCategorizer): digits/letters/numpad digits/numpad operators/all OEM punctuation to alphanumeric; Space and Enter to whitespace; Tab and the arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown cluster to navigation; Backspace/Delete/Insert to editing; Shift/Ctrl/Alt/Win to modifier; Escape and function keys to "other". Ctrl+F6 in journey 06 therefore logs one modifier plus one "other".
- NumLock off silently reclassifies the whole number pad from alphanumeric to navigation. Journey 03's profile inverts if this is wrong; check the LED.
- Scrolls: ScrollAggregator opens a span on the first notch and closes it on direction change, on identity change, or after hooks.scroll_idle_close_ms (800 ms) of idle. A single flick gives t_start_ms == t_end_ms. No scroll sweep may straddle a context switch.
- In-app title changes: EVENT_OBJECT_NAMECHANGE on the foreground hwnd is coalesced over hooks.namechange_quiet_ms (200 ms) and then emitted with the namechange's own timestamp. For non-Edge processes ContextIdentity is (process, raw title verbatim), so Notepad++ tab switches and Word document switches genuinely produce context_switch rows. Journey 06 depends entirely on this and pre-flights it.

JAMS CONSTANTS, STATED CORRECTLY. The proposed set called 9.6 "the hard content floor". It is not: ContextSwitchParams.min_content_val defaults to 12.0 and 9.6 is min_content_val x low_response_candidate_floor_factor (0.8), the candidate floor below which a low-response candidate is discarded. min_gap_seconds is 2.0 and PROXY_FPS is 5.0, which is why sub-200 ms scroll flicks are predicted invisible and why two switches one second apart cannot both survive. segmentation.MIN_SEGMENT_MS is 10,000 and SNAP_WINDOW_MS is 3,000. jem_eval.MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS is 500 and it scores context_switch ONLY.

SEGMENTATION STRATA — now six genuinely distinct conditions (the proposal had journeys 01 and 03 both cue-free, a near-duplicate that has been fixed by making 03 partial-cue):
01 NO CUES — fall back entirely to scene boundaries; predicted gross under-segmentation.
02 ALL CUES — a cue at each of six boundaries, all far beyond MIN_SEGMENT_MS.
03 PARTIAL CUES — cues at 3 of 8 boundaries ("First" 36 s, "Now" 296 s, "Finally" 580 s), none elsewhere.
04 CUES AS DISTRACTORS — "then"/"after that" mid-line at three NON-boundaries, and no cue at either genuine boundary.
05 HIGH BOUNDARY DENSITY — eleven switches in six minutes feed many candidates into the union and several fall inside the 10 s floor; measures over-merge.
06 DONE-FAMILY ONLY — the corpus's only exercise of the done branch, with the two done cues 16 s apart, just above the floor.
Every narration array has been re-checked word by word against DEFAULT_CUES using the same word-boundary regex _matches_cue applies. Two accidental violations were fixed: office-content-01's closing line originally read "The draft is finished", which matches the done cue and would have destroyed its no-cue stratum. Note that "completely" does NOT match "complete" because the regex requires a trailing word boundary.

NARRATION DISCIPLINE. Read every line verbatim from narration.txt on DISPLAY2. Leave at least two full seconds of silence between lines and end every line with a falling full stop, so Silero VAD segments them cleanly and each utterance carries exactly one declared sentiment label. Line densities were checked against 150 wpm delivery and now span a deliberate range: 23 wpm (01), 30 (06), 31 (03), 38 (05), 47 (02), 60 (04) — three below and three above the spoken_word saturation knee. The proposal's office-content-02 packed 30 lines into seven minutes with 13-second spacing; trimmed to 28 at 15-second spacing, which still clears the knee while leaving genuine gaps. Sentiment labels are roughly balanced within each journey for macro-F1. Several borderline labels were rewritten rather than relabelled, because a mixed-valence line is a bad reference regardless of which label it carries: "The draft is in reasonable shape" (labelled positive but reads neutral) became "in good shape and I am genuinely pleased"; "The form blocked my submission, which is exactly what I wanted to see" (negative surface, positive intent) became "The validation caught it cleanly and I am impressed"; "The submission went through and the confirmation page is on screen" (labelled neutral but mildly positive) became a flatly descriptive line. Neutral lines are now purely descriptive statements of fact with no evaluative adjective.

KEYPRESS ESTIMATES WERE CORRECTED DOWNWARD. office-content-03 claimed ~2,600 keypresses with 380 navigation and 420 whitespace; the content it specified is about 615 keys and its column-wise (Enter-per-cell) entry pattern could not produce meaningful navigation at all. Since navigation coverage is the entire scientific purpose of that journey — the prior 825-keypress calibration session had ZERO navigation keys — the entry pattern was changed to row-wise (Tab across, Enter at row end) and the row count raised from twelve to twenty, which yields ~1,000 keys with ~70 genuine navigation rows. office-content-04 claimed ~430 keys with "roughly 90 Tab presses" across fourteen fields; corrected to ~330 keys and ~20 Tabs. office-content-01's ~1,900 was close and stands at ~1,800.

OTHER PERFORMABILITY FIXES. office-content-01's "Ctrl+click to select the three section heading lines" is not performable — Ctrl+click selects a SENTENCE in Word, not a line, and non-contiguous multi-select needs Ctrl+drag; the step now applies Heading 2 to each heading one at a time. office-content-03's claim that decimal rate values would autoformat as dates is false — only slash-separated values convert, so the beat now types literal "3/4", "5/8" band values, which really does trigger it and really is locale-dependent as the risk note said. office-content-02's layout and Format Shape steps now name the exact ribbon paths (Home > Layout; right-click border > Format Shape > Text Options > Textbox > Do not Autofit). office-content-05's Snipping Tool process names are no longer predicted — they are Windows-build dependent and a protected surface can resolve as "unknown", so that journey now carries a pre-flight that records what this build actually emits, and its expected_context_switches of 11 is explicitly an estimate to reconcile against events.csv.

MISSING SIXTH JOURNEY, NOW AUTHORED. The proposed set was truncated inside office-content-05 and contained no office-content-06 at all, even though office-content-02 twice referenced it as "the precise structural mirror where in-app file switches DO change the window title". office-content-06 has been written to be exactly that: fourteen JEM context switches in eight minutes, ten of them in-app document changes between deliberately near-identical dark files, giving context_switch RECALL a real denominator for the first time. Journeys 02 and 06 must always be reported as a pair — 02 measures precision on a sparse-truth, high-visual-change background and 06 measures recall on a dense-truth, low-visual-change background, and neither number is interpretable alone. Note also that 06 contains a pre-declared 50% recall ceiling on its double-Ctrl+Tab pair (two real switches one second apart cannot both clear min_gap_seconds of 2.0), which must be excluded from any claim that recall is improvable by tuning.

DISTINCTNESS SUMMARY. 01 typing-dominant, 1:225 click-to-key, no cues, low narration density, low-delta background. 02 click-dominant, JAMS-sees-all/JEM-sees-nothing, all cues, saturated narration. 03 navigation-and-scroll probe, paired long/short scrolls, partial cues, longest take. 04 shortest and most surgical, the only paired dual-visible/JEM-blind probe, distractor cues, densest narration. 05 drag-heavy and keypress-light, four apps, highest switch rate, the corpus's only fully aligned full-frame positive control. 06 the recall mirror of 02, highest modifier share, done-family cues. No two share a stratum, a dominant input modality, or a measurement role.

PRIVACY SWEEP. Every journey uses wholly invented content — the fictional "Northwind Trace" tool, synthetic task names and owner initials, fabricated hours and rate bands, an RFC 5737 documentation-style address and an email on the reserved .invalid TLD. No journey requires any sign-in, account creation, password, payment detail or real credential, and none was present in the proposal either. All fixtures are local, static and client-side; nothing is submitted over any network. AutoSave is off and OneDrive is unused everywhere, so no document leaves the machine. Word and PowerPoint Recent Documents are cleared, Edge runs on a clean profile with the favourites bar hidden and all other tabs closed, so no personal filename or bookmark reaches the video. privacy.capture_key_text stays FALSE in every journey so typed text is not written to the plaintext CSV alongside the video. One residual exposure to state plainly: the microphone is live for the entire take and JEM's video captures everything visible on DISPLAY1, so the room must be clear of other voices and DISPLAY1 must hold nothing but the journey's own applications.

POST-TAKE ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST (run before counting any take as good): (1) detect_flash_runs finds exactly the manifest flash count plus the end flash; (2) events.csv customer-app context_switch row count is within one of expected_context_switches, and any discrepancy is explained in the session notes rather than ignored; (3) both claps are audible in narration.wav and the two-point fit residual is under 50 ms; (4) the key-category histogram matches the journey's expected proportions, with navigation specifically non-zero for 03 and 06; (5) scroll row count matches, with journey 03's four single-notch flicks present as four separate rows with t_start_ms == t_end_ms. Per the evaluation matrix, detector settings stay FIXED while scoring; nothing is retuned and no hard sample is dropped after seeing a score.
category_notes.realistic-mixed:
I verified every mechanical claim against D:\git\jem\src and D:\git\jams\worker\src before rewriting. Six of the proposed premises were factually wrong, two of them fatally. Corrections, highest impact first.

1. FATAL - realistic-mixed-02 would have produced ZERO ground truth. JEM's Edge branch (ContextSwitchConsumer.BuildEdgeContext -> EdgeUrlParser.TryGetHttpHost) uses the FULL ADDRESS-BAR URL as the ContextIdentity whenever it parses as http/https, and ignores the document title entirely. fixtures/jem-journeys/index.html is an innerHTML-swapping SPA that never changes its URL, so all thirteen claimed switches collapse into one span. Repair: add hash routing to the fixture (one line in page(), setting location.hash per view) and pin that revision. That makes the identity change under either resolution branch. Corrected count 14. A pre-flight now exists specifically to catch this failure mode.

2. FATAL - realistic-mixed-04's headline stress did not exist. It claimed nine terminal commands produce nine context_switch rows. SwitchTo() is only reachable from a foreground change, a title NAMECHANGE, or the Edge-only workspace recheck. There is NO periodic re-scrape for terminals, so with a stock PowerShell prompt the title never moves and commands are invisible to JEM. Repair: a session-scoped prompt function that writes the last command into the window title, pasted in before Start. Also corrected: the detail column will read title:<command>, not uia:<command>, because at the instant the title settles the terminal's last line is a fresh empty prompt and TerminalPromptParser returns empty. I then turned this into an asset - realistic-mixed-05 now deliberately runs the DEFAULT regime with no hook, so the pair brackets both and the corpus can state how much terminal ground truth is an artifact of shell configuration.

3. AUDIO - the clap plan was unperformable and unnecessary. JEM's flash is 300 ms and fires 500 ms after Start; no one hits that window reliably. JEM already ships Jem.Platform.SyncTonePlayer, which plays a 1 kHz 150 ms tone at the exact flash paint instant precisely so a separately recorded microphone track can be aligned, and D:\git\jams\capture\audio_align.py already implements the two-anchor offset-plus-rate fit and the mux. sync.sync_tone defaults to FALSE and is absent from jem.config.json, so it must be turned on explicitly. The config comment is blunt: "The output device must be audible to that microphone - headphones defeat it." The proposed global setup said "wear headphones", which would have silently destroyed alignment on all seven takes. GLOBAL SETUP v2 now specifies speakers, sync_tone on, the parallel ffmpeg dshow WAV started before Start and stopped after Save, and the align-then-mux post step. All claps removed.

4. MISSED SIGNAL - VS Code's default window.title template includes ${dirty}, so every edit/save pair emits TWO extra JEM context_switch rows whose only visual difference is a bullet glyph. Same for Notepad's asterisk. The proposal ignored this entirely, which is why its counts were low by 30 to 50 percent. Rather than suppress it I kept it and named it the micro-visual stratum: it is the most extreme low-evidence true-positive class available, well under min_content_val 12.0 and its 9.6 effective floor. Corrected counts: 01 is 21 not 14, 03 is 7 not 6, 04 is 30 not 22. Every journey now carries a pre-flight that re-predicts rather than recording blind, per the EVALUATION-MATRIX rule about not moving anything after seeing scores.

5. JEM HANDOFF - JEM does not minimise itself, so jem.app.exe is foreground when Start is pressed. Journey 01 asserted "Edge is already foreground", which is false. Every journey now opens with an explicit bring-the-app-forward beat, and notes that jem_eval drops process=='jem.app.exe' spans so that transition is unscored.

6. SCROLL TRUTH - the 02 fixture pages all fit on one screen, so wheel input produces JEM scroll rows with zero pixel change. I kept two such beats and relabelled them honestly as the "physical input with no video evidence" stratum, which pins the recall ceiling for any video-inferred scroll detector at exactly zero. Scroll burst gaps raised to 2 s throughout, since scroll_idle_close_ms is 800 ms and "about a second apart" was too close to the boundary to be deterministic.

7. PRIVACY / STATE repairs. Journey 03's pointer-size slider applies immediately with no Apply button, so dragging it is a real persistent personalisation change - that beat is removed and only the text-size slider (which previews without applying and is discarded via Back) remains, preserving the stress at zero cost. Journey 03 also now explicitly excludes the Settings Accounts page (real account name and email) and the network pages. Journey 06 was rewritten to use six pre-authored synthetic PNGs rather than a real screenshots folder, because real screen captures routinely contain addresses, tokens and customer data and JEM renders the preview pane full size. Journey 05 is the only journey that writes to an application's settings file; it is now flagged for explicit operator agreement first, with a backup step, additive-only edits to a throwaway profile, and the default profile untouched.

NARRATION. Rewritten against three constraints. (a) Speakability: every journey now sits at 27 to 38 percent speech density at 150 wpm, with line counts scaled to duration (13 lines in the 4-minute journey, 33 in the 13-minute one). (b) Label defensibility: lines that were labelled neutral but read as mildly positive ("There we go, three files, exactly what I expected") were either made explicitly positive or stripped of evaluative language. Neutral now means purely procedural. (c) Cue hygiene: DEFAULT_CUES matches bare word-boundary substrings including "first", "next", "now", "then", "done", "complete" and "finally", so I audited every line and removed accidental occurrences. Deliberate cues are confined to journeys 01 and 04 (stratum A, four each at real boundaries), 02 carries incidental-only cues (stratum C), and 03, 06 and 07 are cue-free (stratum B) so scene boundaries must carry segmentation unaided.

SENTIMENT CEILING - flagging this now because it will dominate step 4. The sentiment provider is Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX, a BINARY model; jams_worker only calls a label neutral when |positive_prob - negative_prob| <= 0.15, which a confident binary classifier almost never produces. Roughly 45 percent of these lines are genuinely neutral, so 3-class macro-F1 will look catastrophic for reasons that are structural rather than tuning-related. Report BOTH 3-class macro-F1 and binary macro-F1 over the non-neutral subset, or the hillclimb will chase a number that cannot move without changing the model. I confined all irony to realistic-mixed-05 (two declared lines) and left realistic-mixed-06 irony-free with a balanced 9/6/4 mix, so the irony penalty is separately measurable rather than smeared across the corpus.

DISTINCTNESS. 04 and 05 were near-duplicates (same three applications, same editor-terminal-browser shape). They are now deliberate opposites: 04 has ~700 keypresses, 30 switches, and the prompt hook that makes commands visible; 05 has ~100 keypresses, 19 switches, no hook so commands are invisible, and a genuine frustration-to-relief emotional arc. 06 and 07 were authored fresh to fill two gaps the original set left open. 06 is the EASY-CLASS CONTROL - no browser, no editor, nine high-contrast process switches where recall should be near 1.0, so a regression is unambiguous; without it every journey is a hard case and a detector regression is indistinguishable from a uniformly difficult corpus. It also carries the largest JEM-blind block anywhere (13 full-frame image repaints driven by bare arrow keys, zero rows) and is the only scroll-free and only click-drag-heavy journey. 07 is the HIGH-RATE BRACKET at ~9 switches/min against 03's 0.85, which is the only way to locate where the cognitive lane clips past its 2.72/min saturation point.

CORPUS DESIGN. The seven now bracket every axis deliberately rather than all crowding the hard end: switch rate 0.85 to 9 per minute; duration 4 to 13 minutes; keypresses 18 to 700; clicks 12 to 31; scroll spans 0 to 11; click-to-switch ratio from 16:7 (03) to 1:1 (07). Cross-journey totals: about 139 context switches, 1500 keypresses, 130 clicks and 30 scroll spans. Two warnings for whoever aggregates: journey 04 alone is 47 percent of all keypresses and will swamp a naive corpus-wide denominator, and journey 07 alone is 26 percent of all switches. Weight by journey or report per-journey.

OPEN ITEM the plan cannot close by itself: jem_eval.py is context-switch-only and explicitly excludes click, keypress, scroll, sentiment, utterance and spoken_word. These journeys produce rich ground truth for all of those, and none of it can be scored until the evaluator grows those comparisons. Journeys 01, 03 and 06 are the right first targets for the human visual-change annotation pass, because their JEM-blind events are large, unambiguous and easy for a person to timestamp.
category_notes.multi-app-switching:
TRANSMISSION NOTE, read first. The proposed set was truncated in transit: journey 05 was cut off mid-sentence in its step at 455 s, and journeys 06 and 07 were not transmitted at all. Since the brief requires seven journeys with the same ids, 05 has been completed from its own stated design intent (the matched low-delta versus high-delta pairing was clearly the payload and has been preserved and finished), and 06 and 07 have been authored to fill the two largest gaps left by 01 through 05. Those gaps are stated under section E. Nothing that survived transmission was deleted; 01 through 04 are repairs of the originals, not replacements.

=== SECTION A: SHARED PREFLIGHT (every journey references this) ===
A1. DISPLAY1 is the recorded monitor. Everything that is not part of the journey lives on DISPLAY2 or is closed. Verify every journey window is actually on DISPLAY1 immediately before pressing Record; JEM IGNORES foreground windows that resolve to any other monitor, so a window that has drifted produces no event at all and a wrongly long context span.
A2. NEVER PRESS PAUSE. This is the hardest rule in the whole corpus and it was absent from every proposed journey. jem_eval._offsets raises "paused sessions require per-segment ending anchors; not yet safe to score" whenever the manifest contains more than one start flash. A paused take is not degraded, it is unscoreable, and the only remedy is to re-record. Decide before starting that the take runs start to finish.
A3. FLASH MARGIN, measured not assumed. The gate is a full-frame grey mean above 245 on a 64x36 downscale, sustained for at least 2 consecutive frames. Measure with: ffmpeg -i <still.png> -vf scale=64:36,format=gray -f rawvideo - | (byte mean). Dark working surfaces read roughly 30 to 60; light ones read roughly 210 to 235. Record the number in the scenario notes. Separately, jem_eval aborts with "sync alignment ambiguous" if the detected flash count is not exactly the logged count plus one, so a single phantom bright run discards the entire take.
A4. TITLE DRY RUN. Every journey specifies a short throwaway recording whose only purpose is to confirm the context_switch row count matches the script before minutes are spent. This exists because JEM emits a row only when the derived ContextIdentity changes, and whether a given title change crosses that bar is application and build specific. The dry runs are not optional and two of them (journey 04's switcher question, journey 07's foreground-activation question) are blocking.
A5. SCROLL DISCIPLINE. JEM closes a scroll span after hooks.scroll_idle_close_ms = 800 ms with no notches. Any step that expects "one scroll span" requires the notches inside that burst to be under 800 ms apart, and requires at least 3 seconds of stillness before the next burst. Several proposed steps said "slow wheel bursts", which would have fragmented into many spans and broken the expected counts.
A6. DEDICATED PROFILES. Edge always uses the 'JEM Fixture' profile with no synced history, because a resolved URL lands in JEM's uia detail column as plaintext CSV, not only in the video. Clear the MRU list of every Office application before every take.
A7. ARCHIVE. Keep the JEM video, events.csv and manifest outside Git per EVALUATION-MATRIX rule 1. Commit only the fixture recipes, the redacted labels, the metrics and the reports. Journey 07 additionally produces interrupter-log.csv, which must be archived with the session.
A8. FIXTURE PAGES must not call document.title after load and must not navigate, unless a journey explicitly wants the resulting rows. The existing fixtures/jem-journeys/index.html does call document.title on every page() transition, which is exactly why it emits JEM rows; do not copy that helper into the new fixtures.

=== SECTION B: VERIFIED CONSTANTS (corrected against source; the brief's figures were wrong in several places) ===
B1. min_content_val default is 12.0, not 9.6. Source: worker/src/jams_worker/providers/context_switch.py, ContextSwitchParams. The 9.6 figure that appeared throughout the proposals is min_content_val multiplied by low_response_candidate_floor_factor (0.8), which is a different gate governing low-response candidate admission. Every journey's threshold reasoning has been corrected.
B2. There is ONE 2.0 second floor, not two. min_gap_seconds is 2.0, and min_scene_len_frames is 10 at PROXY_FPS 5.0, which is also 2.0 seconds. The proposals treated these as two independent constraints.
B3. The analysis proxy is 480 pixels wide (PROXY_WIDTH 480, PROXY_FPS 5.0). A 3072-pixel-wide source is downscaled about 6.4 times before the threshold is consulted, so a title-bar highlight or a caret is sub-pixel before min_content_val is even reached. This strengthens the structural-false-negative arguments in journeys 02 and 05 and was not mentioned anywhere in the proposals.
B4. Paused sessions are rejected outright. See A2.
B5. MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS is 500. Detected cuts are only counted inside JEM's customer-app spans, widened 500 ms at the leading edge, so cuts during the recorder-owned opening and closing spans are neither true nor false positives. This is why every journey keeps a quiet dwell at both ends.
B6. THE EVALUATOR ALREADY STRATIFIES BY VISUAL CORROBORATION. This is the largest correction to the proposals' framing. Since the September 18 fix, jem_eval decodes a grayscale delta profile at VISUAL_DELTA_FPS 10 and records, for every truth event, the peak frame-to-frame delta within the match tolerance, reporting three groups: all truth, visually corroborated at VISUAL_CORROBORATION_DELTA 0.30, and proxy-only. Journeys 02 and 05 claimed this capability did not exist and that they were the argument for building it. They are not. They are the argument for POPULATING it, which is a smaller but still real contribution, and their stresses text has been rewritten accordingly. Calibration anchors already on record: 0.03 to 0.04 for a switch into an already-visible window, 1.13 and 1.89 for genuine missed transitions on IANA, 0.46 to 11.66 on the controlled fixture, about 180 for a sync flash.
B7. WHAT IS STILL GENUINELY MISSING is the OPPOSITE direction: visual change with no JEM row. The evaluator has no mechanism for it, because a detection with no nearby truth row is simply an unmatched cut. Journey 03 (ten reading-pane repaints) and journey 05 (a maximise and a restore) between them supply twelve pre-registered instances at known instants. That is the concrete input to the human visual-annotation pass EVALUATION-MATRIX rule 5 requires.
B8. PER_MINUTE_SCALE context_switch is 36.75 with the score clamped at 100, so the cognitive lane saturates at 2.72 switches per minute. spoken_word is 2.47, saturating at 40.5 words per minute. Natural speech is about 150 wpm, so every journey's narration must be sparse (roughly 25 words per minute averaged over the whole take) simply to keep the speech lane off its ceiling. That is a constraint on narration design, not a stylistic choice, and it caps every script at roughly 2 lines per minute.
B9. JEM CSV kinds are SINGULAR: click, keypress, scroll, context_switch. The evaluator's excluded_kinds list is ["click","keypress","scroll","sentiment","utterance","spoken_word"].
B10. The Windows key is categorised as a MODIFIER by KeyCategorizer. So one Win+2 press emits exactly 2 keypress rows: 1 modifier (Win) and 1 alphanumeric (the digit). Journey 01's proposal claimed 28 modifier rows for 14 switches and journey 03's claimed about 50; both double counted and both have been corrected. All switching overhead is now stated separately from work typing in every expected_physical field, because pooling them inflates the physical measure by the switching mechanism.
B11. hooks.namechange_quiet_ms is 200, so a burst of title changes coalesces into one row rather than many. And JEM writes no row at all when the derived ContextIdentity is unchanged, which is why every title-flip claim in journeys 03 and 05 is now conditional on a dry run rather than asserted.
B12. probe.py rejects anything over MAX_DURATION_SECONDS (20 minutes) with "too_long", with no partial result. jem_eval's CFR re-encode subprocess has a 300 second timeout and its flash detection, which decodes every frame, has a 120 second timeout. Journey 05 at 14.5 minutes is the canary for all three and is recorded first.
B13. DEFAULT_CUES CONTAINS VERY COMMON BARE WORDS and this is the biggest narration hazard in the corpus. The start list includes "first" and "starting"; the next list includes bare "next", "now", "then" and "after that"; the done list includes bare "done", "complete" and "finally". Matching is a word-boundary regex on the lowercased utterance, so any line containing "now" or "then" creates an unintended segment boundary. Every narration line in all seven journeys has been audited against the real lists. Only journey 02's proposal had actually done this audit; the others had not, and were lucky. The audit is now a standing requirement for any new line.
B14. _merge_short_boundaries discards any boundary less than MIN_SEGMENT_MS (10 s) after the preceding one, and the first preceding boundary is video_start at 0. So an opening cue spoken in the first 10 seconds is silently dropped. Journey 01 keeps its cue at 6 s and pre-registers the drop as a prediction; journey 03 places its cue at 14 s and pre-registers survival. That contrast is deliberate and is the cheapest available test of the merge rule.
B15. SENTIMENT REALITY, and this matters for how the declared labels should be read. The production ONNX path is Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX, which has only NEGATIVE and POSITIVE classes. "Neutral" is derived post hoc as a band where the mapped value falls between -0.15 and +0.15, and twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) is characteristically overconfident, so that band will almost never be occupied. Expect declared-neutral lines to be classified as polar at close to a 100 percent rate on the ONNX path. That is not a flaw in these scripts, it is the neutral false-positive rate EVALUATION-MATRIX explicitly asks for, and the neutral-heavy narration is the right instrument for measuring it. Only the VADER fallback, which has a real neutral band, can produce a neutral label at all. Every journey therefore keeps enough clearly polar lines that macro-F1 over positive and negative remains measurable independently of the neutral collapse.

=== SECTION C: OUTLOOK-FREE FALLBACK (journey 03) ===
If Outlook is signed into a work tenant with compliance or DLP tooling, do not record its window. Build fixtures/jem-journeys/mailbox.html instead: a dark three-pane mailbox mock, list on the left and reading pane on the right, holding the same ten synthetic messages. Clicking a message repaints the reading pane and must NOT call document.title, which reproduces journey 03's central payload (a large visual change with no JEM row) with no account, no credential and no real mail anywhere on the machine. What is lost is the native-application stratum, which has independent value given that the existing Outlook session is one of the two real-world zeros driving strategy. Record the variant in the scenario name and never pool the two.

=== SECTION D: WHAT I CHANGED AND WHY (per test) ===
D1 PERFORMABILITY. Added measured numeric gates in place of judgement calls (the flash-margin one-liner with a 240 threshold and a documented fallback). Added a short discarded dry run to every journey, with the two blocking ones called out. Specified the 800 ms scroll rule wherever a step said "slow bursts". Journey 04's "repeat the cycle four more times" and journey 05's shell commands were left as written because both are genuinely unambiguous once the command list is fixed in setup.
D2 GROUND-TRUTH VALIDITY. Corrected journey 01's modifier arithmetic (28 to 14) and journey 03's switch count (28 to 23, with the derivation shown: 21 Win+number presses plus 2 title flips; the original 28 was not derivable from its own step list). Made every title-flip claim conditional on a dry run, since JEM suppresses rows when the derived identity is unchanged. Closed journey 04's open-ended "MDN navigations add a handful of rows" by making MDN scroll-only, which is what makes 44 exact. Raised journey 04's task-switcher question and journey 07's foreground-activation question to blocking gates, because in both cases an unverified assumption does not merely shift a count, it changes what the journey measures. Rewrote journeys 02 and 05's claim that visual-corroboration stratification does not exist (B6) and redirected the argument to the direction that genuinely is missing (B7).
D3 NARRATION QUALITY. Audited every line against the real DEFAULT_CUES lists (B13). Fixed journey 01's factual error, where the narration called the gasket set "the last row" when it is row six of seven, and added the missing row seven line so the script covers what the steps actually do. Relabelled or rewrote lines whose declared sentiment an independent rater would plausibly dispute: mixed-valence lines ("a relief after that truncation", "broken link, which is quick to verify") were split so each line carries one clear valence, and flatly factual lines that had been labelled positive were either made genuinely positive or relabelled neutral. Line density is held near 2 per minute everywhere, which B8 requires anyway.
D4 TIMING COHERENCE. Journey 01 7.5 to 8 minutes, 02 9 to 9.5, 03 12 to 12.5, 04 4 to 4.5, all to match their own step lists. Journey 05 is set at 14.5 with an explicit 17 minute abort against the 20 minute probe limit. Journey 06 carries an explicit note that its step timestamps run to about 15 minutes against a 10 minute intended pace, with the closing block named as the place to trim; that is flagged rather than silently reconciled because the pace is the point of the journey and the step list is the upper bound. Moved journey 04's 175 s narration line to 182 s so it does not land inside the harder violation block, and added an explicit no-narration instruction to both violation blocks, since narrating while performing six switches in nine seconds is not physically possible.
D5 PRIVACY. No journey requires any credential, and none ever did. The two changes that matter: journey 03 now has a tenant gate as its first setup step and requires File > Work Offline, which is strictly stronger than Do Not Disturb because it stops mail arriving rather than merely suppressing its toast. Journey 07 was designed from the outset to use a local script raising a Notepad window rather than a real notification, precisely so that no real sender content can enter the dataset. Journey 06 notes that light themes make recent-files panes more legible in the recording than the dark journeys do, so MRU clearing matters more there.
D6 DISTINCTNESS. 01 is full-window high-delta at a diagnostic rate. 02 is side-by-side near-zero delta. 03 is half-screen repaints with no JEM row, plus title flips with no visual change. 04 is dark-on-dark at saturation with labelled spacing violations. 05 is the within-session matched control, the same app pairs switched under two visual regimes minutes apart. 06 is the light regime at the low end of the cognitive lane. 07 is imposed switches with no preceding input, plus an independent third clock. The closest pair is 02 and 05's low-delta phase, and they are kept distinct by 05 being a two-regime control rather than a single-regime sample, which 02 cannot be because it never maximises anything.

=== SECTION E: THE TWO GAPS 06 AND 07 FILL ===
E1. LUMA BIAS. Journeys 01 through 05 are all dark on dark. That means the corpus cannot distinguish "the detector struggles with low delta" from "the detector struggles with dark content", and it also means nobody has ever measured how close a normal light desktop gets to the 245 flash gate. Journey 06 inverts only the luma regime while holding the task shape close to journey 01, and produces three measured flash-margin numbers as a first-class deliverable.
E2. INPUT-CORRELATION SHORTCUT. In journeys 01 through 06 every single context switch is immediately preceded by a click or a keypress, because Chris initiates all of them. A heuristic that simply fired on "Win key pressed" would score near-perfectly on all six without looking at a pixel. Journey 07 supplies 10 switches out of 22 with no preceding input at all, which makes it the discriminator between a real detector and that shortcut, and it should be a mandatory member of the holdout split for that reason alone. It also adds the only independent third timestamp source in the corpus, which lets the flash-offset mapping itself be validated rather than assumed; given that timestamp integrity is patent-core, that is arguably worth more than another detector sample.

=== SECTION F: RECORDING ORDER ===
05 first (pipeline timeout canary; confirm it scores end to end before recording anything else), then 01 (the calibration anchor), then 04 (short, cheap confirmation of the capture and upload chain), then 07, 02, 06, 03. Journey 03 is last because it carries the highest privacy risk and the most setup, and because by then the dry-run discipline will be routine.

=== SECTION G: RESERVED FOR THE HOLDOUT ===
Per EVALUATION-MATRIX rule 3, detector settings stay fixed while a holdout is scored. Recommended split for this category: development = 01, 03, 05 (the ones with the richest per-event structure to reason about); holdout = 02, 04, 06, 07 (the four pre-registered known-limit and discriminator samples). Journeys 02 and 04 must never be hillclimbed against; both are expected to fail and their value is entirely as regression samples that a candidate change must not worsen elsewhere in order to improve here. Journey 04's two violation blocks must be reported under their own label and never folded into a headline recall number.
category_notes.adversarial-edge:
SCOPE: five adversarial-edge journeys were supplied (ids 01-05) and five are returned, same ids, repaired rather than deleted. The distinctness test mentions eight journeys; that appears to span the whole corpus across categories. Within this category the five are distinct: 01 is motion-energy versus motion-coherence with zero input events; 02 is the grayscale luminance floor and a hue-only change; 03 is sparse everything, the only journey that keeps all four scoring lanes off saturation; 04 is disfluent speech against a fixed reference; 05 is a controlled acoustic degradation with visual and physical truth held constant. No two of them stress the same provider mechanism, and each one's primary target is a different file.

=== SHARED PREFLIGHT (every journey in this category references this) ===

1. SYNC TONE CONFIG. Edit jem.config.json before launching JEM and set the sync block to include "sync_tone": true, "sync_tone_hz": 1000, "sync_tone_ms": 150 alongside the existing flash_duration_ms 300, pre_flash_delay_ms 500, end_flash true. SyncTone is a plain bool with no initializer in Jem.Core/JemConfig.cs, so it defaults to FALSE, and it is NOT exposed in JEM's Settings window (the Sync Flash group offers only flash duration, pre-flash delay and End flash). If this is not set in the file there is no audio anchor and the narration can never be aligned to the video.

2. AUDIO PATH. JEM records no audio. Narration goes to a separate 16-bit PCM mono WAV (the Yeti Nano), started BEFORE pressing Start in JEM and stopped AFTER pressing Stop so both tones are inside it. Afterwards: python -m capture.audio_align mux --video <mp4> --audio <wav> --manifest <session.json> --out <muxed.mp4>, and feed the muxed file to the JAMS pipeline. Check the align report's drift_ppm and residuals before trusting the take.

3. SPEAKERS, NOT HEADPHONES. The tone plays through the Windows default output device and must be audible to the microphone. capture/audio_align.py says so in its own error text: headphones defeat this anchor.

4. DO NOT CLAP. This is the single largest correction to the proposed set: every journey originally opened and closed with "clap once, sharply, inside the white flash". That is obsolete and actively harmful. detect_tone_onsets requires at least 90 ms (MIN_TONE_MS) of continuous energy whose share of frame energy in the 1 kHz Goertzel bin exceeds DOMINANCE = 0.35. A hand clap is broadband, would never pass that test, and if it overlaps the tone it inflates total frame energy and pushes the real tone's share under the threshold. The correct protocol at both anchors is silence and stillness for about two seconds either side.

5. START AND STOP. Click Start; about 500 ms later (pre_flash_delay_ms) the flash paints on the recorded monitor and the tone plays. The END flash and tone fire on STOP, not on Save (SessionController calls StopRecorderSegment(writeEndFlash: true) on stop). JEM's buttons are Start, Pause/Resume, Stop, Save, Discard. Every journey originally said "click Save ... the end sync flash fires", which would have had the operator waiting for a flash that already happened. Sequence is: Stop, stay silent two seconds, then Save.

6. MONITOR DISCIPLINE. JEM records monitor 1. JEM's own window, the fixture HTTP server terminal and any helper process live on monitor 2. ContextSwitchConsumer filters foreground AND name-change events by monitor (Jem.Core/ContextSwitchConsumer.cs lines 157 and 215), and InputEventConsumer filters clicks and wheel events by monitor rect but NOT keypresses. So nothing on monitor 2 reaches events.csv except the sync-flash window, which is painted on the recorded monitor and which jem_eval identifies by flash and excludes. Keypresses are logged wherever the operator types, which is why all typing in these journeys happens on the recorded monitor.

7. FIXTURE SERVER. python -m http.server 8099 --directory D:\git\jams\fixtures\jem-journeys, in a terminal ON MONITOR 2. The fixture is a single committed index.html whose page() helper sets document.title on every screen, so its in-page routing DOES change the Edge window title and IS visible to JEM. Screens and background colours, verified from source: Journey selection #142d44, Create workspace #142d44, Workspace ready #244831, Product selection #142d44, Review cart #4d304c, Test receipt #244831, Upload failed #663c28, Upload recovered #244831.

8. WINDOWS TERMINAL DETERMINISM. Set the profile's "suppressApplicationTitle": true and a fixed "tabTitle". Without it, every shell command rewrites the tab title, which is a NAMECHANGE on the foreground window and therefore an extra JEM context_switch. Three of the five proposed journeys quietly assumed this did not happen and their expected counts were wrong because of it.

9. NOTEPAD++ DETERMINISM. Before pressing Start, type one character into the scratch file and do not save. The modified marker is then already in the title, so no title change (and no phantom switch) occurs during the take. Do not press Ctrl+S during a recording: clearing the marker is also a title change. Save after Stop.

10. EDGE DETERMINISM. One window, one tab, dark theme, memory/performance tab badge OFF. Navigate only by Ctrl+L, full URL including http://, Delete to clear inline autocomplete, Enter.

11. QUIET ROOM. Do Not Disturb on, phone out of the room, mail and chat closed. A toast is simultaneously a foreground change, a visual change and an unscripted sound.

12. PRIVACY FLOOR. No sign-in, no account creation, no payment, no real customer data. No .env, no infra/ connection strings, no tokenised git remotes, no password typed anywhere. privacy.capture_key_text stays OFF (JEM default), so events.csv records key_category, not characters. Everything on the recorded monitor is the local synthetic fixture, locally generated media, or JAMS' own source and docs. Nothing in this set requires credentials, and nothing was removed on privacy grounds because nothing in the proposals crossed that line.

13. DRY RUN FIRST. Record a 60 s throwaway with the identical setup, run capture.audio_align align on it, and run jem_eval on it. Alignment is the failure that destroys a take, and journey 03 (12 minutes) will also exercise jem_eval's subprocess timeouts, verified as 120 s for flash detection and 300 s for the CFR re-encode, both sized for 90 s clips.

14. FIXED SETTINGS. Detector parameters are frozen for the whole category and recorded in the run as context_switch.params. No retuning after seeing a score (EVALUATION-MATRIX rule 3). Missing providers are reported as missing, not as zero.

15. NARRATION IS ITS OWN GROUND TRUTH. The written line is the WER reference and carries the pre-declared sentiment label. Leave at least 1.5 s between lines; SPLIT_GAP_MS is 1200 and MERGE_GAP_MS is 700, so shorter gaps merge lines and break the one-line-one-label mapping. Where numbers are spoken as words, declare the normalization protocol in writing before computing WER.

=== CONSTANTS VERIFIED AGAINST SOURCE (so no journey asserts a number it cannot support) ===

providers/proxy_motion.py: PROXY_FPS 5.0, PROXY_WIDTH 480, grayscale.
providers/context_switch.py ContextSwitchParams: adaptive_threshold 4.0, min_scene_len_frames 10 (= 2.0 s at 5 fps), window_width 3, min_content_val 12.0, phase_response_threshold 0.25, phase_shift_px_threshold 2.5, low_boundary_response_exemption 0.1, borderline_post_count 1, drop_post_count 2, borderline_multiplier 0.6, low_response_candidate_floor_factor 0.8 (hard candidate floor 9.6), min_gap_seconds 2.0.
providers/transcription.py: distil-small.en, SPLIT_GAP_MS 1200, MERGE_GAP_MS 700, MAX_UTTERANCE_MS 45000, VAD threshold 0.5 with max_speech_duration_s 30, two-pass rescue at threshold 0.35 fires only when coverage < 2% of duration AND audio_rms_db > -45, mean-word-duration invariant 60-1200 ms raising PipelineError at line 255, n-gram de-repetition collapses an n-gram repeated 4 or more times.
providers/segmentation.py: MIN_SEGMENT_MS 10000, SNAP_WINDOW_MS 3000. DEFAULT_CUES in full, matched by word-boundary regex on lowercased text: start = let's get started, lets get started, get started, to start, first, starting; next = okay next, next, moving on, now, then, after that; done = done, finished, complete, that's it, that is it, finally.
effort_score.py: PER_MINUTE_SCALE context_switch 36.75 (saturates at 2.72/min), spoken_word 2.47 (saturates at 40.5 wpm), clicks 1, keypresses 1, utterance 10. neg_density is share * 250 and is DURATION weighted over sentiment measure spans with the negative test value_num < -0.15, not a line count; raw minutes normalizes as minutes * 100/30.
jem_eval.py: MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS 500, MAX_DRIFT_MS 250, NORMALIZED_FPS 30, VISUAL_DELTA_FPS 10, VISUAL_CORROBORATION_DELTA 0.30, RECORDER_FLASH_TOLERANCE_MS 250, bright-frame test is mean grey > 245, flash-detect subprocess timeout 120 s, CFR re-encode timeout 300 s. The workload filter is an INCLUSION test (kind == "context_switch") at line 418; excluded_kinds at line 537 is a report field that filters nothing. _point_match is at line 320.
capture/audio_align.py: DEFAULT_TONE_HZ 1000, MIN_TONE_MS 90, HOP_MS 5.0, WINDOW_MS 25.0, DOMINANCE 0.35, onsets merged within 400 ms; two outermost anchors solve offset and rate; detect_transients uses a 3 ms/60 ms envelope ratio with default threshold 6.0 and is used by refine_offset_by_events to correct speaker-to-microphone latency against JEM click and keypress times.
JEM: keypress is one row per key-DOWN with OS auto-repeat suppressed and modifiers written as their own rows with key_category=modifier; scroll is an aggregated span with value_num = total notches, closed after hooks.scroll_idle_close_ms = 800; hooks.namechange_quiet_ms = 200 collapses a burst of title changes into one switch. JEM writes kinds click, keypress, scroll, context_switch (singular); JAMS writes clicks, keypresses, scrolls (plural).

=== WHAT WAS CHANGED AND WHY ===

Applied to all five: claps replaced with the sync-tone protocol; Save replaced with Stop-then-Save at the end; speakers made an explicit requirement; Windows Terminal title suppression and Notepad++ pre-dirtying added wherever the expected count depended on them.

01: VLC removed. The original played clip-c fullscreen in VLC while clips a and b played windowed in Edge, which confounded coherence with player, chrome and window rectangle and made the "matched control" claim unsupportable. All three clips now play in the same Edge media viewer at the same geometry, which is the only version of this experiment that isolates the discriminator. The uncertain "VLC may or may not emit a title change" beat disappears with it. Two clean app switches (Win+2 / Win+1) were added to preserve the switch count at 10. The mislabeled "Three clean page changes, each one obvious and nicely spaced" (written positive, labeled neutral) was reworded to a genuinely neutral observation, and the ambiguous "a bit hypnotic" positive was made unambiguous. Address-bar navigation made deterministic.

02: Three extra unlabelled context switches would have appeared per terminal command and one from the Notepad++ modified marker; both are now suppressed in setup, which is what makes the count of 17 actually correct. The hillclimb claim was corrected: docs/JEM-HILLCLIMB-2026-09-09.md does not say min_content_val=4 broke IANA and Outlook, it says the variant moved IANA from F1 0.0 (0/0/2) to F1 0.6667 (2/2/0) with two scroll-driven false positives and left Outlook at 0/2/1. That is a precision-recall trade, and the journey's real value is supplying data to adjudicate it. "The welcome screen is green, so at least one of these transitions is genuinely loud" was labeled positive but reads as a factual observation to any independent rater; reworded and relabeled neutral. A third cue line was added at t=397 so the audio-cue path gets three boundaries to snap.

03: The t=0 step said "sit still and silent for 40 s" while the t=10 step pressed a hotkey, a direct self-contradiction; fixed.
