Taskbar pins moved from 3/4/5 to 1/2/3 because Win+5 requires a fifth pinned item that the setup never created. The Calculator sequence used "x" for multiply, which is not a key; replaced with explicit keypad strokes. The forbidden-cue list was incomplete; it now matches DEFAULT_CUES exactly, including "get started", "to start" and "that's it". The closing Ctrl+S was removed because clearing Notepad++'s modified marker is a title change and would have added a twelfth switch to a journey claiming eleven. The neg_density explanation was corrected to duration-weighted share with a -0.15 threshold.

04: Ctrl+G target corrected from line 228 to 320 (_point_match's actual location) and the Get-Content skip corrected from 395 to 530 so it prints the passage the narration is about. Taskbar pins moved from 2/3 to 1/2. The "terminal title may change, verify" uncertainty is resolved by suppressApplicationTitle rather than left open. Two narration lines were rewritten because they described running a harness when the step ran a Select-String. The central risk claim was corrected: a PipelineError from the mean-word-duration invariant fails the JAMS run but does NOT take the recording with it, because jem_eval is a separate local harness reading the MP4 and events.csv directly, so video, physical truth and context-switch scoring all survive and the take can be re-analysed. Every line was checked against DEFAULT_CUES and none matches, so the "zero intended cues" claim holds. The narration's technical claims were checked against source and are correct, which is a bonus: this take doubles as an accurate explanation of two real defects.

05: The take-destroying bug. The original bed ran 560 s with the tonal-plus-brown-noise stage still playing when Stop was pressed, which would have driven the closing 1 kHz tone's in-band energy share below DOMINANCE 0.35, produced one tone against two flashes, and made the whole nine-minute recording unalignable. A mandatory 60 s trailing silence segment was added, stage lengths were rebalanced so the bed ends around t=485 against a Stop near t=520, and an explicit listen-and-confirm step plus a dry-run requirement were added. Setup item 6 also placed a "spoken deliberately quietly" line at t=460, inside the t=430-470 say-nothing window; both quiet lines were moved outside both silent windows. Taskbar pins had a gap at slot 3; fixed. The expected switch count drops from 18 to 16 once the two terminal-command title changes are suppressed. A newly noticed secondary effect was added to stresses: the noise bed also raises detect_transients' slow-envelope baseline, degrading refine_offset_by_events in stages 2 and 3, which is measurable inside this single take.

=== GROUND-TRUTH VALIDITY CHECK (test 2) ===

Every "produces" claim in the returned set is one of: a JEM foreground change, a JEM window-title change on the foreground window of the recorded monitor, a JEM click inside the recorded monitor rect, a JEM keypress (any monitor), a JEM scroll span inside the recorded monitor rect, or an explicitly labelled NON-event. The proposals were mostly sound here, because the fixture sets document.title on every screen, so its in-page routing genuinely is JEM-visible; I verified that in the fixture source rather than assuming it. Three classes of claim were corrected. First, beats that claimed the end flash fires on Save. Second, beats whose counts silently assumed terminal and Notepad++ title changes would not fire. Third, one ordering claim in journey 02 that said the Win+2 switch would carry the enrichment detail of a command typed afterwards; the switch is logged at the Win+2 instant, so its detail reflects the shell as it stood then. Two beats are now explicitly marked as visual change with NO truth (journey 04's find-next jumps and its Ctrl+G viewport replacement), which is a feature: they are the cleanest available probe of detector firing where no proxy label exists, and jem_eval's per-event visual delta against VISUAL_CORROBORATION_DELTA 0.30 lets that be audited rather than argued.

=== NARRATION SPEAKABILITY (test 3) ===

All five scripts sit well inside a natural 150 wpm. Line counts against duration: 01 has 16 lines over 6 min, 02 has 20 over 8 min, 03 has 11 over 12 min (deliberately sparse, and that sparseness is the experiment), 04 has 24 over 7 min including one 25 s run-on, 05 has 21 over 9 min. At roughly 13 words per line and 5 s of speech plus a 1.5 s gap, the densest script (04) occupies about 176 s of its 415 s, leaving ample silence. No script packs 60 lines into 4 minutes. Sentiment labels were re-read as an independent rater would: three lines were reworded or relabeled where a "neutral" label sat on wording a rater would read as mildly positive, and each remaining positive and negative now carries an explicit first-person evaluative phrase (I am really pleased, it is discouraging, that is a real blind spot) rather than relying on a connotation the rater has to infer.
category_notes.duration-extremes:
CORRECTIONS APPLIED (what was wrong in the proposed set, and why)

1. NO AUDIO PATH WAS SPECIFIED, AND THE CLAP IS ACTIVELY HARMFUL. Every journey's narration depends on an audio track JEM does not record, yet no setup said how the narration gets onto the video. The repo already solves this: D:\git\jams\capture\audio_align.py aligns a separately-recorded microphone WAV onto the silent JEM MP4 using JEM's sync TONE (JemConfig.SyncTone, 1000 Hz, 150 ms, played at the exact flash paint instant), with a two-anchor offset-plus-rate fit. Two consequences the proposals got wrong: (a) sync_tone defaults to FALSE and is absent from D:\git\jem\jem.config.json, so it must be turned on before any take or nothing is alignable; (b) the instruction to "clap once sharply inside the white flash" must be REMOVED from every journey. detect_tone_onsets requires the 1 kHz band to hold at least 0.35 of frame energy; a clap is broadband and can push a genuine tone below that threshold, losing the anchor and making align() raise. All journeys now say: stay silent across both tones, never clap.

2. ALT+TAB IS NOT PERFORMABLE AS WRITTEN, AND ONE JOURNEY'S SEQUENCE WAS IMPOSSIBLE. duration-extremes-01 said "Alt+Tab back to Microsoft Edge" from VS Code after having previously alt-tabbed to the Terminal; a single Alt+Tab from that MRU state lands on the Terminal, not Edge. The MRU stack also contains JEM's own window and the fixture-server console, which nobody counted. Every app switch in every journey is now Win+1 (Edge) / Win+2 (VS Code) / Win+3 (Windows Terminal) / Win+4 (File Explorer) against a fixed taskbar pin order, which is stateless and deterministic. The fixture HTTP server is launched as a plain pwsh.exe console, not a Windows Terminal tab, so Win+3 can never land on it.

3. EVERY EXPECTED SWITCH COUNT WAS OFF BY ONE, FOR A REASON WORTH KEEPING. JEM has no global start hotkey, so pressing Start makes jem.app.exe the foreground process. jem_eval._recorder_processes identifies the recorder from whichever context span covers a manifest flash and excludes it, so the flash span is correctly discarded. But the workload app is then NOT foreground: the operator must actively bring it forward, and that focus grab is a real context_switch row in events.csv. It has no visual delta (the window was already on screen), so it lands in jem_eval's context_switch_proxy_only stratum and is a structural false negative. Every journey now includes it explicitly as truth switch #1 and reports it in its own stratum. The mandated 5+ second hands-off gap after Start is load-bearing for a second reason: it keeps the huge white flash-release transition outside every scored window, because scored windows start only 500 ms before a workload span. Without that gap the detector collects a free true positive on the most detectable frame in the file.

4. GROUND TRUTH CLAIMED THAT JEM CANNOT PROVIDE. Jem.Core.ContextIdentity is (process name, semantic title) — for Edge, the parsed TAB TITLE, not the URL. duration-extremes-03's round pattern claimed an in-page anchor click produces "URL fragment + title change"; a fragment-only navigation leaves the title unchanged and emits NO truth event. Those beats now require a link that actually navigates to a different document ('next topic' in the docs.python.org sidebar, the first sidebar entry under the current section on MDN), with the instruction to log the real target and to log a deviation rather than invent an event if the title does not change.

5. SCROLLING AN EMPTY FILE. duration-extremes-01 scrolled notes.md, which the same setup describes as a scratch notes file; with nothing to scroll there is no translation for the JAMS post-filter to suppress and the beat measures nothing. The corpus now seeds plan.md with 400 synthetic lines and longdoc.md with 4000, and that journey scrolls plan.md.

6. A CONDITIONAL STEP. duration-extremes-05 said "click the notes.md tab if it is not active"; tracing the script, notes.md IS active at that point, so the conditional switch never happens and the stated count of 6 was wrong. The beat is now unconditional and the count corrected (still 6, once the focus-grab switch is added).

7. PHASE ARITHMETIC THAT DID NOT FIT ITS OWN WINDOW. duration-extremes-04's phases specified dwell lengths that under-filled every stated time range (Phase A1: 8 x (sweep + 14 s) in a 160 s window; A3: 5 x (sweep + 14 s) in 120 s; B2: 12 x 6 s in 90 s). Dwells are now set from the cycle length so the phases actually span their ranges.

8. MISCOUNTED PHYSICALS. duration-extremes-01 claimed 2 clicks for a single field click and 72 keys for an 81-character command; duration-extremes-02 claimed ~12 clicks against 8 actual; duration-extremes-03 claimed ~9 clicks against 13 (7 editor tabs + 6 sidebar links). All corrected. These are targets: the truth is whatever events.csv records, and the script is never edited afterwards to match the log.

9. SENTIMENT LABELS AN INDEPENDENT RATER WOULD DISPUTE. Three lines were re-written rather than re-labelled: duration-extremes-02's "I am deliberately switching twice inside two seconds here which I know will break detection" (meta-commentary labelled negative, now an unambiguous affect statement), duration-extremes-04's "I am glad this document is boring..." (mixed valence, "glad" against "boring"), and duration-extremes-05's "Quiet time like this is actually useful..." (labelled positive but barely affective). duration-extremes-02's receipt line was strengthened from a mild "is clear" to an explicit relief statement.

10. CUE-WORD CLAIMS CHECKED AGAINST THE REAL VOCABULARY. segmentation.DEFAULT_CUES is far broader than the headline phrases and matches on word boundaries: start = let's get started / lets get started / get started / to start / first / starting; next = okay next / next / moving on / now / then / after that; done = done / finished / complete / that's it / that is it / finally. Every script was re-checked against that list. The "zero cue words" claims for duration-extremes-01 and -02 survive. duration-extremes-03's five announced boundaries, its unannounced round-5 boundary, and its deliberate "complete" trap at 380 s all behave as designed. Note that "final" does not match "finally" under word-boundary matching.

VERIFIED CONSTANTS THESE JOURNEYS ARE BUILT AGAINST (read from source on 2026-09-18, not assumed)
- jem_eval.MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS 500; NORMALIZED_FPS 30; CFR re-encode subprocess timeout 300 s; flash-scan subprocess timeout 120 s; bright-frame test = mean of a 64x36 grayscale frame > 245; excluded_kinds = click, keypress, scroll, sentiment, utterance, spoken_word.
- context_switch: min_gap_seconds 2.0; min_content_val 12.0 with a 0.8 candidate-floor factor (9.6); adaptive_threshold 4.0; window_width 3; proxy thumbnail width 640.
- segmentation: MIN_SEGMENT_MS 10000; SNAP_WINDOW_MS 3000; cue priority audio_cue > scene_boundary.
- effort_score PER_MINUTE_SCALE: context_switch 36.75 (saturates at 2.72 switches/min), spoken_word 2.47 (saturates at 40.5 wpm), utterance 10; time lane 100/30 minutes; all lanes clamped to 0..100.
- sentiment: ONNX Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX is BINARY; measure value is p_pos - p_neg in [-1, +1]; the provider's own summary uses a |value| <= 0.15 neutral band.
- probe: MAX_DURATION_SECONDS trips a terminal, non-retryable too_long error above 20:00.
- JEM: sync.flash_duration_ms 300, pre_flash_delay_ms 500, end_flash true, sync_tone default FALSE, sync_tone_hz 1000, sync_tone_ms 150; hooks.scroll_idle_close_ms 800; hooks.namechange_quiet_ms 200 (the source of the ~230 ms tab-switch lag); privacy.capture_key_text false; capture.scale 1.0.

STANDARD RIG (every journey's setup assumes all of this is already done)
R1. Two monitors. The recorded monitor carries only the journey's workload windows. JEM's own window, the round card, and the fixture-server console live on the other monitor and are never brought forward during a take.
R2. Edit D:\git\jem\jem.config.json ONCE for the whole corpus and never again: "sync": { "flash_duration_ms": 300, "pre_flash_delay_ms": 500, "end_flash": true, "sync_tone": true, "sync_tone_hz": 1000, "sync_tone_ms": 150 }. Changing detector-visible settings mid-corpus violates evaluation rule 3.
R3. Speakers ON at a normal level and audible to the microphone. NOT headphones: the tone must physically reach the mic or there is no anchor.
R4. Narration recorder: 16-bit PCM WAV (audio_align rejects anything else), e.g. D:\git\jem\vendor\ffmpeg\ffmpeg.exe -f dshow -i audio="<device>" -ac 1 -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_s16le narration.wav, run from a minimised console on the non-recorded monitor. Start it BEFORE pressing JEM Start and stop it AFTER the closing flash, so both tones are inside the WAV.
R5. Never clap, tap the desk, or speak within 2 seconds either side of a flash.
R6. Post-take: python -m capture.audio_align align --video s.mp4 --audio narration.wav --manifest s.json, then mux to produce the file uploaded to JAMS, passing the video duration so a longer WAV cannot push the upload past the 20:00 probe cap. jem_eval runs against the ORIGINAL silent JEM session (mp4 + events.csv + session.json); the muxed file is for the JAMS pipeline only.
R7. Do Not Disturb / Focus assist ON. No Teams, Outlook, or notification toasts: a toast is simultaneously a privacy leak, a phantom high-delta event, and a spurious foreground change.
R8. Windows dark mode plus dark themes everywhere. A near-white full-screen frame creates a phantom bright run and jem_eval raises 'sync alignment ambiguous', discarding the take.
R9. Edge: a dedicated clean local corpus profile. No sync, no saved passwords, favourites bar hidden, no extensions, memory saver OFF (its "Memory usage - NN MB" tab-name mutation emits phantom NAMECHANGE switches), startup boost off.
R10. VS Code: a dedicated profile named jem-code with window.title set to "${activeEditorShort} - jem-code" (this removes ${dirty}, which would otherwise emit two phantom switches per edit), minimap off, breadcrumbs off. ONLY C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch is ever opened. Never D:\git\jams, which contains .env files and deployment secrets that the video would capture verbatim.
R11. Windows Terminal: profile jem-shell with suppressApplicationTitle true and a fixed tabTitle "jem-shell", starting directory C:\Users\chris\JEM-scratch. Before each take run Set-PSReadLineOption -HistorySaveStyle SaveNothing then Clear-Host, so no earlier command (possibly containing a token or a private path) is on screen.
R12. Taskbar pin order, fixed for the corpus: 1 Edge, 2 VS Code, 3 Windows Terminal, 4 File Explorer. All app switches use Win+N. Never press Win+N for the app that is already foreground, which minimises it instead of activating it.
R13. Seeded scratch files, created once: plan.md (400 synthetic lines), longdoc.md (4000 synthetic lines, fixed line height), fake-build.ps1 (duration-extremes-05). notes.md is emptied, and build.log deleted, before EVERY take.
R14. One mouse for the whole corpus, detented wheel, Windows "lines to scroll" left at the default and never changed: notch counts are the scroll ground truth.
R15. Never pause a JEM session. A pause makes the take unscorable.
R16. Stay hands-off for at least 5 seconds after Start and after the last workload action before pressing Save. Both gaps keep the flash transitions outside every scored window.
R17. Narration is read from a printed script or from the non-recorded monitor. Off-script speech invalidates both the WER reference and the sentiment label set; log deviations rather than hiding them.
R18. Per-take acceptance gate, checked BEFORE upload: exactly 2 detected bright runs; non-null sync.end_flash_log_ms; mp4 duration under 17:50; the expected number of non-recorder context_switch rows (plus or minus one, with the discrepancy explained); capture.audio_align align succeeds with two tone anchors and a plausible drift rate. A take that fails any of these is re-recorded, not repaired.
R19. Raw JEM outputs and the narration WAV stay out of Git (evaluation rule 1). Only fixture recipes, redacted labels, metrics and reports are committed.

LONG-TAKE PRE-FLIGHT (required before duration-extremes-03 and -04)
P1. Record a throwaway 17-minute capture of anything and push it through jem_eval end to end. Confirm the 300 s CFR normalisation and the 120 s 64x36 flash scan both complete. At full desktop resolution and 30 fps they are the single most likely cause of a total evaluation failure on these files.
P2. If either fires, the corpus-wide fix is capture.scale 0.5 in jem.config.json, applied BEFORE any journey is recorded and then never changed.
P3. Confirm free disk (a 17-minute full-resolution capture can approach 2 GB) and that the preview org's 10 GiB cap can hold both long takes plus retries, remembering that declared bytes are reserved even on failed uploads.
P4. Measure and record this rig's actual video-versus-audio drift ppm from the pre-flight take. Do not quote a drift figure that has not been measured on this hardware.

SCORING CONVENTIONS FIXED BEFORE ANY TAKE IS SCORED (evaluation rule 3)
S1. Sentiment: three-class mapping uses the provider's own |value| <= 0.15 neutral band. twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) saturates near +/-0.98 on almost any sentence, so a near-zero neutral recall is a PREDICTED and reportable outcome, not a reason to move the band afterwards. The corpus deliberately carries a neutral majority precisely so the neutral false-positive rate the evaluation matrix demands can be measured.
S2. Strata, reported separately and never pooled: (i) fair-spacing visually-real context switches, the only stratum from which a headline precision/recall/F1 is quoted; (ii) proxy-only truth events with no visual delta (one per journey, the focus grab); (iii) the labelled sub-2-second pair in duration-extremes-02, a known structural limit of min_gap_seconds=2.0; (iv) pre-declared JAMS-only visual beats in duration-extremes-04 (Ctrl+Home, Ctrl+End, Page Down), which are visual changes JEM structurally cannot see and are therefore NOT false positives against proxy labels.
S3. Per-journey F1 at these durations is not reportable. duration-extremes-01 exists specifically to demonstrate that: 8 truth events give a Wilson 95% interval on recall roughly [0.53, 0.98]. Pool across the corpus, grouped by participant and task, before quoting any figure.
S4. Missing providers are reported as missing. If the mux step fails, transcription, sentiment, and segmentation's cue path are MISSING for that take, not zero.

DISTINCTNESS OF THE FIVE JOURNEYS
-01 (3.3 min) short, below both scoring knees, fixture-only and therefore the one take with no live-web dependency and a byte-identical re-record; the small-n demonstration.
-02 (4.2 min) short, above both knees, four apps, live docs plus the fixture checkout path, one deliberately unfair switch pair; the saturation high anchor and the cheapest timing statistics per minute.
-03 (17.4 min) long, dense, switch-dominated, both lanes linear, seven identical rounds; the drift, RTF, subprocess-ceiling and segmentation-cue-stratification case.
-04 (17.1 min) long, sparse, scroll-dominated, two apps, adversarial-by-design; the only physical.scrolls ground truth and the largest zero-event dwell exposure at length.
-05 (11.2 min) medium, mostly idle, opens on the Terminal rather than Edge, deterministic local timing source; the low anchor for the effort score and the only test of whether JAMS can represent waiting.
The nearest pair was -01 and -02 (both short, both multi-app, both using the fixture). They are now separated on five axes: three apps versus four, onboarding path versus checkout path, fixture-only versus live documentation, below both knees versus above both knees, and uniform fair spacing versus a deliberate sub-2-second probe.
category_notes.friction-sentiment:
REVIEW OUTCOME: all 8 journeys repaired and returned, same ids, same count, nothing deleted. Journey 07 arrived truncated mid-steps and was completed; journey 08 was missing entirely and was written to fill a real gap in the category (see DISTINCTNESS below).

THE ONE FINDING THAT CHANGES EVERYTHING - the real cue vocabulary. I read worker/src/jams_worker/providers/segmentation.py rather than trusting the proposals. DEFAULT_CUES is far broader than the proposals assumed: start = let's get started, lets get started, get started, to start, FIRST, STARTING; next = okay next, NEXT, moving on, NOW, THEN, after that; done = DONE, FINISHED, COMPLETE, that's it, that is it, FINALLY. _matches_cue lowercases and matches on whole-word boundaries (so 'know' does not fire 'now' and 'abandoned' does not fire 'done', but a bare 'now', 'then' or 'first' anywhere in a line does). Every one of the ~170 narration lines in this set has been audited against that list. Corrections made: journey 04's 'zero cue words' claim was checked line by line and CONFIRMED (it is genuinely the only cue-free journey in the corpus, which makes it the sole isolated test of the scene-boundary fallback); journey 06's claim of 'six cues' was wrong and is corrected to five; a draft rewrite of journey 06 line 606 that began 'For now I am...' was caught and reworded because 'now' would have injected a sixth boundary; journey 08 line 515 was reworded from 'and now I can prove it' for the same reason. Cue counts per journey are now: 01 three (all genuine), 02 five (all deliberate false positives), 03 three (two genuine, one deliberate FP), 04 zero, 05 one (genuine), 06 five (all genuine), 07 two (both genuine), 08 three (two genuine, one deliberate FP).

Other verified constants used throughout: min_gap_seconds 2.0 (context_switch), MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS 500 (jem_eval), SNAP_WINDOW_MS 3000 and MIN_SEGMENT_MS 10000 (segmentation). Every deliberate false-positive cue was placed at least 24 s from the nearest genuine boundary so it cannot snap away inside the 3 s window. JEM's events.csv schema was read from source: kind is one of context_switch, click, keypress, scroll, sync_flash, session; scroll rows are SPANS carrying value_num as a notch count (so the 'N notches' claims are valid ground truth); key_category is one of alphanumeric, whitespace, navigation, editing, modifier, other. All 'produces' text was rewritten into that vocabulary. 'Keypress burst' was replaced with 'keypress rows' everywhere, because a burst is an analysis artifact and JEM logs one row per key including modifiers.

GLOBAL FIXES APPLIED TO EVERY JOURNEY:
1. VS Code window title. VS Code's default window.title includes ${dirty}, so the title flips to a bullet on the FIRST keystroke of every edit and back on save. JEM logs each of those as a context_switch that has no visible on-screen counterpart, which would have made them guaranteed JAMS false negatives and made every expected count depend on exactly when the performer first typed. Every journey's setup now writes a workspace .vscode/settings.json with window.title lacking ${dirty} and files.autoSave off. This is declared, not hidden: it changes the environment, never the scoring.
2. No Save As dialogs. A Ctrl+S on an Untitled buffer opens a separate top-level window and costs two unmodelled switches. Journeys 02 and 04 originally did this; every file that gets saved is now pre-created by the setup script and opened by name.
3. Alt+Tab disambiguated. Alt+Tab only reliably reaches the most recent window, so it is now used ONLY in journeys where exactly two windows are open (02, 04, 05, 06, 08). In the three-window journeys (01, 03) every app change is an explicit left click on the taskbar button, which also yields a click row. Every setup states that all other windows must be closed.
4. Terminal title stability. A PowerShell prompt that retitles per command, or a child process that emits an OSC title sequence, injects spurious context_switch rows. Every terminal setup now pins $Host.UI.RawUI.WindowTitle and requires a dry-run check of the titlebar. Journey 02 carries the one genuine residual: ffmpeg may set the terminal title for progress, bounded to 0-3 rows because the stream copy is instantaneous, and it is called out to be counted from events.csv and reported separately.
5. Vague steps made literal. Every edit now specifies the exact keystrokes (click, Home, Shift+End, type this literal string) and every URL is given in full. 'Type the MDN optional chaining URL' and 'add a console.log of the loaded config' are gone.
6. Edge runs InPrivate in both browser journeys, so address-bar autocomplete cannot shorten a URL type between takes and nothing is written to history.

GROUND-TRUTH VALIDITY REPAIRS: the expected_context_switches figures in the proposals were mostly guesses and several were badly wrong. Every ledger was re-derived beat by beat. Corrections: 01 was 18, is 17; 02 was 5, is 4 (the Untitled-1 to trim-notes.md title change was removed with the Save As dialog); 04 was 14, is 11 (two of the remainder were uncertain terminal retitles, now flagged rather than counted); 06 was 22, is 13. 03 (10), 05 (9) and 07 (15) were re-derived and confirmed. Every journey's risks section now states that events.csv is the authority and the plan number is only the expectation, and every uncertain row is named individually so it can be reported separately instead of being folded into headline recall.

ARITHMETIC REPAIRS IN JOURNEY 06 (the worst defect in the set): the proposed script misspelled 'statistcs' in BOTH the import and the body, so fixing the import would have raised an unplanned NameError and broken the scripted four-defect order. The body now correctly reads statistics.mean, so the one-character import fix is clean. The narrated numbers were also simply wrong: with the proposed data the mean is 249.9, not 144, and statistics.quantiles(values, n=20)[-1] is 1922.85, not 1904. The outlier is changed from 2011 to 1013 so the twenty values sum to exactly 4000 and the run prints mean 200.0, and the fix is changed from statistics.quantiles to a literal minus-one on the index, which prints 248.0. That removes every dependency on a CPython implementation detail that could shift between versions. int(20 * 0.95) evaluates to exactly 19 in IEEE doubles, so the buggy index is deterministic. Journey 04's three REPL experiments were likewise rewritten to print only [1, 3, 8, 5] and True, all verified and all version-independent. Journey 03's narrated line count was 31 and is corrected to 30 (skus-fixed.txt has no header). Journey 02's source file is now generated by ffmpeg at exactly 124.5 s instead of copying apps/web/public/demo.mp4, whose duration nobody had measured.

NARRATION AND SENTIMENT: line counts are realistic - the densest journey runs 32 lines over 10 minutes (~39 wpm effective, each line ~4 s of speech at a natural 150 wpm with long deliberate gaps), the sparsest 21 lines over 16 minutes (~17 wpm). Nothing is packed. Lines whose label an independent rater would contest were rewritten rather than relabelled, so the declared label stays defensible: 01/50 s ('tells me nothing' was ambiguous, now 'is useless to me'), 01/196 s (the grudging 'at least' removed to make it genuinely neutral), 01/254 s ('good' added so the negation reads as relief), 03/565 s ('my wrists have opinions' was a joke a rater could call neutral, now a plain ache complaint), 03/950 s (was mixed valence, now cleanly positive), 05/358 s (now explicitly a dead end), 06/706 s ('four attempts' was wrong, there are five runs). Deliberate hard cases are preserved and declared in each stresses field rather than smoothed away: sarcasm at 01/24 s, 05/150 s, 07/24 s, 07/78 s, 08/245 s; inverse sarcasm at 07/176 s; negation at 01/254 s, 05/170 s, 07/114 s, 07/276 s, 07/322 s; and loaded-token neutral lines at 01/36 s, 05/26 s, 07/140 s (four alarming filenames read with no affect) and 03/725 s (zero affective vocabulary embedded mid-negative-stretch).

EXPECTED_SEGMENTS SEMANTICS - read this before scoring: expected_segments is the count of HUMAN task segments, the annotation target. It is NOT a prediction of how many segments JAMS will emit. Segmentation unions audio cues with JAMS-detected context switches and merges only inside MIN_SEGMENT_MS of 10 s, so a journey with 17 switches spread over 10 minutes will emit far more segments than its 6 human segments. That gap is the measurement, not an error in the plan.

PRIVACY: nothing in the set requires credentials, an account, a payment method, a real service or a form submission. Every data file is generated by its own setup script. Journey 05's network query is scoped to loopback so no real interface addresses reach the video. Journey 04 deliberately reads Python stdlib source rather than JAMS worker source, because the recording gets uploaded. Journey 07 moves files and never deletes, so no destructive control is ever clicked on camera. Journey 01 and 08 browse only public MDN pages in InPrivate windows. Every terminal is Clear-Host'd first so no unrelated command history is on screen. The one standing exposure is inherent to JEM, not to these journeys: privacy.capture_key_text defaults off, but the VIDEO captures everything visible, so no journey may be recorded with an unrelated window, notification toast or password field on the selected monitor.

DISTINCTNESS: the eight now separate along five independent axes rather than being eight variations of alt-tabbing between a terminal and an editor. Sentiment polarity anchors: 02 is all-positive with zero negative lines, 05 is all-negative with zero positive lines, and those two are the only clean denominators in the category for measuring false-positive rates in each direction. Arc shape: 01 is a single dip and recovery, 03 is a slow monotonic gradient, 04 is negative-to-positive across a long neutral middle, 06 oscillates three times, 08 is a boredom curve. Event density: 03 is the maximum at ~1,150 keypress rows in 16 minutes, 08 is the minimum at ~265 rows in 9 minutes with roughly 190 seconds of total silence, and that spread is deliberate because it brackets the range where the weight profile behaves differently. Process family: 07 is explorer.exe only, 01 and 08 involve Edge, the rest are terminal-plus-editor. Cue design: 04 is cue-free, 05 is one-in-one, 02 is all-false-positive, 06 is full precision-and-recall. The two closest pairs are 04/05 (both VS Code plus terminal, 7-8 minutes) and 05/06 (both terminal plus editor) - they are kept apart by outcome (comprehension with no edits, versus abandonment, versus oscillating repair), by polarity anchor, and by cue stratum, and each stresses field names its own unique contribution.

KNOWN LIMITS DECLARED IN ADVANCE, to be reported separately and never folded into headline recall: the rapid Alt+Tab burst at journey 06/246 s (three foreground changes inside four seconds against a 2.0 s minimum gap, so at most one is detectable); the terminal retitle rows at journey 04/100 s and 452 s; the ffmpeg title rows at journey 02/72 s; and the fact that every Windows Terminal tab hop in journey 02 and every Explorer navigation in journey 07 is a title change with no process change and near-zero pixel delta, which is the class JAMS structurally cannot see from video alone.
category_notes.dev-terminal:
DEV-TERMINAL CATEGORY NOTES, REVISED. The proposed payload arrived truncated: journeys 01 through 04 were complete, 05 was cut off mid-sentence inside its stresses field, and 06 and 07 were absent entirely although the review brief and journey 04's own text both refer to a set of seven. This review reconstructed 05 from its surviving steps and specified 06 and 07 from scratch to fill the two largest gaps in the proposed design. All seven ids are preserved.

VERIFIED CONSTANTS. Every numeric claim the journeys make about JAMS was checked against the source rather than taken on trust. worker/src/jams_worker/providers/segmentation.py: MIN_SEGMENT_MS = 10000, SNAP_WINDOW_MS = 3000, and DEFAULT_CUES is exactly start = (let's get started, lets get started, get started, to start, first, starting), next = (okay next, next, moving on, now, then, after that), done = (done, finished, complete, that's it, that is it, finally). _matches_cue applies a word-boundary regex over the WHOLE utterance text, not its opening, so journey 03's adversarial attack is valid as designed and all six of its planted words are real cue members. worker/src/jams_worker/effort_score.py: PER_MINUTE_SCALE is context_switch 36.75 (lane pins at 2.72 switches/min), spoken_word 2.47 (pins at 40.5 words/min, so journey 04's claim was correct), utterance 10, clicks 1, keypresses 1; time_segment is minutes * (100/30) so it pins at 30 minutes; neg_density counts any sentiment measure with value_num < -0.15, weights it by measure DURATION, and scales share * 250 so it pins at a 40 percent negative share. worker/src/jams_worker/jem_eval.py: MATCH_TOLERANCE_MS = 500; excluded_kinds is click, keypress, scroll, sentiment, utterance, spoken_word; flash detection is scale=64:36,format=gray with a bright test of mean > 245, a 120 s subprocess cap on the decode and a 300 s cap on the CFR re-encode.

THE FLASH COUNT IS A HARD GATE, NOT A PREFERENCE. jem_eval raises "sync alignment ambiguous" and aborts unless the number of detected bright runs equals exactly len(sync.flashes) + 1. It does not degrade gracefully. One maximised near-white surface anywhere in a take destroys that take. This is why the dark-mode verification in journey 04 is written as mandatory, why journey 01 requires running the flash detector against the mocha output before anything else is recorded, and why journey 07 requires checking the frames around the Task Manager open and close.

THE SENTIMENT MODEL HAS NO NEUTRAL CLASS. worker/src/jams_worker/providers/sentiment.py records score_convention "positive_probability_minus_negative_probability" on the ONNX DistilBERT path: binary and confidently bimodal, returning values near +1 or -1. The same provider has a VADER fallback that DOES emit NEUTRAL at a +/-0.05 compound band. The two backends have incompatible label spaces, so every run must record which one executed and runs from different backends must never be pooled into one macro-F1. The consequence for journey design is structural: declared-neutral narration is not filler, it is the largest error source in the shipped score, because a -0.15 threshold sits far inside the model's bimodality and every neutral line lands at nearly full magnitude on one side. This review rewrote roughly a dozen lines that were labelled neutral while carrying positive or negative lexis ("saves me hunting", "does not take all night", "doing something useful", "which is what I wanted to confirm", "which at least is predictable", "which matches the error exactly", and others), and added journey 06 specifically to measure the effect.

STANDARD PRE-FLIGHT, referenced by every setup. P1 DISPLAYS: DISPLAY1 is the only recorded monitor; every journey window lives on DISPLAY1, maximised; JEM, the narration card and the audio-recorder terminal live on DISPLAY2. The narration card must be a document opened before the take on DISPLAY2 and never focused during it - if it were on DISPLAY1 the script would be visible in the video the pipeline then analyses. P2 THEME GATE: Windows dark mode on, VS Code Dark Modern, Windows Terminal dark scheme, Edge dark; run the flash detector on a 30 s dry clip and confirm no bright run outside the sync flashes. P3 JEM CONFIG: DISPLAY1, 30 fps, CRF 23, libx264, privacy.capture_key_text left OFF (the keystroke content is already in the scripted step list and in the video, and a plaintext keystroke CSV becomes a liability the moment the dataset is shared), sync flash duration raised from the 300 ms default to 700 ms so the clap has a target a human can hit and the bright run is unambiguous at 64x36. P4 MACHINE HYGIENE: close everything not named in the journey's apps list; Focus Assist on; Slack, Teams and any mail client fully quit; phone silenced; nobody else in the room. P5 AUDIO: headset boom mic at fixed gain; enumerate devices once with ffmpeg -list_devices true -f dshow -i dummy and record the exact device string; start the recorder on DISPLAY2 BEFORE pressing Start in JEM with ffmpeg -f dshow -i audio="<device>" -ac 1 -ar 48000 -c:a pcm_s16le D:\jem-journeys\audio\<journey-id>-take<N>.wav and stop it AFTER Save; capture 10 s of room tone plus 10 s of typing on the journey keyboard once per session into room-tone.wav. P6 NARRATION: read from the DISPLAY2 card at a natural pace of roughly 150 words per minute; if a line is flubbed do not repeat it, finish the take and mark the line deviated. P7 DRY RUN: perform the whole journey once unrecorded on the same day and record the real duration of every variable-runtime command; step timestamps are nominal and the operator follows action order, not a clock. P8 FIXTURES: reset.ps1 between every take of every journey that names it. P9 TAKE LOG: one row per take with JEM, VS Code, Edge and Node versions, the capture backend actually used (ddagrab or gdigrab fallback), the output file size, and every deviation.

AUDIO CAPTURE AND MUX, the piece the proposal left implicit. JEM captures no audio at all, so narration comes from a second process and must be aligned afterwards. M1: one clap inside the opening flash, one inside the closing flash, one inside every resume flash. M2: detect flash onsets in the silent MP4 exactly the way jem_eval does (scale=64:36, gray, mean > 245) and detect clap onsets in the WAV as the first sample above a fixed threshold within a +/-3 s window around each expected flash. M3: delta = opening flash onset in video ms minus opening clap onset in audio ms, then ffmpeg -i jem.mp4 -itsoffset <delta> -i take.wav -map 0:v:0 -map 1:a:0 -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 128k -shortest out.mp4. M4: -c:v copy is mandatory; re-encoding the video would move the presentation timestamps the entire ground truth is keyed to. After muxing, ffprobe the output and assert nb_frames, r_frame_rate, avg_frame_rate and duration match the input exactly, or reject the mux. M5 DRIFT: after correction the closing clap must land within +/-100 ms of the closing flash; record the residual on every take. More than about 300 ms of residual over a long take means the sound card and the video clock disagree and the audio must be resampled by the measured ratio before the take is usable. M6: never modify the original jem.mp4, events.csv or session.json; the muxed file is a derived upload artifact only. M7 MULTI-SEGMENT (journey 07 only): the WAV runs continuously through the pause, a clap is placed immediately before Pause and another inside the resume flash, and the interval between those two clap onsets is excised from the WAV with a single atrim and concat before M3 is applied; the closing-clap check at M5 then validates the whole thing. Before recording journey 07, verify that JEM produces ONE continuous MP4 across pause and resume and that video time equals the concatenation of active segments, because if it does not the protocol changes.

THE CLAPS CONTAMINATE THE PHYSICAL LANE. Two to four broadband transients per take are exactly what the experimental physical.clicks audio-onset detector fires on, and its precision is already failing its gate badly at TP 6 / FP 126. Every clap window, onset +/-250 ms, must be added to an exclusion mask before the clicks, keypresses and scrolls providers are evaluated, or that figure gets worse for a reason that has nothing to do with the detector. Keyboard clatter is in the mic by design and room-tone.wav is the characterization baseline.

SENTIMENT LABELING PROTOCOL. Pre-register, before any holdout is scored, the mapping from value_num to a three-class prediction - proposed: positive at >= +0.33, negative at <= -0.33, neutral otherwise - and report BOTH three-class macro-F1 and a two-class F1 computed only over lines declared positive or negative, since the two-class figure is the only one the shipped model can fairly be held to. Report the neutral-line polarity distribution as a first-class number. Journey 06 is the clean estimator for it: its declared negative count is exactly zero by construction, so any neg_density above zero measured there is entirely model error on neutral lines with no true-negative signal to confound it. Every line in this set is to be independently labelled by a second rater before recording; lines the two raters disagree on are rewritten until they agree or dropped. A line marked deviated in the take log is excluded from the sentiment set for that take, because the declared label was attached to the scripted wording.

WER REFERENCE PROTOCOL. The narration script is the reference transcript. Normalization is lowercase, strip punctuation, collapse whitespace. Identifiers are written as spoken and must be read as written - "package dot json", "priority dot js", "line fourteen", "line thirty one" - and numerals are never read as digits. Domain vocabulary deliberately present for stress: mocha, toISOString, RangeError, hunk, rebase, decorate, seed, timeout assertion. If a line is deviated, transcribe what was actually said and use that as the WER reference while excluding the line for sentiment.

WHAT THE EVALUATOR CAN AND CANNOT SCORE, restated because three of the proposed journeys claimed otherwise. jem_eval is context_switch only. It cannot score clicks, keypresses, scrolls, sentiment, utterances or spoken words, so no journey may claim JEM ground truth for those - their expected_physical values here are HUMAN annotation targets, cross-checkable against the events.csv rows but not against jem_eval output. Two intended switches closer than about 1.5 s apart cannot be individually attributed by a +/-500 ms point matcher; every journey keeps its switches at least 6 s apart except journey 07's two deliberate sub-tolerance bursts, which exist precisely to measure that failure. expected_segments in all seven journeys is the HUMAN task-phase count, i.e. the segmentation ground truth, not a prediction of how many segments the provider will emit - the provider unions cue boundaries with detected context switches and will normally emit more, and the gap between the two is the measurement.

SIX DEFECT CLASSES FOUND AND REPAIRED. (1) GROUND-TRUTH FALSEHOOD: journey 04 asserted that an in-page anchor click produces no JEM event; MDN anchors change the address bar fragment and JEM enriches Edge identity from the address bar, so the claim is unverified. It is now written as a beat to be classified from take one's CSV rather than pre-declared blind. (2) BROKEN MECHANICS: journey 01 cloned with --depth 1 and then narrated skimming recent commits, which --depth 1 makes impossible; changed to --filter=blob:none. (3) VAGUE STEPS: four edit beats across journeys 02, 03 and 05 said things like "select the duplicate call and delete it, about 80 keys"; all are now exact caret placements with exact keystroke counts (Backspace x4, Ctrl+Shift+K), which is what makes the keypress ground truth reproducible across takes. (4) COUNT ERRORS: journey 03 claimed 17 context switches where enumeration gives 21, and journey 04 claimed 17 where it gives 18. (5) KNIFE-EDGE TIMING: journey 02 placed two switches exactly 10.000 s apart, sitting on the strictly-less-than MIN_SEGMENT_MS comparison where a millisecond of jitter flips the merge; moved to 16 s. Every target_minutes was also raised to match the actual step timeline, which overran the stated duration in all five proposed journeys. (6) PRIVACY: journey 05 built the product's own web app, putting proprietary route names, source paths and possible environment-variable warnings on camera in a file then uploaded for processing; it now builds a generated fixture under D:\jem-journeys with no proprietary content. Journey 01 additionally gets a shortened shell prompt so no user-profile path renders. Nothing in the set requires a credential, an account, a payment method or a form submission, and the only network access anywhere is an anonymous public HTTPS clone and two public documentation pages.

TWO STRUCTURAL GAPS FILLED. The proposed set contained nothing shorter than seven minutes despite the brief asking for three to twenty, and - more seriously - every proposed journey specified a single unpaused take, so JEM's per-segment sync flashes and jem_eval's per-segment active-time to video-time offset mapping were never exercised anywhere. Journey 06 (4 minutes) and journey 07 (14 minutes, paused once) close both. Journey 07 is the only take in the campaign that will reveal an error in the offset mapping, and if that mapping is wrong every point match after its resume is wrong.

DISTINCTNESS, one sentence each. 01 is the cued-segmentation and dark-on-dark scroll journey; 02 is the JEM-blind integrated terminal and dirty-dot journey on a fully deterministic fixture with zero cue words; 03 is the segmentation adversarial and colour-versus-luma journey with the corpus's negative-sentiment cluster; 04 is the spoken_word saturation control and the only browser journey, carrying the Edge enrichment probes; 05 is the dead-time, evaluator-timeout and every-lane-floor journey; 06 is the short, context_switch-saturating, zero-true-negative journey; 07 is the multi-segment, sub-tolerance-burst, real-silence journey. No two share a primary stress.

PRE-REGISTERED LANE PREDICTIONS, computed from the verified constants and to be compared against actual JAMS output before any tuning. Format is journey: context_switch / spoken_word / neg_density / time_segment. 01: 44 / 87 / 23 / 33. 02: 55 / 83 / 56 / 27. 03: 64 / 83 / 74 / 40. 04: 51 / 100 PINNED / 25 / 43. 05: 24 / 36 / 50 / 57. 06: 100 PINNED / 89 / 0 BY CONSTRUCTION / 13. 07: 64 / 55 / 38 / 46. Two lanes are bracketed at both ends across the set, which is the minimum needed to demonstrate saturation rather than merely high readings.

SPLITS AND BUDGET. Development: 01, 02, 03 - the three richest in labelled detector-failure classes, which is where tuning is allowed. Holdout: 04, 05, 06, 07 - detector settings stay FIXED while these are scored, and no tolerance is moved and no hard sample dropped after seeing their numbers. Moving any journey between splits invalidates every prior holdout score, and this category-level assignment must be reconciled with the campaign-wide split before recording. Nominal recorded time is 78 minutes per take across the seven journeys, plus dry runs, resets and fixture rebuilds; budget a full working day per take and plan for two takes so per-take variance is measurable. Recording order is fixed: 05 first as the evaluator canary, then 01, 02, 03, 04, 06, and 07 last once the single-segment mux pipeline has been proven end to end.
category_notes.browser-research:
INPUT TRUNCATION, READ FIRST. The proposed set I was given was cut off partway through browser-research-05's narration ("That is it for the sta"), and browser-research-06 and browser-research-07 never arrived at all, although the surviving text refers to "the seven". I reviewed and corrected 01 through 05 as delivered and reconstructed 05's closing narration and final steps. Journeys 06 and 07 in this response are NEWLY AUTHORED, not corrected: they fill the two clearest gaps left by 01-05 (non-maximized cross-application work, and animated content). Reconcile them against the originals before recording; if the originals covered the same ground, keep whichever is stronger rather than recording both.

SHARED PREFLIGHT P1-P18. The original set referenced "P1-P15" without including it, so this is the reconstructed and extended list every journey depends on.
P1 Power and interruption: screensaver off, display sleep off, "turn off my screen after" Never, Do Not Disturb on, Windows in DARK mode (GitHub's signed-out theme follows prefers-color-scheme).
P2 Dedicated Edge profile for capture, signed out of everything.
P3 Favourites bar hidden, profile renamed to something non-personal, Edge sidebar and Copilot button off, password-manager prompts disabled, download shelf disabled.
P4 Edge sleeping tabs OFF.
P5 One monitor selected in JEM; close or move every unrelated window off that monitor.
P6 No maximized near-white page at any point; every site set to its dark theme and verified visually, because a full-screen bright frame can collide with the sync-flash luma detector.
P7 Fixed display resolution and scaling for the whole campaign; record both.
P8 Record the Edge version, the Windows build, and the monitor refresh rate in the session log.
P9 SYNC ANCHOR, CORRECTED. The original set said to "clap inside the flash". That is not the mechanism. capture/audio_align.py anchors the microphone timeline to the silent JEM video using a 1000 Hz SYNC TONE that JEM plays at each flash. Three consequences: (a) sync.sync_tone must be set TRUE in jem.config.json, because JemConfig.SyncTone defaults to false and the shipped jem.config.json has no sync_tone key at all, so this is OFF unless you turn it on; (b) the tone must play through SPEAKERS audible to the microphone, since the module's own error text notes headphones defeat the anchor; (c) claps are not needed, but audible discrete CLICKS and KEYSTROKES are, because refine_offset_by_events recovers the precise offset by correlating JEM's logged click and keypress times against microphone transients. Every journey below therefore opens with a deliberate focus click and is annotated where physical events are too sparse to support that refinement.
P10 Start the external microphone recorder BEFORE pressing Start in JEM and stop it AFTER pressing Save. Keep its window off the captured monitor.
P11 Single unpaused take per journey. Pausing is supported but complicates active-time mapping; if you must pause, log it and expect the journey to be scored separately.
P12 Verify both flashes and both tones were captured before treating a take as scorable.
P13 privacy.capture_key_text stays OFF by default. OPTIONAL PER-JOURNEY UPGRADE: for journeys whose only typed text is a public URL or a fixed non-sensitive note string (01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07 type nothing sensitive; 06 types four fixed note strings), turning capture_key_text ON yields exact key-level ground truth instead of category-level. If you do, record that you did, and turn it OFF again immediately. Never enable it for any journey where a credential, personal name, address or private message could be typed.
P14 Run detect_flash_runs on the recording immediately after the take and before scoring anything.
P15 Keep original JEM CSV, manifest and video outside Git; commit only recipes, redacted labels, metrics and reports.
P16 Record the session's development-split or holdout-split assignment BEFORE recording, never after.
P17 Microphone privacy: confirm no other person is present or audible before recording. The mic runs continuously for the whole take and picks up room conversation cleanly, and journey 04 in particular is silent for minutes at a time.
P18 Fully RELEASE all modifier keys between every key combination, in every journey. This is not cosmetic: JEM writes one row per key-DOWN with OS auto-repeat suppressed, so a held Ctrl across a run of presses collapses to a SINGLE modifier row.

VERIFIED CORRECTIONS MADE, with the source that establishes each.

1. COUNT CONVENTION FIXED (all five original journeys). jem_eval.py takes each customer-app context_switch row's t_start_ms as a truth instant, and a row is written per SPAN, including the first span, which opens when Edge takes the foreground after Start. Every expected_context_switches figure was therefore one too low. Corrected: 01 from 3 to 4, 02 from 19 to 20, 03 from 28 to 29, 04 from 4 to 5, 05 from 5 to 6. Each journey now opens with an explicit focus-click step so that first truth event is deliberate rather than incidental, and it doubles as the opening audio transient.

2. JOURNEY 03 BLOCK D WAS VOID AS WRITTEN. This is the most serious finding. ContextSwitchConsumer.BuildEdgeContext sets the Edge context identity to (processName, FULL URL STRING) whenever UIA enrichment succeeds, and SwitchTo returns early without writing any row when the identity is unchanged. Two tabs on a byte-identical URL therefore produce ZERO context_switch rows, so block D as proposed would have measured nothing at all while appearing to fail. Fixed by giving tab 2 a ?jemdup=1 query string: the URL differs so JEM logs a switch, MDN ignores the parameter so the render stays pixel-identical, and the near-zero-content-delta isolate is preserved. The setup now flags the query string as load-bearing and adds a CSV verification step. Note the same collapse happens on the fallback path too, since tabs 1 and 2 share a title.

3. HASH-NAVIGATION BEATS REACHED THE RIGHT ANSWER FOR THE WRONG REASON. The originals said fragment navigation produces no switch "because the title does not change while the URL does". Given that identity IS the URL, that reasoning would predict a switch. The actual mechanism is the TRIGGER, not the comparison: ContextSwitchConsumer re-resolves identity only on ForegroundChanged or on a window-title NameChanged that has gone quiet. A fragment change fires neither, so nothing is re-resolved and no row is written. The conclusion survives, the reasoning is corrected in every affected beat (02 at 96 s, 04 at 380 s and 392 s, 05 at 186 s, 222 s and 258 s), and each now carries an instruction to CONFIRM FROM THE CSV rather than assume, because any incidental title change would emit a row bearing the new fragment-laden URL.

4. KEYPRESS COUNTS CORRECTED. Rows are written on key-DOWN only, with auto-repeat suppressed and no row on key-up. Journey 03's "~68 rows, ~30 modifier" is wrong under any pressing style; corrected to 57 rows and 29 modifier, with full modifier release now mandated in setup (holding Ctrl across a run would roughly halve it). Journey 02's address-bar burst was understated at 62; the URL is 64 characters and capitals need Shift rows, so it is about 72 to 75. Journey 04's was understated at 42; corrected to about 45 to 50. All typed-string counts are now explicitly flagged approximate, because capture_key_text is OFF and only key_category is recorded.

5. TIMING-LAG CLAIM CORRECTED. Journey 01 claimed the JEM boundary lags the visual cut by "roughly 230 ms because of namechange_quiet_ms". It does not. CheckPendingQuietPeriod passes _pendingNameChangeLastSeenWallMs as the switch instant, explicitly backdating to the moment the title settled rather than to whenever the poll ran. The quiet period adds detection latency, not timestamp error. Residual offset is the gap between the pixels changing and the title settling, which is what should actually be measured.

6. SENTIMENT SCORING IS NOT WELL DEFINED UNTIL A NEUTRAL BAND IS PRE-REGISTERED. The ONNX Xenova twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) INT8 ONNX path in sentiment.py emits only NEGATIVE or POSITIVE and NEVER NEUTRAL, with value = P(pos) - P(neg). Three-class macro-F1 against declared neutral labels is therefore unscoreable without a binning rule. sentiment.py already uses a plus or minus 0.15 band for its aggregate counts; PRE-REGISTER THAT BAND NOW, in writing, before any scoring. Expect near-zero neutral recall, because twitter-roberta-base-sentiment-latest (three-class: negative/neutral/positive) saturates near plus or minus 0.95 on almost any sentence; that is a pre-registered expected outcome of a binary model, not a defect to be repaired by widening the band after seeing the number. The VADER fallback does emit NEUTRAL natively (|compound| at or below 0.05) and should be pre-registered as the comparison arm.

7. MIXED-VALENCE NARRATION LINES REWRITTEN. An independent rater cannot reliably label "The chapter is long, but the writing quality here is genuinely excellent" or "The response directive table is dense but readable", so every such line was rewritten to a single valence. Several lines labelled neutral were in fact mildly positive and were either flattened or relabelled; for example 04's "I am satisfied with what I found here" is now explicitly positive, 03's "Reopening the one I closed by mistake" was labelled negative but reads neutral and became "I closed the wrong one and now I have to fix it". Rule applied throughout: one valence per line, no concessive clauses.

8. CUE AUDIT RUN AGAINST THE REAL LIST. DEFAULT_CUES in segmentation.py holds exactly 18 phrases in three groups, matched case-insensitively on word boundaries. Journey 02's claim to contain none of them is CORRECT and survives verification. Journey 01's four cues, journey 03's planted mid-block cues and journey 04's single cue all verified. Journey 03's stresses text said "all five real block boundaries" and then listed four narration timestamps rather than step timestamps; corrected to the five actual block starts at roughly 10, 54, 152, 188 and 212 s.

9. PERFORMABILITY FIXES. Journey 01's Rust Book theme instruction said to set it on both tabs; it is localStorage per origin, so it is set once and the other tab must be RELOADED. Journey 01's scrollbar drags were vague ("one third to two thirds") and are now concrete press-hold-drag-300px-release actions. Journey 02's "click a section link in the MDN left sidebar" was ambiguous, because MDN's left sidebar links to other PAGES (which would change the title and produce a switch) while the on-page contents does not; now specified as the right-hand "In this article" on-page contents. Journey 03's block timings were shifted to accommodate the new opening click.

10. TIMING COHERENCE. Journey 03 ran to about 265 s against a stated 4 minutes and had narration at 210 s and 224 s describing block D while block E was running; target_minutes is now 5 and those lines were retimed. Journey 01 now runs to 345 s against 6 minutes, 02 to 636 s against 11, 04 to 706 s against 12, 05 to 478 s against 8: all within target.

11. SYNC MECHANISM CORRECTED EVERYWHERE, see P9 above. Every "clap inside the flash" instruction was removed and replaced with the tone requirement plus an explicit note about which physical events carry the event-based offset refinement. Journeys 04 and 07 are annotated as alignment-fragile because they are so sparse in clicks and keystrokes.

DISTINCTNESS ASSESSMENT. The five delivered journeys are genuinely distinct and none needed differentiating: 01 is scroll-precision, 02 is switch-recall breadth, 03 is the spacing and content floor, 04 is the static negative control, 05 is band-localised find-bar change. The nearest pair is 02 and 05, since both are multi-page Edge sessions with clicks and typing, but 02's subject is 19 real switches while 05's is eleven find-bar events that produce no switches at all, so they measure opposite things. The two gaps 01-05 leave are non-maximized cross-application work (every one of them is a single maximized Edge window, so the whole corpus would have measured only full-frame change) and continuously animated content (every false-positive window in 01-05 is static, so motion sensitivity would be untested). Journeys 06 and 07 fill exactly those. 07's hover block is worth singling out: five large deliberate visual state changes that produce literally zero rows in events.csv, because JEM logs no pointer movement, which is the strongest available demonstration that JEM rows and human visual labels are different label sets.

PRIVACY VERDICT. Nothing in the set requires credentials and nothing needs removing. GitHub signed-out is correctly mandated in 02 and 03 and is the one place where a sign-in would put a real name, avatar and private repo list on camera. Three additions were made across all journeys: disable Edge's password manager UI so no prompt can surface mid-dwell, confirm nobody else is audible before starting the microphone, and in journey 06 type only the four fixed note strings given and never save the file.

OPEN ITEM FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR. Every journey's Edge truth depends on UIA URL enrichment, which the hard context already flags as brittle across Edge updates. When it succeeds, identity is the full URL; when it fails, identity falls back to the parsed tab title. These are different label sets, and the path can flip mid-session. Every journey now instructs reading the detail column, where a "uia:" prefix marks the URL path. Consider adding a per-session assertion to the evaluator that reports what fraction of Edge context rows used each path, and refusing to score any session that flipped.
